agreement between the employers and the employees of the railways. all this is provided for in the texts, but, generally speaking, with a certain amount of certainty, we quite often get rid of this agreement between railway workers and the bosses of railway companies, or more generally between employees and management, whereas there is no longer any question of getting rid of it when everyone feels concerned by a european project and a directive. i am one of those who believe that in order to achieve the railway europe which is absolutely necessary, railway workers must join this europe and be convinced that, far from igniting a kind of economic civil war between railway companies, it serves the development of the railway. the text presented is quite exemplary. i would add to mr jarzembowski, because we have always had a disagreement on this subject, that it is not enough to set dates for liberalization to make the european internal market. this date battle is terribly restrictive. the european internal market requires first of all that trains be interoperable, which requires considerable funding. i would like to say that i am very pleased that the commission has taken the initiative to introduce a new system of taxation. the directive will have little effect on britain because there is only one tunnel to get into and there are few land borders. it will affect spain quite a bit because the track gauge is different. it will affect a number of other countries, which do not necessarily have direct railway borders with the union, to a limited extent: i am thinking of finland and greece. so the essence of liberalisation is interoperability and my report is about human interoperability, that is to say the recognition of a train driving licence throughout the union. i shall be thanking my colleagues today for their outstanding work. i would like to make the following comments on the directive. firstly, it is a licence for the whole network and not just for the international network, because we believe that every train driver should be able to have the ambition to go international and that there is little difference between driving a tgv, a high-speed train, within a member state or a tgv crossing a border. i think that is absolutely essential. secondly, the great contribution of parliament - which is also at the origin of a dispute with the council - is that we consider that aircrew who perform safety duties must be taken into account in a subsequent text, and we propose a road map. there are lives saved, on a regular basis, by train crew who have been trained in a number of tasks: evacuating trains, taking passengers to safety, signalling, activating certain warning circuits. it is quite legitimate for these qualified people to be recognised and, above all, for an attempt to harmonise their qualifications in all the countries of europe to avoid some of them being underqualified. this is a security issue and not just a social issue. parliament has made a proposal on this and we think it is very important to do so now: we are indeed in a world of several railway companies and it is quite legitimate, since we are making rail europe, to provide for compensation rules to be applied between railway companies when they exchange staff whom they have trained. in other words, when a company trains a driver at great expense and the driver leaves after two years for another company, a minimum of rules is required for the company that inherits the driver to partially pay the training company. as there is no railway university, training is currently provided by some companies, mainly the historical companies, and those entering the market should not take advantage of this to become more competitive at lower costs. i think the european parliament is sending you a good copy, commissioner. i am certainly not unaware of the remaining disputes with the council, mainly those i have just mentioned concerning the scope of understanding... mr president, as you know, the greens are determined to put in place a genuine european transport policy which will enable a modal shift from road to rail. the road is 25% of greenhouse gas emissions, so the stakes are high. the question we have to ask ourselves is: will opening up to competition, particularly in rail passenger transport, solve this problem? i think, on the contrary, that the proposals in the jarzembowski report can be expected to lead to a risk of a deterioration in the service to users. tariff, ticketing, timetable information, connection management: how will users find their account among the different services offered by railway companies? the least profitable lines, which nevertheless fulfil fundamental tasks of social and territorial cohesion, are expected to be abandoned. it is also to be expected that there will be increased pressure on the working conditions of railway staff, as is the case with low-cost airlines in the aviation sector, or that there will be fierce competition for the most profitable lines without any effect on the final number of passengers carried. to strengthen the railway, a genuine european commitment is needed to finance the modernisation of infrastructure, the obsolescence of which is a major obstacle to its development. it is also necessary to overcome the obstacles to interoperability and adopt - this is crucial - a taxation system which actually penalizes the most polluting transport modes, such as a tax on kerosene or the internalisation of environmental costs for road transport. liberalisation is certainly not the only way of europeanising transport policies.

on behalf of the its group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, we are discussing the revision of a complex agreement, the cotonou agreement, which has 100 articles, 6 parts, 5 annexes and 5 protocols. in this revised agreement, we find the entire briefing of today's politics, with human rights, democracy, terrorism, weapons, the international criminal court. the only thing missing is reach, whereas the acp countries are at risk of falling victim to this regulation on chemicals, with lost revenues and 315 000 jobs affected. metals, alcohol, oil, ammonia, which are the exports of 24 major acp countries, will fall under reach, which represents a potential loss of revenue of 6 billion euros for these countries. this is the heart of the truth of our europe-acp relations over the last thirty years. on the surface, from the yaoundé agreement of 1963 to the cotonou agreement of 2000, revised in 2005, and the lomé i, ii, iii and iv agreements since 1975, europe has been bold, especially with the stabex mechanism, which has protected cocoa, tea, coffee, peanuts. it was the spirit of the compensatory inequalities of the unced. europe has also been generous in its financial support from the edf. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the programme to include the acp countries, the mediterranean countries and the countries of central and eastern europe. but the reality is different. in the figures, the acp share of the union market has fallen from 6.7% in 1976 to 3% in 1998, and while the gdp of a european was growing by an average of 2.3% a year, that of an african from an acp country, i dare say, was only growing by 0.6%. in fact, europe has forgotten the acp countries, just as it has forgotten the mediterranean. since the fall of the berlin wall, europe has been looking east, but more to the south. and worse: with the wto, europe has drowned the acp in the world market, as we have seen with sugar and as we have seen with bananas. the multinational banana company chiquita has been preferred in cameroon, which produces bananas, or in côte d'ivoire. the ultra-liberal europe has chosen to give a customs gift of almost 2 billion euros to the multinationals chiquita, del monte and others, rather than to the acp countries, which are now competing on an equal footing with these multinationals. cotonou, with democracy and dialogue, is very good, but when you have aids, human rights, it does not cure. in other words, instead of being revised, the cotonou agreement should be reworked to be bold on two points. firstly, the technical audacity of a new customs technology: instead of seeking, within the world trade organization, the reduction of customs duties and, eventually, their abolition, it is necessary to invent the deduction of customs duties in the form of a customs credit deductible from any purchase in the economy of the importing country. this customs credit would be eligible for subsidies, i.e. it would be higher than the amount of customs duty borne, for example, by the acp country. with new, flexible, refundable, subsidized and negotiable customs duties on the world stock market, europe-acp relations would be in harmony with the necessary free trade and the equally necessary protection of the acp. secondly, we must bring political audacity to a rebuilt cotonou. with globalisation, the challenge of the 21st century is to organise the common parts of planetary co-ownership - i.e. water, food, basic medicine or vaccine and education - all with a resource other than the conventional state contribution from the edf, a tax resource such as a vat based on the turnover of telecommunications services provided from space satellites. in this case, we would also be doing improved assistance under the name of co-development, but we would be gradually moving towards the planning of the planetary territory. we would regain the spirit of lomé and finally begin to build the world, which is the challenge of the 21st century.

in writing. i voted in favour of the main points of my excellent german colleague, mr georg jarzembowski's very good report, which deals with the recommendation for second reading on the amendment of the 1991 directive on the development of community railways and the 2001 directive on railway infrastructure (3rd railway package). it is essential to introduce more competition in rail passenger transport in continuation of what has been done, rightly, for freight. this is the necessary condition for an increase in services at a fair price. however, like my political group, the ump, i have not joined in a pace of liberalization too strong for internal traffic in the member states to allow the incumbent operators to prepare for competition. i hope that parliament will find, in conciliation, an acceptable compromise to move this sector rapidly from the administered economy to the social market economy. the development of rail transport for people at fair prices, as well as for goods, is one of the essential conditions for the proper functioning, development and competitiveness of our european internal economic market, which is a source of prosperity, and for the social needs of our citizens.
in writing. once again, the ultra-liberal ideology promoted by brussels is present in this dossier on the third railway package. the aim is to accelerate the liberalisation of international passenger traffic by 2010 and of domestic traffic by 2017. if the end justifies the means, it is regrettable that the means and precautions taken in this matter are weak to prevent railway undertakings and employees, currently protected by their public status, from being left to the savage competition of the world rail market. the commission, the council and parliament seem not to have learned the lessons of the privatisation of the british railways in 1993, which resulted in more train accidents, delays, deterioration of infrastructure, higher fares and the dismissal of 50% of the total workforce. the situation is such that many people in britain are now campaigning for the renationalisation of the railways. such a europe must not exist, it must not be built at the expense of security, employment and vocational qualifications. we reject this anti-national philosophy which destroys national jobs and systematically ensures foreign preference.
in writing. following the adoption of the second rail freight package, the commission proposes nothing less than full liberalisation of all international and domestic passenger services by 2010 and 2017. this ultra-liberal acceleration comes at a time when the question of the viability of the liberalisation of french rail freight is being raised. in december 2006, sncf noted that, despite the european measures designed to reduce road transport, there had been a free fall in the volume of rail freight. what about the future effects of the third package? we are heading for economic and social failure, which is predictable. this is a lesson which our european leaders should learn, if only by recalling the disastrous experience of the liberalisation of british railways in 1993. let us not make the same mistakes by favouring anti-national ideology over national jobs and preserve the unification of the french railway. the liberalisation of the railways is the risk of insecurity. we'll have too many private players on the same rail network. safety must always take precedence over return on investment alone. the railways, given their importance, must remain a viable public service, but above all a safe one.
in writing. i voted to withdraw this report because it is urgent to stop the liberalisation and deregulation of public services, especially for passenger transport. the eu must also be aware of the negative consequences of its policy and the growing rejection of its citizens, since it refuses to take a public view of these conditions. we cannot accept any new opening up to competition as long as a framework directive on public services does not provide guarantees for equality and spatial planning, tariff policies ensuring the necessary equalization or future investments ensuring the modernization and quality of infrastructure. all indications are that safety and rail services, especially where the profitability of the service is low, will decline in europe, which will also go against the objectives of combating the greenhouse effect and increase inequalities.

mr president, i should like to congratulate the european parliament on the great wisdom it has shown in postponing the liberalization of the railway system and of national railway systems. i am personally very much in favour of the opening up of the networks and i am a strong supporter of the construction of a railway europe without frontiers, which will effectively mean the end of national monopolies. that said, i consider that the way in which the european commission proposes to liberalize, which is reduced to a battle of deadlines and dates, is unacceptable and will naturally lead to the concentration of the railway economy around a few large companies, with the disappearance of many national companies, a great fight over the most profitable market segments, that is to say the high-speed lines, and probably a very great difficulty in financing the budget lines relating to spatial planning. the train is also the regional train, it is also the mainline train, which is often in deficit, which is financed by what are now the main international lines, and i am very concerned to see that this aspect of things has not really been taken into account. how can we finance small railway lines which are very useful when the financing and margins of railway companies are going to dry up as a result of opening up to international competition? that's a question we need to answer. we have until 2010 and i personally hope that the financing of the public service and the lines for spatial planning will soon be on the agenda of our assembly.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my uk colleague diana wallis, which deals with the recommendation for second reading for the adoption of the regulation on non-contractual obligations. while, as a rule, the law applicable to a non-contractual obligation is the law of the country in which the damage occurred, this report, if followed, will allow, for example in the case of personal injury following a car accident, the law of the country of the victim to be applied. given the complexity of the situations, this position allows people to be put back in the situation they were in before the accident. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. the work of compromise will not be easy.
in writing. the rome ii regulation is intended to facilitate the handling of crossborder disputes by extending to many situations the application of the general rule that the law applicable to a non-contractual obligation is the law of the country in which the damage occurred. we are in favour of harmonizing the rules on conflicts of laws, which alone can increase legal certainty. it should still be precise and clear, which is far from always the case. the rules on the specific issue of road accidents, but also on cases of defamation or violation of privacy by means of a written or audiovisual media, are designed to protect the victim by making it easier for him to obtain redress. while freedom of the press and freedom of expression must be guaranteed, they must not unduly restrict the rights of the persons concerned. this report provides for safeguards through the adoption of standard rules on conflicts of laws, and we shall vote in favour of it.

member of the commission. madam president, the issue of the renegotiation of the wto government procurement agreement, known as the gpa, is important for europe as it should provide our companies with future opportunities outside the community. last december, after many years of long and difficult negotiations, the gpa parties reached a provisional understanding on a new revised text. i consider this to be a major achievement in the current context of the doha round. it demonstrates that the political will to reach an understanding on sensitive issues remains alive. the new text provides for more clarity and transparency, as well as better guarantees for equal treatment in the procurement procedures. it includes, for the first time, provisions for conducting electronic procurement. the european community played an important role during the negotiations. the existing agreement is unbalanced, both in terms of procedural guarantees and coverage. our main objectives were to fill the gaps and to eliminate ambiguities. we wanted to obtain better legal guarantees for our suppliers, similar to those offered by our internal regime. at the same time we sought to make the new agreement more attractive for developing countries via new specific measures. the final agreement on the new text is subject to a satisfactory outcome of the market access negotiations which are ongoing. here as well, we need to rebalance the situation in favour of the community. hence the coverage our partners currently offer should be extended to the level the community has offered and it should be more uniform. we all want to see improved access for our companies to foreign countries’ procurement markets. the council emphasised in its recent conclusions on the commission’s communication ‘global comprehensive request and offer which will give the other gpa parties all the necessary incentives to offer significant additional procurement opportunities. should we fail to get a substantial improvement from other gpa parties, we will consider taking the necessary measures to adapt the community commitments in the new gpa accordingly. in the absence of improved access for the eu to third-country procurement markets, commissioner mandelson and i are reflecting on a market-opening instrument to enhance eu access. the case of our smes certainly deserves particular attention. it will specifically benefit from the new text, with the introduction of rules on electronic procurement and, if negotiations are completed successfully, the lowering of thresholds of some parties. however, let me remind you that the agreement deals with rather large procurement contracts which are mainly undertaken by big companies. smes certainly have an important role to play, but mostly as subcontractors. this is why we have asked our gpa partners who currently maintain specific derogations for their domestic smes to abandon them. on the prospects of extending the geographical scope of the agreement, eight wto members are in the process of acceding to it. among those, jordan is the most advanced. china has indicated that it will start accession negotiations by december this year treatment for developing countries. i believe we have achieved a good result with tailor-made new rules that fully take their specific needs into account. i am confident that if we succeed, this new agreement will constitute a milestone for international trade and create new opportunities for our companies.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in view of the constant increase in the waste we produce and the need to revise the 1975 text, the european commission last year proposed an amendment to the existing framework directive. the intention was good, but the legislative proposal is not up to the challenge and falls far short of the objectives to be achieved. the proposed measures to prevent waste and thus reduce the volume of waste produced are not sufficiently concrete and are not binding. i also regret the absence of quantified recycling targets. the commission's proposals on hazardous waste are also inadequate in relation to existing community legislation. the objective of merging the texts in order to simplify them and improve their implementation must not be seen as weakening the provisions on the treatment of hazardous waste. as far as waste is concerned, no backsliding can be tolerated, especially when it is hazardous. recent news is a wake-up call. when you mix hazardous waste with other waste, you don't remove the hazardousness. we cannot support the possibility of exemptions from the requirement to hold an operating licence when dealing with hazardous waste. as regards the concept of energy recovery from waste, i understand the aim, but it is dangerous to confuse recovery with energy recovery. there is nothing to prevent the recovery of energy produced during incineration operations even if the latter is classified as waste. this is a point that needs clarification. such a proposal, which would make it possible to classify incineration as a recovery operation and not just as a disposal operation, would put waste recovery and energy recovery on the same level. but above all, it is contrary to the five-level hierarchy adopted by the committee on the environment and, therefore, to the objective of preventing and reducing waste. this objective is supported by mrs jackson's report, which considerably improves the commission's proposal. the waste problem is a major social issue which merits ambitious legislation. more and more surveys show us that a large majority of consumers want products that are more environmentally friendly, and they want to be better informed about the nature and quality of these products. we need to hear them.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we produce daily household, industrial and mining waste which is very difficult to dispose of. waste management is complex and raises the question of our ability to respect the environment and health, but also our own european policies. since 1976 we have developed an inefficient common regulation. this second directive, a revision of the waste directive, cannot be concealed behind the simplification of existing arrangements. the numbers speak for themselves. the waste is constantly increasing: 3.5 tonnes per capita per year, or 460 kg more in ten years. beyond a regulation that can be converted into future devices, it is important to give european citizens a general view of the circuit followed by our garbage. the european hierarchy, based on five key principles: prevention, sorting, recycling, incineration and landfill, must not be called into question by the promotion of incineration. like many citizens living near incineration plants, i am concerned that the union is not giving more incentives for waste prevention and recycling, for example by setting up genuine recycling channels. we must drastically reduce the use of incineration and prevent it from gaining energy recovery status. on the contrary, it is important to increase recycling, with a target of 50% of municipal waste and 60% of other waste by 2020, with a gradual decrease in landfilling and incineration of all materials that can be reused, recycled or composted. i would also draw your attention, madam president, to the incorporation of the dangerous waste directive into the new regulation. dangerous waste must be strictly controlled, it must be traceable and subject to a very strict authorization system. we agree to prevent and reduce the impact of waste, commissioner, but to give in to the ease of incineration would not be acceptable.
mr president, i would first like to warmly congratulate our colleague, mrs jackson, on her very good work, which reflects the quality of her expertise on the delicate issue of waste management. i am quite satisfied with the clarification that has been given with the five-level hierarchy. what is important is first of all prevention, which is to reduce the volume of our waste and which really requires a lot of effort, and recycling. however, not everything is recyclable. the necessary market does not always exist. the recovery is therefore necessary, in the absence of other solutions, but with high energy efficiency. this hierarchy should be a guiding principle, but it should take into account many parameters, including local ones, as it is important to introduce some flexibility by varying priorities where appropriate, in line with practical considerations and the necessary complementarity of management methods. on this point, i also welcome the introduction in the report of the principle of the responsibility of waste producers on the one hand, and of the control and traceability requirements for hazardous waste on the other, which also cover the provisions governing the necessary authorization of treatment facilities and transport controls. finally, on the amendments concerning co-products or by-products, i am strongly opposed to a definition which would exempt certain wastes from environmental protection obligations; this definition would allow waste, considered as co-products, to escape waste legislation and not be subject to traceability and transport authorisation requirements, or in some cases to the reach regulation applicable to products. it is therefore to be feared that certain combustible residues from manufacturing and chemical industries, such as fuel oil substitutes, which are currently considered hazardous wastes, will be able to meet the proposed definitions for co-products which are not tempered by other criteria. this seems to me particularly dangerous because there is then a risk of a general declassification of all waste streams meeting these criteria.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we should welcome the fact that our parliament is making bolder proposals than the commission on the recycling of waste. but what can we expect from a commission whose policy is to sacrifice the general interest of citizens systematically to the particular interests of the shareholders of multinational companies? environmental dumping of waste must be combated inside and outside the union. this issue should be one of the cornerstones of commissioner mandelson's negotiating mandate at the wto. it is about saving the planet, but also about fighting against relocations due to non-compliance with basic environmental rules. all waste produced in the union, including waste from ships chartered by european companies, must be treated in the union by job-creating industries under public responsibility. africa, india and asia must no longer be regarded as the garbage dumps of europe. local authorities have been able to anticipate, lead by example, innovate. i want to see the model plant for methanation and the multi-line recovery of waste that the union that owns my town has built. unfortunately, these exemplary achievements in the union owe everything to local taxpayers and nothing or little to the union and the industrialists. it would be good to take that into account and help those who have fewer opportunities than others.
mr president, like all our colleagues here, i believe that we need a clear european framework to tackle the great challenge of responsible waste management. i also think we all share the view that the new european waste strategy must make it possible to see in each of them not only a source of pollution to be reduced but also a potential resource to be exploited. i therefore wholeheartedly support the approach being taken and i welcome the remarkable work done by our rapporteur to modernise the legislation that has accumulated over the last thirty years on this subject. it is therefore essential, as has also been stressed by many, to re-establish a clear five-step hierarchy in a descending order of priority: prevention, reuse, recycling, recovery, disposal. this is achieved by maintaining a minimum of flexibility, taking account in particular of the economic aspects affecting the sectors. we have seen what it can cost to want to be free from these kinds of constraints, which are unavoidable. i would also like to say that i fully support the amendments to consolidate the definitions, in particular those on end-of-life waste, the responsibility of the producer of waste and prevention. finally, i believe that it is important, as has also been stressed by many of our colleagues, to strengthen the regulation on hazardous waste, in particular by imposing separate collection and reliable traceability.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, there are three points on which i would like to insist so that our parliament can improve the directive. firstly, we need to set quantified targets, particularly for the reduction of waste, which our committee on the environment has rightly set as a long-term obligation. this is important for the protection of the environment, but also for limiting our vulnerability in terms of the supply of raw materials, which we know are highly contested in the world. secondly, although incineration cannot be prohibited, it must be limited as far as possible. it's a disposal, not a recovery. of course, energy production is better than landfilling, but let's not get confused: incineration is disposal. thirdly, we must strengthen the principle of proximity and self-sufficiency in waste management, especially in the various forms of disposal and incineration, otherwise we will see the development of an almost uncontrollable phenomenon of waste transport, with an increase in the greenhouse effect and the risks of environmental dumping. but the best practices are not always the cheapest. a weakening of the principle of proximity to create a large waste market would benefit the large economic groups concerned and not the environment. so this is not acceptable.

in writing. since 9/11, airplanes are no longer just a means of transportation, they can also be a means of taking the lives of many people. that is why new - more stringent - security measures have been implemented at airports and i fully support the process that has been initiated. however, the restrictions on freedom of movement should be proportionate. so while i support the main points of the measures taken, i remain sceptical about the restrictions on liquids in the cabin and the way they were decided. these measures are very cumbersome, they cause a lot of inconvenience to travellers, and their effectiveness has not been demonstrated, since their application varies from one state to another and even from one airport to another! moreover, the european parliament, elected by the citizens, was informed of the implementation of these measures only after they had been decided. i fully understand that some information should not be disclosed because of its highly strategic nature in the fight against terrorism, but i believe that we should be more involved in decision-making.

mr president, in your speech you mentioned several important elements of our european tradition, four of which were particularly important: greek philosophy, roman law, judeo-christian spirituality and the enlightenment. but that is precisely a key part of the problem: how faithful is the european union to these elements of its intellectual, moral and spiritual heritage? is the european union today inspired by christian values, or by a general hedonism which is preparing the destruction of these same values in the name of an ideology of human rights, still imperious, but still of variable geometry? is the construction and functioning of the union governed by the greek philosophy of clarity and simplicity and by the hellenic political tradition of direct participation of citizens in the affairs of the city, or is it the reverse, the creation of a cumbersome, centralised structure that is soon outdated, which claims to govern almost 500 million europeans while in practice ignoring their differences? mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in setting its economic objectives, the german presidency of the european council is relying on a report which states that unemployment in europe is falling. this is more the result of a decline in the number of active persons linked to the ageing of the population than the result of a prosperous economy. with an annual growth rate of only 2.6%, compared with 3.6% in the united states and 10% in china, brussels europe is lagging behind the world's major economies. on the other hand, in some member states, official employment statistics are distorted. in france, for example, if one adds to the 2 million or more officially unemployed the retired employees, those in early retirement, the unemployed in training, and the subsidized contracts, unemployment affects nearly 4.5 million french people, or 18% of the active population. with growth at a standstill, a population that does not replace its generations, and companies relocating their activities, the european union is unfortunately continuing its economic decline. if the diagnosis is therefore wrong, the remedies prescribed and inspired by the malthusian and anti-social policy practised for the past twenty years are harmful: the destruction of trade borders, the surrender of our industry to unfair competition from asian economies, the multiplication of bureaucratic constraints, the legal arrival of more than a million immigrants from outside the community every year, the dismantling of our public services, the abandonment of our agriculture subject to the forks of the world trade organization, and the overburdening of taxation. to restore prosperity to our economies and economic and social security to our citizens, to which they are entitled, we must build another europe and in writing. the cap reform introduced, in addition to decoupling aid from production, a new tool: modulation. in concrete terms, this means the possibility of transferring part of the appropriations, direct aid to farmers, to rural development appropriations. it's called "transferring from the first pillar to the second pillar". this transfer may be voluntary up to 20%. the member states may decide to use this partial menu modulation instead of a menu imposed between 'direct aid' as a main course and 'rural development' as a dessert. in reality, modulation is like stripping paul the farmer to dress peter the landscape designer. it is a budgetary technique which seeks to hide the lack of appropriations by creating the illusion of a choice in the management of the shortage of these appropriations.

the president of the council. i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. i am speaking jointly for the commission and the council. the commission and the council take full account of the european parliament's concerns regarding respect for human rights in the russian federation. the commission and the council reaffirm that respect for human rights is a fundamental factor in the implementation of the agreements between the european community and the russian federation on visa facilitation and readmission. they will closely monitor this aspect in the framework of the joint committees established by the readmission agreement and the visa facilitation agreement. in the latter, you will also take into account the principle of reciprocity in the implementation of the agreement, equal treatment in the registration of nationals of the european union and of the russian federation, and the free movement of persons within the territory of the russian federation. respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms is the foundation of relations between the european union and russia as a whole, which are based on the partnership and cooperation agreements and common space roadmaps. in addition, in accordance with the roadmap for a common area of freedom, security and justice, the european union and the russian federation have agreed to strengthen their cooperation by respecting the rights of individuals in the eu member states and russia, including immigrants and persons belonging to minorities, and respecting fundamental rights and freedoms as set out in the convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms and the international convention on the elimination of all forms of racial discrimination. the roadmap also provides for the promotion of cooperation in the protection of children's rights and, in this context, explores the possibility of accession to international conventions. the semiannual eu-russia human rights consultations also provide an opportunity for the eu to discuss more general issues with russia.
member of the commission. mr president, firstly i would like to thank the rapporteur of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, mrs esteves, and the rapporteurs of the committee on foreign affairs, mr pinior and mr vatanen, for their reports on visa facilitation and readmission agreements. they reflect the european parliament’s concerns and the advice to which the commission will pay great attention in monitoring the implementation of the two agreements. i wish to confirm the joint council-commission statement that was just heard by you, that vice-president frattini and i have addressed to the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs at the request of its chairman, mr cavada. i would not underestimate the concerns the european union has over the human rights situation in russia. we remain worried about the shortcomings regarding in particular the rule of law and media freedom in russia. i understand and share the concerns raised by the european parliament in this regard. the commission has always looked to the european parliament as an ally in its promotion of the principles of democracy and the universality of human rights in our relations with partner countries such as russia. for their own sake, but also because they are cornerstones of peace and human development, they are indeed agreed common values and the foundations of the long-term strategic partnership which the european union wants to have with russia. since the beginning, the commission has been and will continue to emphasise to the russian authorities that our strategic partnership is based on common values which underpin eu-russia relations as enshrined in the partnership and cooperation agreement and in the four common spaces roadmaps. they explicitly foresee the strengthening of our cooperation through respect of individual rights in the eu member states and russia. the readmission agreement fully respects human rights and fundamental freedoms and is consistent with the eu’s human rights policies. article 18 of the agreement explicitly clarifies that it is without prejudice to the rights, obligations and responsibilities of the community, the member states and the russian federation arising from international law, in particular from the 1951 geneva refugee convention, the 1950 european convention on human rights and the 1984 un convention against torture and other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. the practical implementation of the readmission agreement will fall under the exclusive competence of the member states and russia’s national authorities. all of those authorities are directly bound by the above-mentioned international instruments and their individual return decisions are subject to judicial review before national courts. as far as asylum seekers are concerned, i would like to clarify that they are not included in the scope of the readmission agreement. they have for the duration of their asylum procedure a temporary right to stay in the territory of member states. the agreement covers only illegal immigrants, that means people who do not or no longer fulfil the conditions in force for entry to, presence in, or residence in the territory. in the case of asylum applications at the border, the principle of non refoulement has in particular to be fully respected by member states in accordance with article 18 of the agreement. honourable members, the extension of our common borders after the eu enlargement has of course broadened the scope of our cooperation with russia. russia is, and should be, a strategic partner and an important neighbour to the european union. now migration policy and movement of people have become strategic priorities for the eu’s external relations in general and with russia in particular. i firmly believe that only by engaging with russia can we achieve real results in those areas of common concern. through visa facilitation, we are decisively contributing to the common objective of building a new europe without dividing lines and facilitating travel among our citizens. we are fostering trust and dialogue. people-to-people contacts are intensifying and our economic and societal interaction is increasing to the benefit of all our citizens. through readmission we are effectively fighting illegal migration, contributing to joint migration management. finally, the first agreement on visa facilitation ever negotiated by the community and the first readmission agreement concluded with a major partner country are tangible signs of our practical cooperation within the aforementioned common space on freedom, security and justice. they are evidence of our resolve to successfully address common challenges with russia. they will remain, i think, as landmark, sectoral agreements within the overall new architecture provided by the strategic agreement on which we hope to launch negotiations with russia soon.

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, budgetary aid has long had a very bad reputation and it is the failure of the ultra-liberal approach to structural adjustment plans that has led to budgetary aid now occupying a prominent place in the union's cooperation policy and being enshrined, as you said earlier, in a european consensus. it is now seen as a key tool in the fight against poverty and in achieving the millennium development goals, because it allows for more direct access to the most vulnerable populations and concentrates resources on the essential sectors of education and basic health. it is also making a decisive contribution to the rehabilitation of states, which is very important, because it is the state's failure and its inability to carry out its basic public service missions that are hindering development today, particularly in sub-saharan africa. it promotes ownership, i.e. the ability of the recipient country to choose its own development process, and it is also a valuable instrument for political dialogue between donors and recipients and perhaps even support for parliaments in their role of controlling public finances. but budget support cannot achieve its objectives unless the necessary conditions are met, in particular good governance and the fight against corruption, democracy, respect for fundamental freedoms, and a system of public financial management controlled by a democratically elected parliament. all this was very clearly stated in my colleague mr gahler's report. but while budget support really needs clarity, transparency and democracy, sometimes it is the lack of transparency that prevails, as the court of auditors' report has shown, because in several countries - kenya, malawi - the commission has used budget support without the conditions, the right preconditions, having been met. it is true that we are now waiting for very precise answers from the commission, that we are waiting for it to shed light on these countries that have been mentioned and to introduce controls. i would rather advocate, as in the report, external control, either through the intervention of the court of auditors or through the creation of a control body in cooperation with the other donors. i believe that parliament will support this new instrument that you have put in place, with careful monitoring.
mr president, i welcome the fact that our committee has taken the initiative to speak on the effectiveness of budget support. the report, which is rather critical, contains many reservations. i agree with each of them and would like to illustrate them a little more. the country strategy papers we are currently examining show that the commission's budget support is often a black box, impossible to evaluate. for example, in cambodia and laos, the commission proposes to allocate between 40% and 60% of the total budget to the national programme to combat poverty, without giving any indication of the sectors which will actually be financed. more worryingly, when the commission reveals the sectors which were financed in the past in its programmes, it is found that they did not contribute directly to the fight against poverty. under the guise of financing national development programmes, the commission is in fact financing measures to improve the business climate, investment and trade. therefore, it is not enough to strengthen sectorisation and conditionality of budget support; the commission must also have a real intention to pursue the objectives of poverty reduction and the achievement of the millennium development goals. that is why, to avoid such a drift - and i propose this whenever i can because it is a deep conviction of mine - care must be taken to decentralize a significant percentage of budgetary support to the benefit of ngos and local authorities. this would prevent central governments from managing and monopolizing all european budgetary support. decentralising aid would bring people closer to european funding and thus ensure that our financial support benefits the people on the ground.
in writing. the achievement of the millennium development goals by 2015 requires a strong commitment by the international community to poverty reduction. the effectiveness of its aid instruments is a key prerequisite for sustainable aid that meets the needs of developing countries. at a time when the principle of aid effectiveness is a priority for the european union, budget support is proving to be appropriate, responding to the principle of appropriation and the need for better coordination between donors. if this instrument seems to meet the requirements of aid effectiveness, it must be used under certain conditions. finally, budget support allows recipient governments to take a more assertive role in the coordination of development aid: this active approach creates the spirit of partnership needed to address the problems of appropriation and sustainability of aid. reducing poverty is a non-negotiable objective. the involvement of all actors is therefore necessary for its achievement. developing countries and the european union must work to ensure that the promises of the millennium summit in 2000 are fulfilled. the european union, on the other hand, must live up to the expectations it has created.
the rapporteur. mr president, illegal fishing is a phenomenon which is now growing considerably and is seriously damaging the activities of both european fisheries, local fishing communities and fisheries in developing countries, particularly those with which the european community has fisheries agreements. it is also, unfortunately, a very lucrative business. i would like to give the example of bluefin tuna, particularly in the mediterranean, which are sold at very high prices. this is a vicious circle, leading to a gradual but accelerated degradation of fisheries resources. legal fisheries, those that respect the regulations, are, on the other hand, very seriously penalized by these illegal activities, which have a rather broad definition. we are talking about illegal, unregulated, unreported fishing. this is true of many activities: illegal fishing, the use of unauthorised fishing gear, the taking of unauthorised species, fishing without a licence or the policy of transhipping cargoes from one vessel to another. the range of illegal activities is extremely wide. what is the purpose of this own-initiative report? in 2002, fao launched an international action plan against illegal fishing, which was then followed by an eu action plan, adopted by the council in 2002, which has unfortunately been implemented by member states in varying degrees. at the moment, the european commission is evaluating the action plans of the member states to combat illegal fishing in the run-up to the fao fisheries committee meeting in rome in the first week of march, which will be the occasion for relaunching the international action plan against illegal fishing. the european union has a huge responsibility in this area. why would you do that? firstly, because the european union is the third largest fishing power after china and peru. it represents one of the largest fleets in the world. it also makes extensive use of flags of convenience, which pose enormous problems not only for fisheries but also for maritime transport. finally, the eu is also one of the largest fish markets in the world. so there are many responsibilities. the commission replies that this is all complex, that there are many players involved, that nothing can be done alone, that it is expensive, that it is not possible to ask member states to respect certain rules and not others, etc. the pretexts and excuses are indeed numerous for not doing much, and unfortunately there have not been enough initiatives to combat effectively this illegal fishing activity, which, once again, has been growing in extreme severity in recent years. the responsibilities are those of the so-called port state, the flag state and the state where the fishery products are marketed. there are many levels: the level of regional fisheries organisations, the level of the member states, the european level; it is at all these levels that action is needed, in a transversal way, involving dg/fisheries as well as dg/environment, dg/development and dg/commerce. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. what are the main points of my report, which was unanimously approved by the committee on fisheries, which shows that this is a matter of common concern to all our member states? there is the traceability of fishery products, the establishment of blacklists, i.e. lists of vessels that are not authorized to fish or that have already been sanctioned for illegal fishing activities. it is regrettable that there is no coordination and consultation between the various sources of information on these vessels, whether they are authorized to fish or not. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the protection of the environment is a very important one. the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat illegal fishing, including the introduction of a new system of fishing quotas for the baltic sea. in conclusion, we absolutely need a more integrated european policy, both in terms of control and surveillance, but also in terms of sanctions. it is in this overall perspective that the report outlines a number of ways and proposes a number of measures which we are discussing here, in view of the fao meeting in march next year, in which we must absolutely show ourselves to be much more willing, much more dynamic.

mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like first of all to thank our colleague, mr joel hasse ferreira, for the work he has done. dealing with social services of general interest, the ssig, is not easy, but he was able to listen throughout our working meetings. the important point of our colleague's report is the launching of a consultation of the relevant actors, in order to take better account of the specificities of the gss in the application of community law. social services are characterised in particular by the fact that they are personalised, that they implement fundamental social rights and that they contribute to social cohesion by protecting the most vulnerable. as such, they are an integral part of the european social model, as they are, in their present form, a european specificity and contribute to the european growth strategy. they are a dynamic sector of activity and job creator, while distinguishing themselves from other services of general economic interest. their operation is based on the principle of solidarity and proximity to the users. the problem with the vast majority of gis is that they are directly within the scope of the community treaties. in other words, they are subject to the rules of the internal market and competition. the question of the application of these rules therefore arose in the light of the need to maintain public intervention in service provision structures. this objective of public regulation meets legitimate objectives of accessibility and continuity of quality of services in the living areas, as well as protection of users and vulnerable persons who benefit from them. our social model, which we want to promote as an alternative to ultra-liberalism, cannot be a victim of our own community rules.
mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate mr hasse ferreira on the quality of his report and the crucial points it contains. i would also like to recall the european citizens' mobilization a year ago when the services directive was voted. this mobilization has made it possible to change the text and to change the position of our institutions in their desire to liberalize all services, regardless of the missions and needs they represent. we must today echo those citizens, the values they hold dear and which we share and which our rapporteur gives substance to. the missions assumed by the ssigs serve human rights, personal dignity, the general interest and social cohesion and are therefore in line with the charter of fundamental rights. to refuse to recognize this, to continue to confuse the notions of economic service and market service, as the commission does, is to renounce the social specificity of europe and what it represents for millions of its citizens. specific legislation is needed to guarantee the exercise and the right to these services.
mr president, as everyone has said, the report by our colleague mr ferreira brings us once again to the heart of this european social model, which is why we are not the united states. and behind this relationship, of course, there are children, there are the elderly, there are the sick, the excluded, the handicapped, and finally, in the end, if we are not careful, there is euthanasia with the netherlands, belgium, and soon france. we are therefore in the sphere of what we french have been calling "public services" for over a century, in thousands of books, courses and university theses. that is why the french people, on 29 may 2005, rejected the constitution of the private services. we, with the beautiful word "public service", say that in the society of women and men, there are common parts of the national co-ownership, and that it is in the common parts, such as the hospital, the school, the health, that services are provided to the public. and this terminology is superior to that of service of general interest, which creates ambiguity and boundary problems between the private and the general interest, as well as between the commercial market, with the competition of major interests, and the public goods, what st. thomas aquinas already called the commons. and it is precisely because of this problem of frontiers that we legislate: what are these services, where do they come from, what budget to allocate to them, what are the competences of the union on the one hand and of subsidiarity on the other, what are the geographical boundaries between mrs thatcher's europe and the europe of social policy, what are the boundaries in terms of housing, employment, childcare, hospital care, between the rich who can go to the private sector and the poor who cannot? a president of the united states had a sign on his desk that said, "here stops the money, here stops the money". that's the definition of public service: "here stops the market".

between member states what has to be done. i should also like to comment on simplification and better regulation. let me start by saying that i have often heard the criticism that the commission is legislating too little or that it is not ambitious enough in legislating. we have compiled and checked all the statistics and, if you look at the amount of legislation adopted by the commission, it has remained remarkably stable. if we look at the number of regulations, directives, decisions and recommendations adopted over the past 10 years, it has only once topped 550 and has only once dropped below 430. the average has been some 489 proposals a year, and last year, at 474, we were very close to that average. so, whatever may be said, those are the facts. nevertheless, with the careful consultation and impact assessments we are now carrying out on every proposal included in the work programme, i think that we are making particular efforts to ensure that our proposals are well prepared and of high quality. it is therefore important to bear these figures and statistics in mind. we take the whole issue of simplification seriously and, as you know, we have set out a very ambitious simplification programme of 100 proposals, covering about 220 legislative instruments to be repealed, codified, recast or reviewed over the next three years. on average, there have been about 40 or 43 proposals to simplify legislation or identify legislation which is outdated. we will continue along the same path and at the same pace in order to constantly review legislation. in some cases, it means that we can introduce new legislation and, at the same time, abandon or scrap directives, as we did with reach, where the 40 existing directives were replaced by a single one. we also have to be careful to ensure that our legislation is up to date and modern and that we get rid of legislation that is outdated. therefore, we will continue along the same path and will inform and involve the european parliament so that we can work hand-in-hand to ensure that the overall political objectives of the lisbon strategy are implemented – the four overall priorities that we set out in in writing. i see three fundamental contradictions in this report on corporate social responsibility. the first is to claim that this responsibility is voluntary, but at the same time to call for the development of frameworks, standards, definitions, controls and incentives so varied and so constraining that the voluntary nature of this approach is called into question. the second is to claim to encourage corporate social responsibility when all the policies of the european union, and in particular competition policy, encourage companies to relocate, to seek the so-called tax, social, environmental and labour cost minimum, including within the eu. the third is to impose the practice of social responsibility on european companies, without really calling into question the global ultra-trading system and by continuing to open our markets to imports from countries which practice dumping in all its forms, forced labour, child labour or political prisoners. there's a certain hypocrisy to that. even if you defend yourself, you are holding corporations accountable and making them suffer the consequences of your policies, your failures, your impotence and your resignations.
in writing. corporate social responsibility is a catch-all concept which, despite the imagination of the europeans, is not original. this uncomplicated gadget appeared in the united states in the 1950's. in france, the concept of "citizen enterprise" appeared in particular with the sudreau report in 1975. and in 1982 social objectives will be imposed on public sector enterprises to impress the people and the cadres of victorious socialism. twenty-five years later, csr simply wants to humanize and regulate globalism. these pious wishes in times of unemployment and social insecurity amid international instability give csr the image of a vast smokehouse. clearly we must stop wasting our time and money on considerations that seek only to pass on silly and nice messages while we are lagging behind the world. let's be responsible for our own first. let us respect ourselves by applying in europe a community preference and protection of persons, products and undertakings. for example, we should increase customs duties on imports of products from third countries which have not been manufactured in accordance with minimum european social standards.

the rapporteur. mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to thank you all for your cooperation and also to congratulate the officials of the parliament's committee on agriculture and the european commission who have given me the necessary technical support. this is a sensitive issue on which the member states and the european commission have been seeking agreement since the early 1990s, as the commissioner has just reminded us. the crux of the problem is that when veal is sold, there is generally no reference to the type of feed the animals received or their age at the time of slaughter, whereas farming practices vary widely from one member state to another. the translation of the texts has led to very different products being offered to traders and consumers, but sold under the same name: veal. as the european commission points out, such a practice is likely to distort trade and encourage the establishment of conditions of unfair competition. the studies show that the term 'beef' is a sales denomination which a number of operators use to benefit from significantly higher market prices, when in fact they market young bovine meat with very different organoleptic qualities. it was at the request of several member states and the european beef sector, which wanted clarification, that the commission drew up its initial proposal, which i think is quite appropriate. the commission proposes to establish precise sales denominations according to the age of slaughter, a rather significant criterion which is easier to control than feeding. the commission proposes to create two categories and to use a letter to identify them: 'x' for animals slaughtered between zero and eight months, and 'y' for animals slaughtered between nine and twelve months, letters which the european parliament's agriculture committee has preferred to replace with 'v' and 'z' in order to avoid gender-related confusion. for the first category, the sales denomination shall always include the terminology 'veal'; for the second, we will use another terminology: "jeune bovin" in french, "vitellone" in italian, etc. i refer you to annex ii (b) to the rules of procedure. there is an exception for the domestic marketing of four countries, denmark, greece, spain and the netherlands, where, in order to take account of cultural usage and traditions, the term 'wheat' may always be referred to in the second category. the terms 'beef', 'veal' or any other sales denomination defined in the proposal will therefore no longer be allowed to be used for the labelling of meat from animals over 12 months of age. of course, traders who wish to supplement the sales descriptions set out in this proposal with other information provided on an optional basis, such as the feed, will be able to do so. so, coming from limousin, i could tell you about the "white vault". i have tried to propose amendments to the original proposal of the european commission to make this legislation more coherent and binding and i thank my colleagues for their support. i have in particular called for the introduction of a system of penalties for non-compliance with the rules and proposed amendments to include meat preparations for human consumption, processed, processed or cooked products within the scope of the regulation. i also insisted that the sales denomination be used at every stage of production and marketing. however, i consider that a number of points are unacceptable and risk upsetting the balance of the proposal for a regulation. these are amendments nos 8 and 12 adopted by the committee on agriculture. amendment no 8 suggests that names and pgi registered after the publication of this regulation could derogate from it, which is not consistent with the legislation as a whole. the already registered protected designations of origin and protected geographical indications are not affected, but it is important that new aocs and pgi are subject to the provisions of this regulation, otherwise they could be circumvented. amendment no 12 calls into question the proposal for a regulation which is based on the age criterion. however, as shown in annex ii, the united kingdom chose to give the name 'veal' to the first category and the name 'beef' to the second category. the specific features of this country have therefore been taken into account. i also do not support the two new amendments 26 and 27 tabled for the plenary. these two amendments introduce a new derogation from article 3 of the regulation which is unacceptable in my view, by allowing a given member state not to apply the regulation if its production of animals of the first category, from zero to eight months, does not exceed 3% of the total production of animals aged from zero to twelve months. i would ask you, ladies and gentlemen, to support me and reject these four amendments which would reduce the scope of the regulation which is supposed to apply throughout the european union and the scope of the harmonization of the first category, 'zero to eight months', which has been very difficult to achieve.

in writing. for ten years now, various initiatives have been taken to harmonize the rules for the marketing of meat from bovine animals aged less than 12 months, without success. until now, france and other member states which gave priority to the quality of meat by fixing the age of slaughter of cattle at less than 8 months and feeding them milk were harmed by the lack of harmonisation in the designation of veal meat. the consumer could be misled, since two meats of different age, taste and quality could bear the same name and the same labelling. i am therefore pleased that we have finally found a compromise, and a compromise which has not been achieved at the expense of tradition or quality. the report takes account of internal market considerations but respects traditions, preserving pgi and aocs. i am glad to see that europe is not only concerned about the safety standards that beef meets, these difficulties have been overcome. it was a matter of promoting quality and consumer information, and that is the spirit of the report we are voting on today.
mr president, we are in the middle of the erika trial. the case of erika is emblematic of these preventable disasters, but they happen anyway, because the gains of a handful of individuals must necessarily come first. this is the result of a liberal profit-making mentality that goes to the extreme, whereby to make a few extra dollars, anything is permissible, including the most basic safety rules, to the point of disaster. the same logic is at work in the infamous case of irish ferries, which will soon be irish in name only: in the name of profit, the entire staff of a company that is functioning properly is thrown overboard. this is the same logic which drives some shipowners operating intra-community cabotage to operate vessels with insufficient crews and in conditions which endanger both the crews and navigation as a whole. these poor working conditions even threaten european maritime traditions and know-how, since they give such an image of the sector that it has become increasingly difficult to recruit european seamen! of course, this profit logic is never invoked. no, it is rather the argument of international competition, essentially asian and obviously 'unfair', which is used to justify these practices. even where such competition does not exist; have we ever seen chinese companies operating ferries in the baltic or the english channel? this competition is not about denying it. it affects a part of the sector, and it also has its merits. but she needs to be coached, and she needs to be loyal. above all, it is possible to choose the elements on which it is to be based, and although social dumping is unfortunately a sad reality in the maritime sector, it is not inevitable. so, yes, there are those who are accommodating, and seeking to profit from it. but it can also be refused by pushing for a general raising of social standards throughout the world, so that all are ultimately on an equal footing in international competition. this is the path i want europe to take, as you will have understood. because we know that competitiveness for europe will not be achieved by minimising costs and lowering social standards. it can only be done on quality. the quality of the ships, the quality of the crews, guaranteed by decent training and working conditions. the ilo convention, which we are discussing tonight, gives us the opportunity to make that choice. it doesn't solve all the problems, but it's a step forward. it is also an opportunity for european shipowners and member states to demonstrate their commitment to defending certain values which the european union and its social model embody. by signing it in february 2006, they signed a declaration of intent to this effect. we are now waiting for them to act. as far as shipowners are concerned, i can only welcome the fact that they have firmly and willingly embarked on the path of european social dialogue with their trade union partners, with a view to the signing, by the end of the year, of a european collective agreement which would incorporate the relevant provisions of this convention. a first round of negotiations ended today, and the climate seems very constructive. that's a good thing. and i think we can also welcome the constructive role played by the european commission in facilitating this process. the member states hold the key to the entry into force of this convention. as we said, if the eu and efta ratify, then the convention will enter into force, and it will apply everywhere. if europe ratifies quickly, other nations will follow, and europe will have played a leading role, also by demonstrating that another way is possible than that of exploitation and dumping, and that competition can also be responsible. it is therefore essential, if we are to believe in the specificity of the european model, to ensure that this convention is ratified quickly. and it is therefore essential to keep the ilo deadline of the end of 2008.

in writing. we still see far too many air disasters, which are not only due to the poor condition of some aircraft but also to non-compliance with safety requirements. the merit of this proposal by parliament and the council is that it strengthens the obligations of the member states in respect of inspection of aircraft of third countries as well as of aircraft of community countries. in addition, if an inspection of air carriers or the activities of civil aviation authorities reveals anomalies or non-compliance with standard safety rules, the european aviation safety agency will have the power to trigger a sanction mechanism and to withdraw the authorisation to carry passengers to the union from the air carriers found to be in breach. i believe that this is a significant step forward in the prevention of the risk of aircraft accidents. finally, the work and mission of this agency will help to complete, i hope, the european blacklist of bad carriers. although not all questions have been resolved in the field of aviation safety, it seems that prevention and enforcement are finally being brought together in this area. we will vote in favour.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on social services of general interest. i welcome the continuity and consistency of parliament's vote on the need for legal certainty and clarification of the community framework for social services of general interest. i believe that this report strikes a balance between the application of community law in the strict sense and the fulfilment of the general interest tasks of the social services. this is a necessary preliminary step to the establishment of a sectoral directive on social services of general interest, which parliament has clearly called for in the rapkay report on the white paper on services of general interest. i also welcome the proposal to convene a forum on social services of general interest at the initiative of parliament and call for its effective establishment under the portuguese presidency of the european union.
in writing. paragraph 6 of this report on social services of general interest recalls 'the freedom of national authorities to define, organise and finance social services of general interest as they see fit', under the principle of subsidiarity. this one sentence, despite the union's alleged 'co-responsibility', makes the rest of the text useless: public services are and must continue to be the sole prerogative of the states. and it is up to each state to decide whether these services depend on the market, or on national solidarity guaranteeing the common good, or on a fair proportion between these two elements. in other words, it is not for the commission or the luxembourg court of justice to define, let alone regulate, public services. we know well what happens if this is not done: privatization of profits in the name of ultraliberalism and competition, to the great advantage of international capital; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft budget for the financial year. it is difficult to overstate the responsibility of these policies for the social disintegration our countries are experiencing today.
in writing. mr ferreira is right when he says that social services of general interest are an essential component of the european social model, based on the protection of the most vulnerable people: children, the elderly, the sick, the disabled, the unemployed, etc. three phenomena are challenging this social model today. one, uncontrolled immigration is wrecking our welfare systems. in france, for example, the cost of providing free public health care to illegal immigrants is estimated at 600 million euros a year. secondly, the destruction of frontiers which, by subjecting our companies to international competition and social dumping, particularly in china, destroys the economic basis of this social model. thirdly, the gradual abolition of public services decided in 2000 at the european summit in lisbon. the report by mr ferreira does not propose any solution, because these phenomena are the result of the ultra-liberal ideology implemented by the europe of brussels. only a different europe, the europe of the homelands, based on respect for national sovereignty, on community preference and on borders protecting it from unrestrained immigration and unfair international competition, will enable our nations to rebuild a european social model.
in writing. social services of general interest are an essential component of the european social model. the communication presented by the european commission on these services opens up the prospect of clarifying their place within the european union as regards the social aspects, the concepts applicable to them and the legal certainty to be granted to them. the models for the organisation and management of gis differ widely in the various member states. one of the aspects on which the commission must concentrate is the creation of a legal instrument, and in particular a sectoral directive, to guarantee political clarity of procedures and legal certainty for the social organisations concerned. the holding of a forum by parliament under the portuguese presidency, in collaboration with all the social partners, will help to achieve this objective. the gis contributes significantly to the social dimension of the lisbon strategy, both in terms of the volume of employment it can create and in terms of the social cohesion it helps to ensure in a differentiated way in the european union. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of mr hasse ferreira's report.

policy is a priority for our institution and must remain so. the report i am presenting to you analyses the results of more than 12 years of cooperation in the objectives of the barcelona conference. spirit, this general balance, reinforced by the vote in committee, must guide the vote in plenary tomorrow. we must first establish a finding. although each part of the world has its own specific features, relations between the union and the southern shore of the mediterranean are marked by a history of conflict, misunderstanding and instability, a troubled and even tragic history. that is why i have tried to construct this report with a view to a highly political approach. a hope was born with the barcelona summit in 1995. the political will expressed was to build a comprehensive partnership between the european union and the mediterranean countries, with the aim of making the region a common area of peace, stability and prosperity. but we must now see that the results have not lived up to the hopes and expectations. we have been living in an unstable political context since then: the war in lebanon, the absence of prospects for peace in the middle east, the complex relations between the western world and the arab and muslim countries since 11 september 2001, the distant relations between the partners in the south. i would like to add that i believe it is wrong
