for the gue/ngl group mr president, what exactly does the transatlantic economic partnership hold for us? mrs merkel said it was not about free trade or a common market, but about market regulation, patent protection, harmonisation of rules and cooperation to improve global economic governance. the secretary of state, mr würmeling, was more direct in stating that the aim was to move towards a transatlantic market without barriers. the chancellor herself had suggested that the experience of the european single market could serve as a model for this new area. but is it necessary to recall the definition of the single market given by the commissioner responsible for monitoring it, mr mccreevy? as he pointed out, the single market 'is by far the most extensive exercise in deregulation in europe's recent history'. is this the kind of experience that should be generalized across the atlantic? the question is all the more worthy of being asked, since this project already has a tumultuous history. in march 1998, commissioner leon brittan, then a leading figure in liberal europe, launched the new transatlantic market project, modelled on the north american free trade agreement, nafta. at the same time, the draft multilateral investment agreement, the ami, was being negotiated in secret at the oecd, and was already aimed at cracking down on any legislation perceived by investors as a hindrance to their increasingly sprawling financial operations. these two projects aroused such a reaction in european opinion that they had to be abandoned. but since then, lobbies such as the transatlantic business dialogue have repeatedly brought this strategic project to the table in a new form. the adoption last year of american accounting standards and, more recently, the takeover of the european euronex stock exchanges by the new york stock exchange are part of this heavy trend. far from the image of constructive cooperation that we are being sold, this is indeed a major front in the battle over the design of europe's future. both its social model and its democratic identity are at stake. i would remind you that the report adopted by parliament on this subject last june deplored the fact that 'the relations between the union and the united states are burdened by political conflicts and are quite frequently characterized by grand declarations'. in the name of the common values of the transatlantic business dialogue, are we to be silent on the war in iraq or guantanamo? on the death penalty or the international criminal court? kyoto or gmos? on the personal data, the swift case, or the cia thefts? as the process leading to a new european treaty is under way, the nature of the relationship between the european union and the united states is a crucial issue that will need to be addressed clearly.

mr president, the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the basis of rule 170 (4) of our rules of procedure, would like to defer the vote on this resolution to the second part-session in september. this postponement is to adapt our timetable to the new timetable set by the commission at our request for the approval of the accounting standard ifrs 8 replacing ias 14. the commission's proposal to approve ifrs 8 would mean the incorporation of the equivalent us accounting standard into european law without an impact assessment of the effect of the application of such a standard on european listed companies having been carried out. the committee on economic and monetary affairs would point out that the convergence between ifrs and us gaap accounting standards, which is the strong desire of commissioner mccreevy, must lead to standards that allow for better quality financial reporting. real convergence means much more than one party simply copying the accounting standards of the other. in this context, the commission services agreed to revise their timetable, thus allowing an impact assessment to be carried out. this information was sent to us by post last night. the committee on economic and monetary affairs would also like to point out that the commission's proposals for implementing measures, at least in the financial field, including financial information standards, must be examined within three months. we hope that the commission will be able to present this implementing measure, together with the results of the impact study requested, to our committee on 10 september, so that parliament can, at its september part-session, give final approval or not to the application of this standard in european law.

in writing. i voted in favour of the excellent report by my colleague nicolas zingaretti on the amended proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on criminal measures aimed at ensuring respect for intellectual property rights. of course, the european commission does not and should not have criminal jurisdiction except to negotiate between peoples. criminal justice belongs to the people and not to the european union. this does not prevent directives from being adopted which send messages to the member states in order to ensure the effectiveness of community law. it is therefore urgent to build a reliable and respected european legal framework in the field of patents and intellectual property more generally. counterfeiting, piracy, copying, theft, etc. are becoming too serious to be left unpunished.
in writing. i voted in favour of the excellent report by my colleague and friend dominique vlasto on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on port state control. i am not an expert on the subject but i welcome the important work done by dominique vlasto to defend a balanced position on the regulations on the inspection of ships entering a port in the european union. it is clear that, in view of the unfortunate events which have occurred, the control of the flag must be supplemented by a control of the port by the state. the directive, which has been revised much more ambitiously than the european commission had originally proposed, and which was led by mrs vlasto, is a step towards increasing maritime safety in the interests of europe's coasts, the environment, businesses and citizens.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text. this report raises the debate on potential improvements to the eu's competitive environment, in particular for private actions for damages for infringements of competition law brought before civil courts. i am of the opinion that such actions for damages should be facilitated. the aim is to "promote competition and not judicialisation". it would be appropriate to promote quick, amicable solutions of an extrajudicial nature. 90% of disputes between traders and consumers are settled amicably. companies tend to compromise, even when they are not liable, in order to avoid a lengthy legal procedure. it is desirable that europe does not directly import the american-style procedure. the commission has therefore decided to give priority to alternative dispute settlement methods. if all the minds are thinking of the large groups that would be attacked in this way, smes are obviously not immune. so we must be on guard against endangering their survival.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on a thematic strategy for the sustainable use of natural resources. no one is arguing that our natural resources are under threat. the present population growth of the planet of one billion additional inhabitants in twelve years with a population, today, of 6.5 billion inhabitants justifies, in itself, the attention we must have to our natural resources. the report could have been more ambitious, structured and documented, but it is nonetheless a good document to be used in this difficult area of sustainable development.
in writing. in the aftermath of the erika and prestige oil tanker disasters, the european socialists fought for eu legislation to improve maritime safety and prevent accidental pollution in its territorial waters this fight has borne fruit, but the creation of a genuine european maritime safety area is not yet complete. this 'third maritime security package' is a decisive step towards this objective. the five reports submitted to the european parliament contain several major advances:- a clear and precise legal framework for places of refuge for ships in distress, under the aegis of an independent authority,- a permanent inspection body to facilitate investigations,- a high level of protection for passengers, in line with that of other means of transport,- enhanced quality and efficiency of controls in european ports, with particular attention to 'high risk' ships. i shall therefore vote in favour of these reports. i now hope that the eu will also improve its legislation against the 'sea bandits' responsible for the 'daily oil spills' in the mediterranean: 650 000 tonnes of oil residues every year from wild discharges, the equivalent of 75 erika!

in writing. the freitas report, which is being put to the vote today, concerns the outermost regions and, in particular, réunion. the outermost regions are subject to geographical and geopolitical constraints which increase their isolation and limit their ability to export their goods to the european continent. this system of compensation for additional costs supports local fisheries through the processing, transport and marketing of fishery products to the european continent. it also contributes to increasing the competitiveness of local businesses and the sector at european level. the effectiveness of this scheme can be illustrated by the fact that these compensations have allowed an increase in volume and value of reunion's exports since 2000. the renewal of this compensation scheme will make it possible to continue the effort to integrate the industrial, long-line and coastal fishing sectors of the outermost regions into the internal market. this effort must be supported by other factors such as taking into account the change in oil prices, since it must not be forgotten that the outermost regions are highly dependent on it and that transport costs represent a drag on the export of local products.
in writing. i am very pleased with the report by mr duarte freitas, which takes full account of the additional costs faced by some octs in exporting fishery products. the interests of guyana and réunion, which export such products, have been well defended. the european parliament has made the following four demands in particular. firstly, the initial ceiling for compensation for additional costs, arbitrarily set at 75%, should be abolished. on the one hand, this rate is not based on any logical criteria and, on the other hand, there is no reason why fishery products should not benefit from a regime as favourable as agricultural products. secondly, that state aid for the production, processing and marketing of fishery products from these regions be allowed and that compensation be granted for imported products used in the processing of fishery products, such as salt or oils. thirdly, that the use of intra-community imports be allowed if the catch of the outermost regions' fleets is insufficient to guarantee the profitability of the processing industries in these regions. finally, the financial envelope for guyana and réunion should be increased to eur 5 518 000.
in writing. the regulation before us establishes a mechanism to provide, for a limited period, assistance in the form of rapid border intervention teams to a member state facing a massive influx of illegal immigrants. this reserve of 250 to 500 border guards within the european border agency (frontex) will be made available to member states that need them to protect their external borders. it is true that while external border control is a matter for the states and falls within the intergovernmental domain, the massive flows of illegal immigration that occurred, in particular, between 15 august and 15 december 2006 off the coast of west africa towards the canary islands, demonstrated how permeable the external borders of the union were to exponential immigration. cooperation between states is therefore essential in this field. more than 31 000 illegal immigrants landed in the canary islands in 2006, six times as many as the previous year. we are in favour of the principle of cooperation between member states for the protection of the external borders of the european union, but we remain very vigilant about the anecdotal nature of frontex, which is mainly used for media purposes, and about any federalist and supranational drift of this agency.
in writing. as several member states have been faced with critical situations due to massive influxes of illegal immigrants by sea, the european union has found it necessary to create rapid border intervention teams. solidarity between member states is the basis of such an undertaking. these teams are not set up with the objective of repressing these people. it is rather a question of providing european assistance to member states which are receiving too large an influx of illegal immigrants. the events of last summer have confirmed the urgency of preventing difficult situations both for the states of destination and transit and for the immigrants themselves. these teams will therefore be tasked with patrolling the outer borders of the european union under the authority of the national border guards of the host member state. members of rapid reaction teams shall be able to exercise all the necessary skills for border checks or border surveillance activities. however, it is foreseen that they will have to fully respect human dignity in the exercise of their activities; the european union has also recognised the right to freedom of movement for workers. in conclusion, the concerns expressed by some about the use of these rapid border intervention teams should not be realised over time.

the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, health services are one of the pillars of the european social model. this is why they have been excluded from the services directive and must be dealt with specifically, as part of a wider reflection on the health sector in europe. the commission's consultation cannot be limited to patient mobility alone, but should be an opportunity to define the role and added value of the european union in ensuring that every citizen not only has equal access to health care, but also a high level of health protection, while respecting the competences of the states and the principle of subsidiarity. european health policy cannot be limited to the mobility of patients and professionals and cannot be limited to the creation of an internal market in health services, which would lead to a two-tier system in which only the most affluent patients would benefit and health institutions would seek to attract the most affluent patients. in addition, due to the disparity in income of professionals, medical demographic problems will undermine access to care in states where providers are less well paid, with providers being tempted to move abroad. patients should have the right to seek treatment in another state, under the freedom of movement, but there is no question of promoting medical tourism. while health services are subject to the rules of the treaty, they cannot be regarded as ordinary market services because they are entrusted with a mission of general interest. there must be a balance between free movement and overriding national objectives, linked to the management of hospital capacity, the control of health expenditure and the financial balance of social security systems. in addition, member states remain competent to organise, plan and finance their health systems. all european citizens, regardless of their income and residence, must have equal access to affordable health care, in accordance with the principles of universality, quality, safety, continuity and solidarity. this will contribute to the social and territorial cohesion of the union while ensuring the financial sustainability of national healthcare systems. patient mobility should not be used as an excuse for the states to neglect their own structures. the court's judgments have introduced a number of concepts which, as the case has shown, require a more precise approach. this is the case for the distinction between hospital and non-hospital care and the concept of reasonable delay. i regret that the commission has only very partially mentioned the mobility of professionals, whereas this subject would require a thorough study. the shortage of staff in european health services will only get worse over time. in addition, we are faced with an ageing population. is it reasonable, then, not to take up this matter now? i don't think he did. the union must commit itself to giving patients complete information so that they can make informed choices about who can treat them and according to what procedures. it is only when all these questions of procedures and criteria have been settled that we will really have 'european patients without frontiers' on our territory". in terms of cooperation, the union could promote the establishment of a european network of reference centres, or exchanges of knowledge on the best treatment practices between different countries. it is regrettable that the consultation described social services in a restrictive way, because, in terms of integration, they have a dimension that goes beyond simple assistance and action in favour of the most deprived. furthermore, the artificial distinction between health services and social services of general interest ignores the reality of the services provided. in many cases, social and health services are provided in an undifferentiated manner. this is particularly the case for health services with social support. what about the medical care in retirement homes and specialised institutions for the disabled? contrary to what the commission's consultation implied, the judgments of the european court of justice in no way require the parliament to limit itself to a mere role of codifying case law, nor do they prevent it from exercising its right as legislator to the full. the court's decisions, taken in reference to particular cases, are not sufficient to define a health policy. decisions must be taken within the framework of the democratic decision-making process. in view of the multiplicity of infringement procedures initiated by dg internal market in the field of health and the unsatisfactory legal situation of citizens who are users, it is necessary, for reasons of coherence, to provide for a directive on health services which specifies the common values and principles applicable to health systems in the union, in order to restore citizens' trust in europe in an aspect of their daily lives, health, which is their most precious asset. the union's added value can be essential in this sense and is also part of the dynamic of the lisbon strategy.

member of the commission. madam president, i am pleased to open this debate on the proposal on environmental quality standards in the field of water policy, which complements the water framework directive, which is the centrepiece of water protection for the european union. i would like to thank the rapporteur, mrs laperrouze, and the committee on the environment, public health and food safety for its considerable efforts. i would also like to thank the committee on industry, research and energy, the committee on agriculture and rural development and the committee on fisheries, and in particular the draftsman and draftswomen, mr rübig, mrs bourzai and mrs corbey respectively, for their very constructive and supportive input on this important file. protecting rivers, lakes, the coastal and marine environment from pollution caused by hazardous substances is a key priority for the commission. since the 1970s when the community took its first decisive action we have made significant progress. however, as we solved some pollution problems, others emerged. the chemical cocktail in our waters has become more complex and the sources of pollution are no longer concentrated at one point but are widespread and diffuse. there has never been a time for complacency. to tackle the pollution problems caused by these dangerous substances the commission has proposed or adopted more than 30 community acts since the water framework directive was agreed. i cannot list them all, but let me highlight some as an example. first, the commission has banned or restricted the marketing and use of 16 of the priority substances of the water framework directive. further decisions on some pesticides, biocides and other existing chemicals are in the pipeline. second, the milestone agreement on reach, the new eu chemicals policy, will require authorisation of the most hazardous substances and reduction of risks for all other chemicals regulated under the water framework directive. in summary, i underline again that also in the future the commission is committed to providing the necessary instruments for emissions control where they can result in the most efficient and proportionate action to resolve pollution caused by priority substances. at the same time i am committed to the principles of better regulation and to coming forward with additional proposals only where it can be demonstrated that the community is the most appropriate level at which to act. i shall now turn to the commission proposal for a directive on environmental quality standards for priority substances. the objective of the proposed directive is to set harmonised and transparent criteria for assessing good chemical status of surface waters, which must be achieved by 2015. thus the most important part of the proposal is annex i: the quality standards which must be respected in all rivers, lakes and coastal and territorial waters. as you know, for marine waters the proposed marine strategy directive will ensure the same level of protection regarding hazardous substances pollution in areas where the water framework directive does not apply. i underline that the proposed values for quality standards already reflect the risk to the marine ecosystem that these substances may pose. in addition, the proposal identifies two additional priority hazardous substances and repeals several directives which were adopted between 1982 and 1990. however, the proposal does not include additional measures for emissions controls for the reasons that i outlined earlier. the commission believes that emissions controls are adequately covered through other existing community legislation such as the directive on integrated pollution prevention and control. as a closing remark, i would like to emphasise that we share the objective of a high level of protection of the water environment. the commission published its first implementation report for the water framework directive on 22 march 2007, world water day. it highlighted that, despite the progress, there is much work to be done, in particular by the member states, if we want to achieve sustainable water management by making the implementation of the directive a success. the current proposal is another step in this direction and i am committed to working with the european parliament and the member states to achieve the goals that we jointly set for ourselves in the year 2000. however, there are many more steps to take and i call for your support in this process.
the rapporteur. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, you have just mentioned that chemical pollution of surface waters is a threat to the aquatic environment, to the ecosystem and, consequently, to human health. you said that the purpose of this daughter directive of the water framework directive was to combat the dissemination of toxic substances into surface waters. to this end, a discard, emission and loss inventory will be established to verify whether the targets for reducing or stopping the release and loss of pollutants are met, in accordance with article 13 (7) of the framework directive, with the deadline for the stopping target being 2025. the directive will repeal the existing daughter directives listed in annex ix to the framework directive. the directive therefore sets concentration limits in surface waters for certain types of pesticides, heavy metals and other chemicals which are dangerous to aquatic fauna and flora and to human health. the impact studies carried out by the commission have led to the setting of levels for environmental quality standards on the basis of an annual average providing a level of protection against long-term exposures and on the basis of a maximum allowable concentration for protection against short-term exposures. however, some of the eqs values are still subject to debate, in particular for benzene and cadmium, hexachlorobenzene and hexachlorobutadiene, mercury, nickel, lead, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons also, because some impact studies have not been completed, which has, nevertheless, hindered our debates. the amendments proposed by the committee on the environment show the desire to establish common methodologies in order to guarantee an adequate level of protection and to avoid distortions of competition between member states. we have also considered the possibility of allowing transitional overrun zones. indeed, if we were to delete this paragraph, would we be more advanced? the analysis area is what counts. if we do not define transitional zones, we may have a perverse effect, which is to avoid checks in these zones and, therefore, to be unaware of what is happening there. we therefore proposed that the states should be allowed to define transitional zones, but with the obligation to reduce these zones in order to ensure that environmental quality standards are eventually met. we have also raised the particular case of port areas where, because of the mixing of water bodies caused by the dredging of rivers and estuaries, the quality standards or the method of analysis do not seem to be adequate. we have discussed at length the advisability of adding highly toxic substances to the list of substances originally proposed by the commission. this was eventually compromised. we ask that the commission carry out an analysis of these new listed substances and decide on their final classification as priority substances or as priority dangerous substances no later than 12 months after the entry into force of this directive. our compromise is about new emission control measures. we insist on control of emissions. while the commission does indeed invoke the existence of other legislation on chemical pollutants, such as reach, ippc, or the pesticides directives, we ask that the commission carry out a full assessment of the consistency and effectiveness of all existing legislation which may affect water quality and, if necessary, adapt or propose new legislation. in conclusion, i would like to thank the commission member of the commission. mr president, it is a pleasure for me to come before parliament to exchange views on the report by mrs pleguezuelos aguilar, launched by the committee on regional development. i am told by my colleague, commissioner hübner, who apologises for not being able to be here today, that, as in the case of the previous reports, it shows again how excellent and efficient our collaboration is. i fully share the view that cohesion policy is essential to reducing internal eu disparities on the one hand and closing the gap between the european regions and the world-leading economies on the other. this is so because cohesion policy is based on a modern paradigm of sustainable development which may be best described as a conditional grant. in order to benefit from the policy, member states are required to draw up a medium-term strategy for the use of the resources, to cofinance european aid from national budgets, to work in partnership at national, regional and local level and to respect eu laws and policies. these conditions have resulted in the development of an efficient management system shared between european, national, regional and local levels – a system of multi-level governance. on top of this, as the report correctly points out, cohesion policy makes a substantial contribution to the increase of commercial flows within the internal market and, as a result, has spill-over effects outside the regions and countries in which the policy is implemented. we all have to admit, however, that the impact of our policy has probably not been sufficiently measured, explained or appreciated. clearly, cohesion should be assessed on the basis of multiple dimensions and should not be limited only to gdp since, in the short- and medium-term, this fails to reflect many important aspects of the impact of european cohesion policy. therefore, the fourth cohesion report will carry out a thorough analysis of economic, social and territorial cohesion in the european union with the help of a wide range of indicators. certainly, one of the keys to its success lies in the fact that cohesion policy is an integrated, fully-fledged policy. it is not a bundle of sectoral approaches, but a policy that integrates different policies in the overriding context of development strategy. that is why it can deliver specific tailor-made solutions for each european region or territory. at the same time, it is a new policy that critically depends on coordination and synergies with other eu and national policies. this brings me to the link between the strategy for growth and jobs, and cohesion policy. as early as this year, each member state will set out how cohesion policy contributes to the implementation of the national reform programme. equally, the commission will, in its annual progress report to the spring european council, summarise the progress towards achieving the union’s priorities of promoting competitiveness and creating jobs, including meeting the objectives of the integrated guidelines for growth and jobs for 2005-2008. we have also introduced an earmarking approach which assures that the predominant share of policy resources is invested in key lisbon drivers. as you know, the programming phase has not yet been finalised. however, according to the available data, we can already state that the reinforcement of the strategic approach of cohesion policy and its concentration on the growth in jobs agenda has been a success. in fact, around eur 200 billion will be invested in lisbon priorities between 2007 and 2013. if we add to this cofinancing and private resources leveraged by cohesion policy intervention, we may well see this figure double, and we need to compare this to eur 150 billion in 2000 to 2006. in addition, in the new 2007-2013 period, we have reinforced the coordination mechanisms inside the commission, both in the context of the programming documents and in day-to-day operation. in a way, the preparation for the 2007-2013 programming period became a meeting point between different eu priorities. take, for instance, research and development and innovation. at eu level, new synergies have been established between cohesion policy, the seventh research and development framework programme and the competitiveness and innovation programme. the last two programmes will take more account of the specificities of the regions that are lagging behind. cohesion policy, on the other hand, will significantly increase its contribution to the financing of r&d and innovation activities. the departments within the directorate-general for regional policy, in cooperation with those of mr potočnik, are working on a communication to provide information and advice on how to combine the resources of cohesion and rdt policy in order to increase their respective effectiveness, which is to be adopted in july.

madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to make four points. first of all, commissioner, i think you were right to insist that the strategy of a globalised europe must not mean giving priority to multilateral negotiations. there is a lot of enthusiasm, but also a lot of illusions, about what bilateral free trade agreements can bring. we are told that we must do so because others have taken this path, for example the united states. in fact, the united states has only signed six or seven free trade agreements, which account for barely 5% of its foreign trade. the other agreements have failed because they pose the same problems as in the multilateral framework, with, in general, the same type of partners. i would add that these negotiations often lead to agreements which are more unbalanced in relation to developing countries, to the advantage, of course, of the developed countries. this brings me to my second point: when we move from the multilateral to the bilateral framework, we must not abandon the development objectives of trade policy in the process. from this point of view, mr caspary, i think it is impossible to say that trade policy is not linked to other dimensions: development, the fight against poverty, the environment and social policy. the link between trade and development, trade and poverty reduction, is not automatic. for example, it is said that if africa does not trade, it will remain poor. which is true. but does that mean that any trade agreement with africa is necessarily good for africa? no, that's not true. a more differentiated and controlled approach, which takes account of the fragile sectors in a number of countries, must be considered. and this is not just the case for the poorest countries, it's also the case for emerging countries, countries like india, which are among the poorest in the world. thirdly, this strategy of a globalised europe should not mean the reintroduction of subjects which have been excluded from the multilateral framework. i am thinking of the singapore issues, the investment negotiations, public procurement, public services. the reintroduction of these subjects is not justified, it will lead to the same problems, the same blockages, or else these subjects will be imposed by force, which go beyond the rules of trade and concern the internal regulation of sensitive sectors, such as access to essential services, to public services. fourthly - and i will conclude on this point - i believe, as mr junker does, that we must not lose sight of the fact that the union, also through its trade policy, is pursuing the implementation of social and environmental rules. we do this through the strengthened system of generalized preferences, we no longer do this in free trade agreements, and i regret that because we also have to promote compliance with, among other things, the ilo rules.

mr president, commissioner, the european union is now making ambitious commitments to development. i welcome this because there is an urgent, urgent need to help developing countries to reduce poverty, to achieve the millennium development goals and to enjoy sustainable economic growth. let us hope that these objectives will be translated into concrete and effective action. as such, the commitments to increase aid to trade are welcome. i would like to highlight a few points which justify the essential nature of this instrument. it is first of all a response to the need for coherence, which must guide the european union's external action: by articulating the different areas of its external action, the european union is responding to two principles, namely better legislation and more effective aid. it also responds to the reality of the multilateral trading system by helping developing and least developed countries to reap the benefits of market access. finally, it contributes to the implementation of trade agreements. these include wto agreements and economic partnership agreements. aid for trade thus helps to make international trade a tool for poverty reduction through economic development. finally, to be effective, trade assistance must meet several requirements: it must be accompanied by concrete commitments, including technical assistance, be subject to control and monitoring of its implementation, and strengthen local ownership and management oriented towards results. this is essential if trade assistance is to enable developing countries to benefit from the benefits of the multilateral trading system and to enable them to effectively increase their trade capacity. we therefore call on all the parties concerned to continue their efforts so that aid to trade can live up to its promises.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, my report on organic production and labelling of organic products will finally be put to the vote today, after first being referred to committee and then to the council for urgent procedure, which was unanimously rejected by parliament last month. unfortunately, the new discussions with the council during these two months have not allowed any further progress to be made on important points. in particular, neither the commission nor the council accept the double legal basis which we have been calling for. the council did not reverse its decision to authorise, by exceptional derogation, additives and veterinary treatments derived from gmos. similarly, certain chemicals could also be authorised by way of derogation. in the absence of codecision, we are forced to take note of it. we regret, however, the council's closed and casual attitude in recent weeks, despite the goodwill of some member states. i also deeply regret that the majority of the groups yesterday refused to postpone the vote to june, since the council itself had postponed its meeting on organic farming. i regret that the majority of the groups did not want to use our means of pressure to the full. that said, the council nevertheless took up many of our amendments in its compromise and regular consultation of all the parties concerned is part of the overall agreement. i therefore ask you to adopt this report. you can count on my determination, and that of my colleagues on the committee on agriculture and rural development, to follow this matter closely in the months ahead. in writing. the extension of the daphne programme for 2007-13 shows the european parliament's desire to continue the plan, which was set up in 2000. violence against children, adolescents and women is a dramatic social phenomenon. certain groups particularly vulnerable to violence need to be better protected, not to mention domestic violence and female genital mutilation. in réunion, for example, crimes against women have doubled in 20 years, and more than one in five women has suffered at least one form of violence in a public space in the past 12 months. i therefore hope that the european commission will dedicate a european year to this type of violence. i welcome the commitment of the commission, which has increased the budget to almost €117 million, even though this is less than the amount requested by the european parliament. the doubling of resources nevertheless shows a certain ambition in the objectives. this effort must also be accompanied by transparency of the programme and facilitate access for civil society, which lacks technical assistance for the preparation of project proposals, especially in the ors. i hope that in future discussions will be led by a panel of experts.
in writing. we abstained on the reports by mr corbett and mr leinen on enhanced cooperation between committees and the practical arrangements for codecision. the report is a very good report, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support it. but they are symptomatic of a parliamentary practice where, in the end, almost everything is decided in advance, in small committees, by interinstitutional or intergroup compromise, in the name of efficiency and rationality. they are also symptomatic of an assembly where the "big" groups, at least those recognised as such, are the rain and the shine and where individual rights of members are reduced to their most basic expression, or even non-existent when it comes to legislating. by policing its own functioning, this parliament, which is already suffering from its lack of national and political representativeness and its lack of closeness to the citizens, will permanently lose the nature that it should have: that of an assembly elected by and for the people.
in writing. i voted in favour of referring the aubert report on organic production and labelling to the committee on agriculture. in my view, it is necessary that the threshold for accidental contamination with gmos should not be the same as that for conventional agriculture, i.e. in the order of 0.9%, because in that case it would be de facto accepted that contamination can no longer be prevented or that a product, even if certified as organic, cannot be guaranteed to be free of gmos. in this respect, i supported the proposal from the european socialists that the presence of gmos in organic products should be limited exclusively to unforeseeable and technically unavoidable volumes up to a maximum value of 0.1% and that the term 'organic' should not be used to designate products with an accidental contamination of gmos above the detectable threshold of 0.1%. finally, i support the request for a change of legal basis on the issue of organic farming. the european parliament, as a consultant, intends to become a co-decision-maker on this issue, which is a step forward in this field.
in writing. organic production now accounts for 1.4% of the number of farms in the 25 member states and 3.6% of the utilised agricultural area (1.8% of the agricultural land in brittany). consumer demand continues to increase and the arrival on the market of these products with various labels, even those manufactured outside the eu, poses new problems in terms of control, certification and labelling. in addition, the subsidies or standards in this area vary widely from one country to another, which creates distortions of competition for the least assisted organic producers. i therefore welcome the adoption by the plenary of the european parliament's opinion to the council for the rapid adoption of the regulation on organic farming. the new regulation is intended to clarify the community framework for organic food production which dates from 1991. parliament called for national inspection systems to be strengthened to allow traceability of products at all stages of production. while the use of the european logo (for food containing 95% organic ingredients) and the mention 'eu-organic' is mandatory, the addition of other private logos should remain possible. finally, the use of gmos in organic production must be banned.
in writing. this report commits the european union and its trading partners to a conquering liberalism, against the background of the foundations of european trade policy. i regret that the meps are abandoning what they have advocated up to now: a trade policy which consisted of making trade agreements subject to social and environmental requirements while respecting the sovereignty of developing countries in the management of a number of sectors vital to their development (public services, investments, public procurement and competition rules). this vote replaced this policy with a strategy of broad liberalization of services and investment in developing countries, which will meet the expectations of european industrialists at the expense of economic needs for development. the principle of free trade must be a tool for development and not an end in itself. i regret that the singapore issues, which were excluded from the doha multilateral negotiations, have been reintroduced by meps in this report as priorities in future bilateral negotiations.

mr president, madam commissioner, mr minister, i think we can only welcome today the reduction in international roaming charges. however, we must avoid shortcuts and, please, let us not systematically and fruitlessly oppose the industrialists and consumers, because a rush to keep lowering the price ceilings is not only beneficial, far from it. in fact, with roaming charges that are too low, the longer term. this will create a competitive market with the widest possible variety of prices, allowing consumers to make an informed choice. under the terms of the compromise, customers will also have a period of three months after the entry into force of the regulation to choose whether or not to benefit from the eurotariff. if they do not indicate any preference, they will automatically be allocated the fare which is most favourable to them. the subscriber therefore has the option of not being charged the eurotariff if he has already benefited from favourable conditions offered by the in writing. at a time when globalisation is causing turbulence and social injustice, it is necessary to highlight european strategies that emphasise the social dimension of globalisation. implementation of the decent work agenda is one of these strategies. decent work can indeed contribute to the fight against poverty and social exclusion, as it maximises the benefits of globalisation while reducing the disadvantages. while trade liberalisation must contribute to the goals of growth, full employment and poverty reduction, it must above all be based on the promotion of decent work for all. moreover, if it is to be a constant feature of the eu's external policies, the promotion of decent work must be the premise and condition of the eu's trade relations with third countries. in this context, it is appropriate to highlight a mechanism guaranteeing the promotion of decent work, namely the generalised system of preferences. the gsp+ is an indispensable lever for sustainable development, good governance and the promotion of fundamental social rights.
the rapporteur. mr president, i am simply speaking to point out to the house that there has been an erratum. the same phrase appears in three different paragraphs, and the parliament's services have rightly deleted paragraphs 47 and 53 of the report, since the phrase appears in its entirety in paragraph 51. i just wanted to inform my colleagues.
in writing. i voted in favour of the rübig report on roaming on public mobile telephone networks within the community, because the positions it takes will make it possible to considerably improve the situation of european consumers. many european citizens, especially those living in nord-pas-de-calais, travel frequently abroad for business or personal reasons, and the current rates for making and receiving calls on their mobile phones are excessive and unjustified. the rübig report corrects a situation which is hampering mobility. i therefore welcome the rates set out in this report: the per minute costs that have been adopted are quite satisfactory and well below those currently applied. we would have preferred even lower fares, however, which could have provided a better incentive for mobility in europe. in addition to the substantially reduced rates, the requirement of transparency is an important principle. the ep also called for more transparency on the cost of calls and for european citizens to be able to know what a call to or from abroad will cost them.
in writing. there are moments, extremely rare in this house, when members are called upon to vote on a text that is really useful for european citizens and where, for once, europe brings a real added value. this was the case a few years ago for crossborder transfers within the euro area: a european regulation required that their cost be identical to that of a national transfer. this was only logical and normal, since the single currency had just been introduced. this is the case today with the regulation on the cost of roaming in the field of mobile telephony. the text, which is not perfect, as all compromises are, will, however, make it possible to control the prohibitive tariffs charged by operators on international communications within the community. and the review clause, due in 18 months' time, will hopefully be an opportunity to go further in consumer protection.
in writing. as the report itself points out, the 1992 excise duty directive did not bring about any approximation of excise duty rates between member states, nor did it even address the alleged problems of distortion of competition. in line with its programme for better regulation, the commission, if it is consistent, should itself call for the repeal of this text. the truth is that it is up to the states, and the states alone, to set the tax, whether direct or indirect, on their territory, according to their budgetary, economic and social imperatives. and the tax harmonization sought by the commission is in fact only an ideological goal. i would like to conclude by saying that it is not a small paradox that those who campaign for the abolition of border controls, the free movement of people, goods and services and free competition are the first to complain when this abolition and freedom of movement encourages citizens to play the game.
in writing. i voted in favour of the vergnaud report. the vote on this report in plenary clearly confirmed the specific nature of health services and therefore their exclusion from the services directive. this vote avoided any challenge to equal access to care and the financial sustainability of social security systems. in my view, the debate on health services at community level must now focus on the legal uncertainties arising from the case law of the court of justice of the european union and on the areas in which the european union can create added value. in my view, a directive on health services, in line with the objective of a framework directive on services of general economic interest, remains the only tool which would enable the european union to bring its added value and restore the confidence of european citizens in an area which is the very essence of their lives.
in writing. health services are not services like other services. they should therefore not be subject to european rules on competition, state aid, public procurement or the internal market. in particular, their organisation and financing must be the sole responsibility of the member states. despite the foreseeable rejection of the paragraph calling for these services to be subject to the so-called bolkestein directive, the text of the report still seems dangerous to us. it proposed that the mobility of health workers be encouraged, as this could create shortages of health workers and thus of care for all citizens in some countries. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the new guidelines and will continue to monitor the implementation of the new guidelines. the objective of access for all european citizens to quality and local care cannot be achieved by a european directive based on the case law of the european court of justice adjudicating on a few crossborder litigation cases. and, to be honest, this can only be achieved if it is guaranteed that brussels will never be able to legislate in this area.
in writing. this report is an attempt to circumvent the content of the services directive which had legitimately excluded health services from its scope. health care is not a commodity but a vital service for our ageing populations. health must be free from the greed of ultra-liberal predators and the european federalist ideology which will harmonize everything from the bottom up. the question of exclusion of health services is and must remain a matter for the member states. it is also worrying that we are still referring to this smoking lisbon strategy as a necessary step, when we have known for a long time that it is a symbol of europeanist inefficiency. moreover, in view of the differences between our countries, it can be said that the universality of a so-called european social model is a utopia. finally, the creation of a legal framework in this area is tantamount to the establishment of a quasi-internal market in health services or at least to laying the foundations for it. our duty is to prevent the quality of health services from being compromised, to preserve medical ethics, to ensure strict controls on authorization and reimbursement of care at the level of nations and their ministries.
in writing. we all agree on the objectives of finally lifting the world of the south out of poverty, even if the real steps have not yet been taken for black africa. that is, the sharing of water, food, basic medicines and education. international trade as a tool to combat poverty is necessary but not sufficient. in the long run, maybe. but as keynes told us, "in the long run we are all dead". so we need to accelerate and innovate. in particular, by the invention of a new customs technology of deductible customs duties in the form of a customs credit offered by the importer to the exporter, to be used as a purchase on the economy of the importing country and equal to the amount of customs duty borne. for the countries of the south, this customs credit would be enhanced, like the matching credit or sparing credit already existing in international taxation. this would prevent the poor countries from losing the valuable revenue from their customs duties.
in writing. the negotiation of the economic partnership agreements enters a crucial phase on 1 january 2008, marking the expiry of the current agreements. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i would stress the development dimension: these agreements cannot be reduced to simple free trade agreements in the sense of the wto and must be instruments for economic and human development. the epas will therefore be as asymmetrical and progressive as possible. i voted in favour of amendments nos 20 and 28 on the need to take into account the specific features of the overseas regions and territories in the negotiations under article 299 (2) of the tec. the specific interests of these territories should be examined, differentiations in market access should be considered and the existing arrangements for support should be better coordinated with those of the acp countries. i would also like to clarify paragraph 13 of the report by recalling the conclusions adopted by the council which provide for transitional periods in the offer of access to the eu market for certain products of particular sensitivity to the eu.
in writing. in the spirit of the cotonou agreement, the epas are not just free trade agreements in the sense of the wto, but a genuine partnership to create a new economic and trade framework favourable to the acp countries. because of their geographical proximity to many acp countries, the overseas communities are at the heart of these preferential and reciprocal agreements with the acp countries. the special situation of the ors must be taken into account in the context of these negotiations, on the basis of article 299 (2) of the treaty. special attention must also be paid to the octs neighbouring the acp countries, in compliance with the association agreements which already bind them to the union, pursuant to article 299 (3) of the treaty. the specific interests of the octs and the octs should be examined, including their involvement as far in advance as possible in the negotiations, in order to consider differentiation in market access, and to coordinate their respective support arrangements in order to strengthen their integration into their regional environment. i welcome the adoption of my amendment, which seeks to strike an intelligent balance between the regional integration of these overseas territories and their links with europe.
in writing. this report by the european parliament is a step in the right direction. it makes decent work a tool of european development policy, first by co-financing with the ilo a development programme for decent work, then by creating a european label and blacklisting companies that violate basic labour standards, and finally by introducing trade sanctions against countries that seriously violate fundamental social rights. it is making progress on decent work in europe, where much remains to be done: by pushing member states to ratify ilo conventions on the safety and health of workers, maternity protection or migrant workers; by calling for the introduction of a minimum wage as a safety net to prevent exploitation of workers; by improving access to lifelong learning and by advocating better harmonisation of pension schemes. these are the foundations of the social europe that the european socialists want to build. i shall therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the promotion of decent work for all. the concept of 'decent work' seems to be a reference in terms of multilateral declarations and agreements, but policies are still far from the concept. presentations and statements are one thing; the daily actions and political decisions of international institutions are another. the world is in a "deficit" of decent work: many jobs are unproductive and of low quality, dangerous jobs with precarious incomes, rights are violated and inequality between the sexes prevails. in response to this situation, the wto and the ilo have adopted international labour standards. but the imf and the world bank do not support any initiative to ensure that the fundamental rights of workers are respected. for decent work to become a global reality, it must be a priority for all international institutions, which will need to work together to ensure its achievement. decent work must be a universal goal for all international institutions. it is imperative that the achievement of its fundamentals - quality employment, workers' rights, protection and social dialogue - determine all economic and social policies at the global level. deputy author. madam president, mr minister, madam commissioner, the reports follow one another and are not the same, since we are now dealing with biodiversity. this week, mr minister, has been marked by the european parliament's expressed determination to combat the erosion of biological diversity. on monday we discussed the report by mr adamou and the report on life+, and today we are examining two oral questions tabled for the next meeting of the conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, or cites. our committee on the environment, whose chairman, i apologize for his absence, is wondering about the member states' negotiating methods and is asking the european council what the union's key objectives will be at the 14th meeting of the conference of the parties to the cites convention, which will take place, as you recalled, madam president, in the hague on 14 and 15 june 2007. the cites convention is one of the oldest multilateral environmental instruments. it was adopted in 1973 in washington by states which were already anxious to go beyond national regulatory frameworks. the aim was to preserve wild plants and animals from over-exploitation by commercial interests. the advantage of this convention over other multinational environmental agreements is its great adaptability. it acts directly on trade through supply, which it limits. in concrete terms, it affects about 500 000 transactions - that is not insignificant, 500 000 commercial transactions! - and thus limits the overexploitation of biological diversity. through the accession of the various institutional partners, almost 170 states, including our 27 member states, scientists and ngos, the cites convention has helped to avoid the removal of particularly endangered species and to save species such as the siberian tiger, the blue whale and the african elephant. of course, the challenges facing the convention are many. on the one hand, they are structural. the convention is struggling to find funding to match its ambitions. it must respond to the overconsumption of natural species, some of which are still not listed. on the other hand, the convention must take account of new data, including, of course, climate change. it must take into account the ineffectiveness of certain instruments, such as the action plan on forestry enforcement, governance and trade, or more simply flegt, which everyone here knows. it must also review decisions that have had a negative impact on certain species: for example, at the 12th conference of the parties, authorisations for the sale of ivory from botswana, namibia and south africa resulted in the estimated loss of nearly 20 000 elephants. in the fight against the degradation of species, the european union must speak with one voice at all costs in the conferences of the parties to the convention. in this connection, i would like to remind you, mr minister, that the european union often abstains when decisions are taken because our member states cannot agree, which means that we lose 27 votes, and 27 votes is not a small number, and it is often a lot. so, mr minister, we ask the council to take account of the european parliament's resolution, which reflects the interests of the european citizens, which expresses what our citizens want you to defend in the framework of this cites convention. firstly, because the resolution calls for certain requirements to be met by the negotiators. the precautionary principle must therefore be applied with the same rigour as that imposed by the european union in other international environmental negotiations. the union must also demand transparency in voting and reject the secret ballot, which is a real practice, particularly in the case of the listing of species. in fact, it is a question of modernising this somewhat outdated procedure, which no longer meets the requirements of the citizens, who must be able to exercise their right of access to the decisions taken on their behalf. we know that ngos are constantly accusing the member states of the european union of not disclosing their votes and of voting by secret ballot in respect of certain species. we find this absolutely unacceptable and we ask for transparency, because this convention is special and the member states, as we know, have special interests in certain matters. the issues on the agenda of the conference shall be submitted to the european parliament. we don't understand why it's any different. every time a conference of the parties to the cites convention is announced, we ask the same questions to the council: we do not understand why we are not consulted in advance to find out what positions the council intends to defend at the conference. i would also ask the commission and the council to involve our parliament delegation in the work of the conferences so that we are not forced, as usual, to haunt the corridors in the hope of gathering information, and again, when the council and the commission are willing to invite us! so thank you for including the european parliament delegation in the the president of the council. the agreement between the european community and the russian federation on the facilitation of the issuance of visas is to enter into force on 1 june 2007. we also had a debate on this a few weeks ago in the european parliament. the purpose of this agreement is to facilitate the issuing of visas for intended stays of no more than 90 days to citizens of the russian federation travelling to the member states of the eu and to citizens of the european union travelling to the russian federation. according to this agreement, a national of the russian federation is a person who holds the citizenship of the russian federation or has acquired it in accordance with the domestic russian regulations. this means that this agreement applies to all russian citizens, regardless of the country in which they reside, according to the current legal situation. no initiative has been taken to give the commission a mandate to open negotiations on a similar agreement with georgia. the eu-georgia action plan and the european neighbourhood policy already provide for the establishment of a dialogue on passenger traffic, in particular on readmission and visa issues.

released into the public domain 70 years after the death of their author and 50 years after the first dissemination of a work by its performers. claire gibault has been thinking about this idea. it mr president, we have talked a lot about whisky and vodka. i'll tell you about the rum. within the european union, it is only produced in the french overseas departments and madeira. it is a drink that is heavily consumed throughout europe; it is therefore imported from many third countries, primarily the acp countries, which enjoy special treatment under the cotonou agreement of 2000. rum is one of the main export products of the overseas departments. the sugar cane and rum sector alone accounts for more than 40% of the value of exports and 40 000 jobs in guadeloupe, martinique and réunion. the issues involved in the community definition of rum are therefore very important. the aim of the proposal is to obtain a definition for dom rum which would enable it to be better distinguished from its competitors in third countries, in particular by the mention of agricultural rum produced exclusively from sugar cane juice, a quality mark recognised by consumers. for the acp, it is also important that this definition is consistent with the union's overall approach to their rum industry to support their growth and not jeopardise the progress made so far by producers in the caribbean region. it was in this context that the professional organisations representing producers in the french overseas departments and the caribbean countries agreed, in october 2006, in barbados, to a common position on the community definition of rum, starting from a generic definition and gradually specifying it between traditional rum, agricultural rum and confectionery rum. i would like to thank horst schnellhardt who listened to my request for an adequate definition of agricultural rum and who finally decided to take up in his report this definition already contained in the council's compromise text. the production of agricultural rum has been able to be enhanced thanks to the considerable work of the whole sector over the long term and this denomination is today one of the main guarantors of the commercial opportunities for this product in the french overseas departments. this is why we can hope for the adoption of this compromise at first reading, which is now before the house for approval.

in writing. the changing world of work, the fragility of certain sectors such as industry, the explosion of the service sector and the increased mobility of the workforce are all phenomena that require the european parliament to work towards greater protection for workers. as early as december, mrs bachelot's report created a european globalisation adjustment fund, and it is in the same spirit of taking into account the rights of workers that the directive on the protection of employees in the event of the insolvency of the employer was introduced. each year thousands of employees lose their income, sometimes for months, because their company goes bankrupt, creating so many distressing situations. this directive will codify all the rules relating to the protection of employees in the event of the insolvency of the employer and will apply to all employment relationships, whatever the type of contract. the completion of the internal market, which is sometimes wrongly accused of increasing insecurity in the labour market, can, on the contrary, be the source of genuine legislation and the creation of a system of protection for employed workers. and this report, which i support, is proof of that.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to improve the applicability, legibility and clarity of labelling of spirit drinks. the spirits will thus be in conformity with the new technical requirements, in particular with the rules and standards of the wto. the aim is to enable european spirits producers to preserve their geographical indications of origin on the world market. the definition of 'agricultural rum' was retained in the negotiations. producers and consumers approved the compromise reached, particularly as regards quality criteria. in the french overseas departments, the definition of 'agricultural rum' distinguishes it from its competitors in third countries. produced exclusively from sugar cane juice, the name 'agricultural rum' is a guarantee of quality recognised by consumers. the solution found on the question of vodka also preserves the name 'traditional vodka' produced from cereals, potatoes or molasses without prohibiting production from other agricultural products. in the latter case, the labelling must bear the words 'vodka produced with ...'.
in writing. i regret that the hökmark report did not take up the many suggestions of the committee on regional development, for which i was rapporteur. it thus puts to the side the initial concern of the european commission that 'despite the general increase in broadband connectivity, access to remote and rural areas is limited due to the high cost of low population density and remoteness' and hence the search for solutions. we must recognise that in some eu territories - remote and rural areas and new member states - there is a market failure which justifies intervention by the public authorities and in particular by local and regional authorities through the structural funds. i have already experienced this in the limousin with the dorsal project. i am therefore pleased that the two socialist amendments have been adopted, which restore the reality on the ground, because it is in these remote areas that icts are most needed and useful, as they make it possible to overcome distances by facilitating relations between users and services - customers and suppliers - administrations and public institutions, and to reduce the costs and time of service provision.
in writing. i voted in favour of the hörkmark report on the development of a european broadband policy, as it is very important to encourage initiatives that promote access to the internet for all, and to knowledge in general. in line with the lisbon objectives, it is essential to develop information technologies, including broadband. although access to new technologies in the most remote regions is an objective to which the european union must devote itself, it is also necessary to take account of the persistent gaps in new technologies within the same region. there are still many villages that are too far from urban centres and still do not have access to the internet or have access but too slow and do not allow satisfactory connections, while the whole region to which they belong is generally well served. in the interests of cohesion, these infraregional disparities should also be better taken into account in order to combat the digital divide.
in writing. the dynamism of regional economies depends heavily on the level of development of information and communication technologies, including access to high-speed internet via broadband connections. the union must undoubtedly play a major role in promoting, among its member states and regions, the fight against the 'digital divide', in order to reduce the gap between individuals, businesses and territories in terms of access to the knowledge society. public aid, delivered through public-private partnerships, must be targeted primarily at underserved areas. wireless, mobile and satellite communications can bring broadband to areas traditionally excluded from fixed networks, thus offering interesting and inexpensive solutions for people living in remote or hard-to-reach areas such as island, mountainous and, of course, ultraperipheral regions (upe). in the ors, these technologies are even more useful than elsewhere, since they make it possible to overcome distances and reduce costs and time by facilitating the relations of users with their service providers, customers with their suppliers, or even administrators with their public authorities.

vice-president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i thank mr roure for his speech and for his report. the political agreement reached in the council last april, after five years of discussion, was certainly very important. this agreement, although on a version of the framework decision which is less ambitious than the commission's original proposal, has in fact made it possible to establish precisely that, once the framework decision has entered into force and has been transposed in each member state, there will be no free port in europe for those who incite racial hatred, racism and xenophobia. this is a political achievement. i am aware that the text of the framework decision contains penal provisions which could have been more stringent. i would have liked to see stricter rules. however, as the rapporteur has just said, we had to accept an agreement because, as it was a framework decision, the principle of unanimity required us to lower the level of ambition a little. nevertheless, for the first time we have a common rule, which requires that behaviour which incites hatred and discrimination on grounds of race, colour and religion be punished by criminal sanctions in all member states. think how important it is to punish behaviour that incites anti-semitic hatred or islamophobia, at a time when we are talking about the integration of non-eu immigrant communities. a major theme has certainly been the balance between the criminal punishment of such behaviour, which is not free expression of thought but concrete incitement to commit violent acts and as such must be punished, and the due respect for freedom of expression. we have worked a lot on this and i think the final result is satisfactory. we do not want to punish ideas with this measure, but rather behaviour which incites other people to commit criminal acts, to hit, to injure, to kill and to commit acts of outright violence. freedom of thought has absolutely nothing to do with it. we do not punish the idea, but those who, on the basis of a wrong but legitimate idea, go beyond the idea to behaviour, incite someone else to strike and commit criminal acts. this is the line between freedom of thought, which must be safeguarded, and the actual incitement to violence. that's why i think this decision is important. that is why we have established the principle - which is also stressed in mr roure's report - that racist motivation is an aggravating factor in all crimes. if a crime of ordinary physical violence is committed for racist reasons, it must be punished more severely, since not only incitement as such, but also racist motivation, makes a given crime more serious than the basic case. this is an important principle and i believe that the fact that 27 member states have unanimously accepted it makes the european union a little stronger in protecting this fundamental value enshrined in the charter of fundamental rights.
