madam president, at this late hour a lot has been said, but i would of course like to congratulate mrs elena valenciano on this report. it marks an important step towards making european development policy more transparent and effective in terms of human rights. i would also like to take this opportunity to call on the council and commission representatives to improve interinstitutional cooperation. it is essential to establish a dialogue between the council, the commission and parliament in order to coordinate human rights activities better and to prevent contradictions and duplication from parasitizing the message to the outside world. unfortunately, this is a constantly updated issue. if we take a concrete example, that of burma, our policy on that country is illegible to the outside world. the members of the union have committed themselves to a common position in favour of national reconciliation, democracy and human rights, but in practice the european states are divided, which results in a weak and ineffective position which has no effect on the burmese regime. politically, the european union has no clear strategy. we are only focusing on humanitarian aid, which is essential, of course, but not enough. we have taken no position on how the un security council should deal with the situation in burma, offering no support for a resolution. in addition, the commission has reduced the volume of its grants for projects promoting human rights and democracy in burma. in short, the european union has not been able to use its influence in a positive and effective way to promote and support democracy and human rights in that country. the recent failure of our appeal for the release of the burmese nobel prize winner aung san suu kyi is proof of this. and yet, parliament awarded him the sakharov prize in 1990. this example illustrates perfectly the fact that our three institutions must work together to present a coherent and legible policy for the defence of human rights.
on behalf of the its group. madam president, commissioner, the reports by our two colleagues, including that by mrs carmen fraga, deal with the insoluble problem of fisheries, because the fishery resources are limited and the demand is constantly increasing. therefore, fisheries policy is not the cap. in the cap, since 1968 and sicco mansholt, the commission has been pursuing for 40 years a strategic error, which is a crime against humanity: the community needs cereals and milk and there is a shortage of these, as the price increases prove. in fisheries policy it is different. the commission's mistakes are merely its usual technocratic sin, not its strategic crime. the management of the resource with tacs, quotas, fifg, pops has failed. the commission has legislated on everything: nets, tonnage, fleet power, number of units and finally - as the rapporteur tells us - there are fewer fishermen, there is less cod, there is even less bluefin tuna in the mediterranean, hence the anger of fishermen in the months of june and july. in my own country, for example, in the port of sète or grau-du-roi, the tuna fishermen, who fish with traditional small-net fishing, a coastal fishing, were protesting against being able to fish from july onwards. however, despite all these checks, all these demolitions, all these sanctions - perhaps one day we will even put an electronic bracelet on the fisherman to monitor him - the stocks are in danger, the rapporteur tells us. the common fisheries policy has not worked and why? because the problem is global: china, indonesia, the philippines, peru are fishing. as with wine, which we pluck when the world is planting, we break the boats when the united states increases them or russia, iceland, norway increase the power of their boats. we can invent indicators, a kind of maximum sustainable yield, but if the neighbour fishes more, then fishing less does not improve the state of the stocks. and since livestock farming, i.e. aquaculture, is also not a real solution because of the fish meal, fisheries is the perfect example of how the community level is both too high when fishing is coastal and that the decision must be local, or too low when fishing is offshore. in that case, either we'll go global very quickly with the help of scientists, or by the end of the 21st century, we'll go to the movies and fish for the last of the nemo's.
the rapporteur. madam commissioner, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, first of all i would like to thank mrs kuneva for the quality of our exchanges. why this green paper and this report from our parliament? three factors justify this exercise to bring the european regulatory framework for consumer protection into line and modernise it, namely eight directives adopted between 1985 and 1999. firstly, the rapid development of new marketing techniques, in particular electronic commerce, has made european legislation partly obsolete. secondly, there are many inconsistencies in the current acquis, which contains different legal definitions for identical concepts. thirdly, the choice made in the past to opt for minimum harmonisation allowing member states to retain specific national provisions has maintained a fragmentation of the legal environment, so that the existing rules set a minimum european threshold but do not define a single rule of the game. the result, according to the september 2006 eurobarometer, is that 50% of citizens are more wary of cross-border purchases and 71% think it will be more difficult to assert their rights when buying from a professional based in another member state. similarly, economic operators have an interest in a secure regulatory environment and in taking full advantage of an internal market of almost 500 million consumers. one of the challenges of this revision is to take a qualitative step forward, in a sense laying the foundations for a european consumer code. what method? the european parliament fully endorses the methodology proposed by the commission, namely a mixed or combined approach, which is based on the definition of a horizontal instrument of maximum harmonisation incorporating the same legal concepts in common factor across the current directives and which, on the other hand, provides for the revision, if necessary, of some of the sectoral directives which will remain of minimum harmonisation. the horizontal instrument must be designed to bring together the basic rights of the european consumer. first, it will contain a single definition of the consumer. parliament proposes that this should be any natural person acting for purposes outside his professional activity, whereas a professional will be defined as any natural or legal person acting in the course of his professional activity. why such a restrictive definition of consumer, you ask? well, for the sake of it. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the consumer is protected in the community. secondly, the horizontal instrument will guarantee the right of withdrawal granted to consumers in the event of an online or home purchase. the rules for calculating the withdrawal period will be harmonised, since the withdrawal period is currently a minimum of seven days for distance purchases, for example, but in some countries, such as germany and finland, a 14-day period has been granted. the procedures for exercising this right will also be harmonised. thirdly, the horizontal instrument will clarify what is meant by 'abusive clauses' in business-consumer contracts. there will be a blacklist of clauses which are still prohibited, a grey list of clauses which are alleged to be abusive, and a list of other clauses which the consumer can prove to be abusive through the courts. fourth, the duration of the two-year legal guarantee will be extended by the period of the property being immobilized for repair. fifthly, the right to compensation will be reaffirmed and its modalities specified, and above all, the horizontal instrument will be scalable. specific legal questions will continue to be dealt with in so-called sectoral directives and will remain mostly of minimum harmonisation, with a mutual recognition clause, we believe, the mechanism of which will have to be defined and which should make it possible to arbitrate any conflicts of laws. finally, my report stresses that without information and without the possibility of exercising these remedies, consumers have only virtual rights. the effective enforcement of their rights requires national and european information campaigns, a strengthening of the visibility and role of european consumer centres and the facilitation of judicial and extrajudicial redress. finally, parliament recalls the debate on group actions. as rapporteur, i believe that class action, as a specific means of resolving mass litigation, is an important avenue to explore. i call on the commission to present specific legal studies and proposals in the coming months, but i am making it clear that european class actions will be different from american class actions, whose very proactive philosophy of aggressive consumer approach by unscrupulous lawyers and the modalities which include punitive damages to be paid by operators, do not correspond at all to the legal culture of european countries. on the contrary, i believe that a european procedure should enable associations to act on behalf of all victims of similar injuries caused by the same unethical professional, so that they can obtain, in a single case and without express protest on their part, the compensation due to them. in conclusion, i would say that this green paper sets ambitious objectives and i personally hope that the vote in this parliament will clearly set the course for a consumer europe.
madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i applaud this initiative for a green paper on the revision of the acquis. i believe that if we want our citizens to see the internal market not just as a threat, we need serious consumer protection, especially as the internal market applies to complex products. of course, i am thinking about this in relation to the question of financial markets. the news shows us every day, if need be, how much of a challenge consumer protection is in this area. in this context, i would like to return to the remarks made yesterday by commissioner mccreevy, who was able to give the impression that the real estate market in the united states is in this state because mortgage borrowers are not financially educated. financial education is important, but it must not be a substitute for genuine consumer protection, which is introduced in all our legislation. this requires horizontal legislation but also sectoral legislation. let us not substitute education for consumer protection and the responsibility of traders when offering products for free circulation in the internal market. my second point concerns group actions. i think our rapporteur for the committee on economic and monetary affairs, mr sánchez presedo, will say something about that, but i think we must make progress in this area too. no one in europe has ever imagined that we would not want to import the american model, but there is a margin between the situation that exists today in the internal market of the european union and the american situation and i trust you, commissioner, to do so with european intelligence. is it normal today that we have no knowledge, no transparency of the complaints that are lodged, the fines that are fixed? let us have a transparent, open debate on the reality of what these group actions cover and let us provide european consumers with this useful tool! one last word, madam president, with your permission. the clear definitions of consumer and trader proposed in the report are important, but we must be careful not to introduce confusion: in the field of financial services, for example, the idea that certain products can be reserved for professionals is an illusion that reduces the guarantees offered to consumers. these products eventually circulate and are offered to all consumers. so let us have that definition, but let us not make it the alpha and omega of consumer protection!

in writing. i voted in favour of the very good report by my excellent czech colleague, miroslav ouzky, on the international health regulations (ihr) as revised in 2005 by the general assembly of the world health organisation (who). the purpose of this regulation is to prevent the spread of diseases and to ensure that citizens are protected against these diseases without, however, creating unnecessary and costly barriers to international trade. it is urgent that this international health system be implemented in a coordinated manner within the european community, because infectious diseases, as my excellent french colleague, françoise grossetête, has pointed out, are a threat and a challenge for all countries. these health issues will again raise the question of the quality of surveillance of our external borders for both people and goods. it is imperative to support the development of the european centre for disease prevention and control (ecdc) established in 2004 and the european public health early warning and response system, which should strengthen the rapid and consistent application of the international health regulations (ihr) in the member states of the union.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report. twenty years ago, infectious diseases were not seen as a major threat. today they are a threat and a challenge to all countries. health threats such as pandemic influenza, malaria and tuberculosis are being posed by mutating viruses, increasing resistance to antibiotics and weak health systems new health risks also include foodborne diseases, accidents or chemical, biological or nuclear attacks, industrial pollution and climate change. these threats could endanger millions of people in several countries. the increase in globalisation, the multiplication of international flows and trade are also aggravating factors. international collaboration in the field of infectious disease control is therefore of paramount importance. it is therefore essential to remove all unnecessary barriers to international traffic and trade. this report is an additional incentive for member states to develop more and more joint actions based on the exchange of good practice. the establishment of appropriate alert systems in the event of a serious pandemic in neighbouring and third countries is also necessary.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution proposed by various political groups, including the european people's party (christian democrats) - european democrats (epp-ed) on the objectives of the european union in the run-up to the 8th meeting of the conference of the parties to the united nations convention to combat desertification, to be held in madrid from 3 to 14 september 2007. the current global warming is causing, among other things, the drying up of springs by evaporation, the reduction of river flows and the level of groundwater, and thus the destruction of the surface structure of soils. according to the united nations environment programme (unep), desertification currently affects 25 to 30 per cent of the world's land surface and 1.2 to 2 billion people are at risk in at least 100 countries. desertification is increasing on a global scale, and it is fuelling poverty, forced migration and conflict. i believe that it is urgent for the european union to embark on a european water policy, not just in terms of quality, but also in terms of quality.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report by my spanish colleague, elena vanlenciano martinez-orozco, on the functioning of human rights dialogues and consultations with third countries. human rights are one of the core values of the european union and it is very important that they are systematically at the heart of the eu's political dialogues with third countries. the council must systematically apply the human rights and democracy clause in all agreements and relations between the eu and third countries. in this respect, i support the idea of improving interinstitutional coherence and thus of establishing mechanisms to improve coordination between the different eu institutions (council, commission and parliament) by setting up an interinstitutional trilogue on political dialogue and human rights dialogues and consultation. at a time when we are experiencing a loss of values in a world which is becoming more complex, the union must impose values linked to human rights and democracy in all its projects and programmes, particularly in the field of development aid and technical, commercial and financial cooperation.
in writing. the report by elena valenciano on the functioning of human rights dialogues and consultations with third countries has just been adopted by a large majority and i congratulate the rapporteur on the thoroughness of her work. the report usefully recalls that the question of human rights must be addressed in the context of a comprehensive political dialogue with third countries. the promotion of human rights is an integral part of the european union's foreign and development policy. it also has the merit of calling on the council and the commission to streamline the procedures for dialogues and consultations. better coherence and more intensive interinstitutional cooperation would give european human rights policy greater credibility on the international stage. objective evaluation and monitoring would also follow. finally, the report stresses the need for transparency in these dialogues at the level of the european executive and for a stronger role for the european parliament in these dialogues. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of adopting this report in the final vote in plenary.
in writing. i voted in favour of the very good own-initiative report by my spanish colleague, carmen fraga estévez, in response to the european commission's communication on the application of the principle of sustainability in the european union fisheries by means of maximum sustainable yield (msy). i share her view that the commission should recognise the failure of the current fisheries management policy and welcome its intention to create a new management model to restore resources, adapt fishing effort to the reality of fisheries and achieve greater profitability and stability of the fishing fleet. however, we must be careful and take our fishing capacity into account in the light of the needs of european and world consumption and the urgent need to be attentive to resources. in addition, any change to the union's fisheries policy will necessarily have to include adequate and financially sufficient compensation mechanisms, not to mention regulatory adaptation, which implies a study of the legal and socio-economic implications of the final proposal.
in writing. i voted in favour of the own-initiative report by my colleague béatrice patrie on the green paper on the revision of the community acquis on consumer protection, taking into account in particular the stated objective of modernising, simplifying and improving the regulatory framework for businesses and individuals, thus facilitating cross-border trade and strengthening consumer confidence. it is right to ask ourselves regularly, especially with the development of internet commerce, whether the proper functioning of the internal market offers a fair balance between a high level of consumer protection and the competitiveness of enterprises, in strict compliance with the principle of subsidiarity. this report offers interesting insights, whether on the general legislative approach, the limitation of unfair terms, the harmonization of legislation, the right of withdrawal, the sale of consumer goods or, finally, the effective application of consumer law.

member of the commission. mr president, the crackdown on peaceful protestors on the last day of august has once again spotlighted the scandal of human rights in burma, and the commission remains very worried about this situation. we believe that the military regime is a threat to the region and, most of all, to the country and the people of burma. a large part of the population of 52 million is in anguish and poverty, which is the result of bad political and economic governance. in an environment of political, social and economic insecurity, issues of human rights are sadly taking backstage, and the most recent detention of political activists is a case in point. the overriding challenge for the government – national reconciliation and economic development – is obvious. but for the international community, helping the transition of burma towards being a more open and more developed society to be led by a legitimate and civilian government must remain the paramount goal. the national convention process, which has just finished, was a very formal procedure to boost the current regime’s power. it was certainly not a genuine exercise to draft a new constitution and was far from inclusive. that is why the commission fully shares the view of the united states secretary-general ban ki-moon, who has requested the government embark on an inclusive, participatory and transparent process, with a view to allowing all the relevant parties to myanmar’s national reconciliation process to fully contribute to defining the country’s future. we also welcome the work of ibrahim gambari, as special envoy for myanmar of the united nations secretary-general. we hope that the good offices of the united nations will continue. professor gambari is due to visit myanmar shortly. we criticise, specifically, the working conditions in the country for the red cross. the government, in its own interests and out of respect for international humanitarian law, should allow the international committee of the red cross to continue its mission. at the same time, we should note a few encouraging signals. the commission hopes that the recent arrangement between the government of burma and the ilo, handling the complaints against forced labour, will help the victims. we acknowledge that the government has agreed in early august with its asean partners to the inclusion of a human rights commission in the planned asean charter, the constitutional document. what can the eu do? an effective policy should aim at bringing the country back into the international community, allowing for political, social and economic development. the eu common position reflects this need; it is a balanced document, detailing our criticisms, while engaging government over its responsibilities and offering assistance to the people. as regards engaging the regime, there is a consensus that more needs to be done, not less. isolation will only make the population pay a greater price. the commission maintains that channels of communication with the government must be kept open, notably to convey our concerns about human rights and, in this regard, the commission uses all appropriate occasions, for instance the asem meetings, and the eu asean meetings, to raise the need for an inclusive dialogue among all stakeholders. we regularly press for national reconciliation and for the liberation of political detainees. to help the people of myanmar, and specifically the most vulnerable parts of the population, the commission is increasing its assistance programmes in quantitative and in qualitative terms. a new country strategy foresees support for health and basic education, for instance the three diseases fund, which is supported by the eu and its partner, is already working well to fights aids, malaria and tuberculosis. this comes on top of our significant humanitarian aid. in particular, as foreseen in the eu common position, the european union wishes to engage the government in a critical dialogue over its responsibilities to achieve the millennium development goals, and the commission hopes that the government is prepared to step up the existing dialogue in areas of health and education, among others. unfortunately, we do not believe that additional restrictive measures will push the government in the desired direction or will alleviate the suffering of the people.

member of the commission. mr president, the european commission shares the concern at the human rights situation in bangladesh articulated in the draft parliamentary resolutions. the european union, by the way, has a commendable history of constructive engagement on human rights and democracy with bangladesh, and the decision to send an eu election observation mission to scrutinise the abortive 2007 elections and to suspend the mission in the face of the awami league boycott and compelling evidence of efforts to rig the polls, is an example of that engagement. in the wake of the formation of the military-backed caretaker government and the declaration of a state of emergency in january 2007, the eu has sought to balance strong support for a return to democracy in 2008 with the rigorous monitoring of the human rights situation. this is reflected in the european commission’s intention to extend substantial support, alongside eight other international development partners, to the development of a voter list with photos. parliament will recall that profound misgivings over the list prepared for the 2007 elections were a key factor in the postponement of the polls. the ec delegation in dhaka is closely following the voters’ list pilot project and has provided highly positive feedback on the process. the eu has, however, consistently made clear that progress on technical preparations for the elections must be matched by progress on political reforms, and as the eu troika underlined during its visit to dhaka in june, the political parties must be implicated in the reform process as soon as possible. in an encouraging move, the bangladesh election commission has now announced a schedule for consultations with the 15 principal parties in the country. the eu has made strong representations to the government of bangladesh, and to the military, on the need to ensure respect for the human rights and due process, most recently during a local eu troika démarche to the foreign affairs advisors on 8 august. that démarche also provided the opportunity to raise seven individual cases of human rights violations. the government has provided detailed responses to some of those cases. eu heads of mission will continue to pursue human rights concerns with the authorities, with a view to ensuring that those who have committed abuses are appropriately punished and the others released. as to the specific case of united nations special rapporteur, sigma huda, the head of the ec delegation in dhaka has conveyed concerns regarding her medical condition and treatment to the ministry of foreign affairs. i understand that mrs suda is appealing the decision of the trial court, and the ec will follow the case very closely. support for human rights and good governance also constitutes one of the three priorities for the ec financial assistance to bangladesh under the country strategy paper for 2007-2013, alongside human and social development and trade and economic development. eur 55 million have been earmarked for action under that priority for the period 2007 to 2010. in conclusion, the european commission remains optimistic that bangladesh is on track to hold credible parliamentary elections in 2008. we are extending substantial political and financial support to that goal, while – and i would like to underline this – remaining very vigilant on human rights and other concerns.

the rapporteur. mr president, i would first like to share everyone's satisfaction with this railway package. we've come from far away. there were four texts at the start, there are three at the finish. we started in 2004 and we're now in september 2007. that means we didn't take the high-speed train, we took the bus. it's been slow, but eventually, we get to the terminal. i believe that we owe this, first of all, to the great determination and the strong cohesion of the members of parliament and, in particular, of all the groups and the three rapporteurs here, but also of all those who, including the fictitious rapporteurs, have contributed to the building. we also owe it to the european commission, and i would like to thank commissioner barrot and the commission for their help in difficult times, because the conciliation was extremely perilous and unlikely. we also owe it to the german presidency and to the german minister for transport, mr tiefensee, who has put a lot of his own money into it: he has participated in several conciliations and i think that without his arbitration and his will to succeed, we would not have this railway package today. i am thinking in particular of the text which has given rise to the greatest number of problems, the text on passenger rights. i would like to pay tribute to the work of dirk sterckx. it is rather curious that there has been so much resistance to rail passenger rights. it's true that the railway is not quite the road, it's a guide. it is also true that delays can sometimes accumulate. it is true that safety is paramount and that trains can be delayed for noble reasons. however, we will be decades behind the airline industry and we have touched on the enormous conservatism of the european railway world: its enormous resistance to passenger rights which will have been finally lifted because we have accepted derogations which may lead us to implementation in fifteen years, that is to say, around 2023. i would just like to say that if we are proud of this text, we will be much more discreet about the timetables, because i believe that introducing passenger rights over a period of perhaps 15 years is not entirely decent when we want to develop the railway, as is the case today. i would also like to say that i am personally pleased that a european driving licence is being created, since it is on behalf of the its group. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as we know, the situation of rail transport compared with road transport has always been unfavourable. in fact, rail is losing the battle in all european countries when it comes to freight transport. today, fortunately, this situation is improving, with the commission's decision to allocate at least 40% of transport expenditure to rail, and this in the framework of the first railway package. infrastructure will have to benefit in particular, since all the railway lines that have been closed down for reasons of non-profitability have meant that a good part of these freight or passenger transport services have been replaced by road transport. as regards the report by mr sterckx on rail passengers' rights and obligations, the main points in the report are in the right direction, namely the protection of passengers, including compensation for delayed trains, the right to transport people with reduced mobility and the responsibility of the carrier towards passengers and their luggage. but there is one very important point for all families which seems to have been completely overlooked in this report. this is the right to a reduced-price ticket for large families. this reduction card for large families, which can range from 50 to 75% depending on the number of children, already exists in a number of eu member states, including france, but, curiously, it is not included or even envisaged in this regulation. however, in order to increase the development of rail passenger transport, this incentive measure in financial terms, but also in terms of transport time compared to road, would certainly be a major asset in the match between rail and road.
in writing. i am pleased that parliament and the council were able to reach agreement on the third railway package. on the report by our colleague, mr dirk sterckx, i am particularly pleased that we have succeeded in getting the council to accept that the rights and obligations apply to all travellers within the european union, not just international passengers. all rail passengers now enjoy important rights, whether in terms of compensation in the event of delays or cancellations, information provided to them or access for people with reduced mobility. according to the georg jarzembowski report, the opening of international passenger transport by rail to competition from 1 january 2010 should increase the efficiency of this mode of transport and have a positive impact on passengers in terms of fares and operator choice. finally, rail transport lines which are in deficit may be financed when they meet public service objectives. this is an important measure to ensure that rail transport is available to all. the provisions introduced by this third railway package are a real step forward for the citizens and i welcome this.
in writing. i am pleased that my position to open up passenger services to competition without haste has been followed. the third railway package allows the liberalisation of international passenger services from 2010 onwards, by providing a viable infrastructure financing mechanism. after the commission has produced in 2012 economic, social and safety studies, we can then calmly discuss the advisability of extending these mechanisms to national travel services. we wanted this modernisation of railway management to be accompanied by important safety considerations. the new rules will require cabin crew to meet common qualification and training requirements leading to the issue of a 'rail driver's licence'. finally, parliament has achieved a considerable strengthening of the fundamental rights of passengers, both on international and national routes: liability in the event of an accident, rights of disabled persons and persons with reduced mobility. i regret, however, the deadlock in the council, which will allow for derogations for a period of up to 15 years in the implementation of the right to information, compensation for delay and accidents, and the transport of bicycles on trains.

the commission's vice-president mr president, i have just presented these proposals on urban mobility to the house and i am pleased to now give them to the european parliament. the united nations is preparing for the international conference on climate change to be held in bali in december. yesterday, a preparatory meeting of heads of state and government took place in new york, at which the european union unveiled its very ambitious proposal to halve greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. urban transport is one area where efforts need to be made. pollution from private and public urban transport of people and goods accounts for 40% of co2 and 70% of other pollutants emitted by road. the green paper i am presenting to you today is the result of an intensive initial consultation process, which began last january and continued until june: consultation of the institutions, city representatives, stakeholders and citizens. the consultation shows that there is a strong desire among the actors to put urban mobility on the european agenda. local authorities and european cities should not be left to manage this delicate situation on their own. it is not my intention to impose central solutions which are not adapted to local circumstances. the role of the union is rather to identify, in partnership with all parties, the obstacles to urban mobility and the means of removing them. the european union must draw attention to this and, if necessary, play a leading role in this area. how should urban mobility be re-imagined? i have five basic objectives. first, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, a more fluid city. across europe, the increase in traffic in city centres leads to permanent congestion. the impact of urban congestion is estimated to be a loss of 1% of the eu's gross domestic product. experience shows that there is no single solution to decongesting our cities. alternatives to the private car, such as public transport, walking and cycling, must be made more attractive and safer. carpooling, car sharing, the establishment of a more efficient system of goods transport can help to make the city more fluid. second, cleaner cities through improved energy efficiency, through the use of alternative fuels. the european parliament has already expressed its concern about the situation in the baltic states, and the commission has also expressed its concern about the situation in the baltic states. the city must also be a smart city. european cities are currently facing a steady increase in demand for transport of goods and passengers. intelligent transport systems and traffic control devices, together with satellite navigation, offer us immense opportunities to improve mobility, if we take advantage of them. the information provided by satellite navigation, now gps and in the future galileo, can be useful for streamlining deliveries in the city. fourth, the city must be more accessible. accessibility, first, for disabled people, for people with reduced mobility, for families with young children. everyone must have access to our cities. it is important that urban planning is effective and well thought out. and, of course, there's passengers. and finally, fifth, we need a safer city. i would remind you that two thirds of all road accidents occur in urban areas. one third of the deaths, one in three, occur in urban areas. if we training of future drivers. and then, in general, we have to ensure that road safety is better respected in europe. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, this green paper will enable us to open a wide in writing. since 1992, the brussels commission has been telling us that there are mountains of cereals. not to mention oceans of milk and other refrigerators filled. so we had to put the land of europe in a fallow, to prevent production. the southern hemisphere and the usa demanded that the wto have a monopoly on wheat and oilseeds. it should be remembered that, in the context of the uruguay round, with the blair house agreement of 1992, the european commission had agreed to limit our oilseed areas to 5 million hectares. what was meant to happen happened. agriculture is subject to the vagaries of climate. joseph in the bible already explained to pharaoh: drought in australia, the fall in production in ukraine, the ever-increasing demand in china, india, africa cause the price of grain and corn to rise. after financing our farmers so that they do not produce, after having even decoupled production aid from 1993, after having put millions of fertile hectares in the ground, when a third of humanity is hungry, the brussels commission discovers the shortage of cereals, the collapse of stocks. and then we're back on the raft. it will be the same with wine. it's already happening with butter, meat. the scum and malthus are in power.
in writing. the globalisation of trade and the lack of transparency and information on the origin of products marketed in the european union increase the risks of acquiring dangerous, defective or counterfeit goods. the joint resolution on the safety of products, and in particular of toys, which i voted on wednesday, was adopted by almost all the political groups. it is yet another example of the european union's, and in particular the european parliament's, commitment to consumer protection. the resolution stresses the need for greater consumer protection, particularly for children, by emphasising the requirements of safety, reliability of the community trade mark, anti-counterfeiting and traceability. however, the request for better cooperation with the third countries concerned should not obscure the responsibility of the contracting companies, which are responsible for ensuring that the specifications comply with these health and safety requirements.
in writing. parliament's resolution offers little to stop the import of dangerous products, half of which come from china. it focuses on toys, but does not mention clothing with toxic dyes, dangerous medicines, food products with components unsuitable for human consumption, electrical appliances that catch fire, toothpastes with antifreeze, etc. the list is too long. and it is content with small measures, focusing on cooperation or certification, and pointing to the responsibility of the member states rather than that of china, that of european companies rather than that of others. in this case, it's not enough. it is time to take exemplary sanctions against a country which, since joining the wto, has been steadily increasing its dubious trade practices, whether dumping, counterfeiting or forced labour. it is true that the few instruments of trade defence available to the union fall within the competence of mr mandelson, who is rightly criticised for his passivity in this area. so if we end up approving this text, it is because, despite everything, a few petty measures are better than none at all. at least it's a reaction.
in writing. children from vietnam, africa and elsewhere jump on land mines. our children in europe are choking, poisoning themselves, and becoming allergic to barbie dolls and toys. the movie theater had already sounded the alarm with the movie "santa is a piece of garbage". it is up to us members to react. in the name of the precautionary principle and to safeguard the demographic future of our continent already tested by the dangerous games of adults in freedom. it's time to go. yesterday, how many faces, as smooth as a brancusi sculpture, were ravaged by the celluloid dolls that caught fire with the slightest match. toys kill, and the children of darfur don't know how lucky they are to not be able to play with food.
in writing. following the mass withdrawal of chinese toys by the us manufacturer mattel because of their dangerous nature, the european commission is reviewing its legislation on the safety of products, and in particular imported toys. the european regulatory system is certainly sound - rapex, ce marking - but it needs to be strengthened. the european parliament therefore goes further and, in its resolution on the safety of toys, expresses its wish to adopt a common framework for the marketing of products and market surveillance. restoring consumer confidence and protecting the health of our children is a vital condition for me. so, in continuity with the reach regulation for strict control of chemical substances in our consumer goods, i voted today for an unconditional ban on all toxic substances in toys. in supporting amendments nos 8 and 6, i have advocated a total ban on dangerous phthalates in all toys that can be placed in the mouth. the chemical safety of toys is not only a regulatory requirement, it is also hygienic and therefore vital for the safety of our children!
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which aims to establish a common foreign energy policy. the solutions must be international and the european union must be able to play a leading role. energy has become a real weapon in international negotiations. since the gas crisis between russia and ukraine in january 2006, the european union has become aware of its fragility in terms of energy supply. the report also calls for the establishment of a european energy agency, which would be responsible for the coordination of the eu's energy policy. the high representative for energy will be a dual-hatted figure, under the authority of the new high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy (cfsp) and a vice-president of the european commission. i welcome this progress, which will make it possible to intensify the dialogue with the producing countries - the euro-mediterranean partnership is an example - and with consumers. this will enable the eu to defend its energy security interests in negotiations with external partners.
in writing. by considering that 'the situation of labour markets in the european union is characterised by a demand for legal immigration', mrs grüber, like mr sarkozy in france, intends to give an economic justification to the immigration policies pursued in our states. but the vast majority of the workforce, coming from the developing countries, is unsuited to the jobs our economies need. it should also be remembered that the essence of legal immigration is not immigration of workers but of settlement. this policy, which brings about two million additional immigrants each year, is in effect a colonization of europe. by 2050, the non-european population, which already stands at 40 million, will have tripled. with turkey's entry, europe under brussels would then have 220 million asians and africans from the mostly muslim world. this settlement colonisation is a mortal threat to the christian and humanist values of our civilization. to safeguard the legitimate right of the peoples of europe to self-determination and to remain self-determined, we must re-establish our frontiers, reverse migratory flows and embark on a great family and natalist policy. only a new europe, a 'european' europe, the europe of sovereign nations, could guarantee our right to cultural and historical self-defence.
in writing. i welcome the adoption of this report, which offers a balanced and realistic view of the phenomenon of immigration and which has been the subject of a broad consensus, as the rapporteur wished. the report is timely, given the current situation and the fact that member states are trying to adjust their legislation one by one to better cope with migratory flows. in reality, we all know that the scale of migration is greater than the capacity of individual states to deal with it, and that a comprehensive and coherent approach is therefore needed at european level, as the report rightly points out. the text sets out several priorities: the fight against trafficking in human beings, respect for the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and the european convention for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms when taking measures against illegal immigration, strengthening cooperation with third countries, the need to be firm in the fight against illegal employment and, finally, the need for a responsible return policy. for these reasons i supported the adoption of this text in the final vote in plenary.
in writing. official figures show that europe is overwhelmed by illegal immigration. it is totally incapable of controlling its external borders. the annual report on eurodac's activities in 2006, the biometric tool used at european level for asylum applications, shows that the number of people registered as having illegally crossed a european border has increased by 64% compared to 2005. the report by mr moreno sánchez considers a number of ways of halting this exponential growth. they are all equally useless, even counterproductive. for example, how can we be satisfied with the idea that encouraging legal immigration, particularly through the 'european blue card', a genuine european work permit for immigrants, will reduce illegal immigration? it's a waste of time. when you open doors for some people, you open them for everyone. what is the use of a biometric database in the fight against illegal immigration? why should we consider more staff and resources for the european border agency, frontex, if the internal and external borders are still not effectively protected by the member states? once again, the european institutions have identified a problem but have proved incapable of solving it, driven by their immigrationist and globalist ideology.

the rapporteur. mr president, madam commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the idea of a european digital library was born of the desire of six heads of state and government of the union to make europe's cultural heritage accessible to all and to ensure its preservation for future generations. this unifying project for europe will strengthen the expression of a genuine european identity and promote the dissemination of our cultural and linguistic diversity throughout the world. this project, unprecedented in europe, combines both the past and the present, the cultural dimension and the digital dimension. it is a perfect response to the challenges posed to our citizens by the new information and communication technologies. the internet, the third favourite medium of young europeans, is one of the main means of accessing knowledge and know-how. the commission should also be able to provide information on the impact of the digital transformation of cultural resources on the union's cultural heritage. to be effective and reach the greatest number of people, initiatives to disseminate and promote our cultural heritage must be coordinated. this is the objective proposed by the european digital library, to which the commission has responded positively through its flagship initiative 'i2010 digital libraries'. the first part of this initiative, the communication of 30 september 2005, focused on three main areas: digitisation, online accessibility and preservation of digital content. the commission analysed in this context the main technical, legal, organisational and financial challenges involved in a project of this scale. at the same time, an online public consultation was launched and a high-level expert group was set up. on the basis of these elements, the commission adopted on 24 august 2006 a recommendation on digitisation, online accessibility and digital preservation, in which it calls on member states to accelerate the pace of digitisation and coordinate their efforts to achieve genuine synergy. on 13 november 2006, the council unanimously endorsed these recommendations. it is now up to the european parliament to send a strong signal in favour of the implementation of this exceptional project. the business is such that it must be done in stages. therefore, while working from the outset on the conceptual and technical organisation of all categories of cultural material, it is necessary to give priority, as a first step, to the potential offered by the textual heritage, free of rights, held by libraries, through a single, direct and multilingual access point. the latter have the advantage of already being coordinated at european level through the tel, the european library, created in 2005 by national libraries and which has a significant amount of digitized public domain works and, therefore, immediately usable. secondly, to promote the success of this tool, the library will also have to provide access to more contemporary works in addition to public domain materials. any such decision will necessarily have to be taken in consultation with all the actors concerned. the protection of the rights of authors and creators is an essential condition for the maintenance and safeguarding of creativity in europe. the project will only be successful if it is based on a coherent economic model. the report proposes that, in agreement with the rights holders, the european digital library should enable the internet user to search for and locate digitised documents, whatever their status, and then to consult public domain works in their entirety, but only short extracts of copyrighted works. furthermore, in order to virtually browse the work or to access the entire protected material, users would be directed to private operators specialising in secure digital distribution, where several options would be offered to them, in return for a fair remuneration of the rightholders. in addition, to enable the library to provide access to reliable and high-quality content for all audiences, it will need to be organised. the report calls for the establishment of a steering committee in which cultural institutions would play a major role. this committee would define priorities and guidelines for the european digital library, while coordinating, managing and monitoring its activities. finally, to give access to all the cultures of europe, other cultural institutions or sectors such as archives, museums, cinema, audiovisual and universities will need to be involved at every stage of the project. this will be the face of europe united in its diversity. in conclusion, i would like to thank all my colleagues on the committee on culture, in particular mr weber and mr graça moura, for their support and contribution to this report. i also thank the commission for its excellent cooperation throughout the preparation of this dossier.
on behalf of the pse group. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, it is a good thing that a subject as often ignored as that of disabled people can be discussed in this parliament, and the fact that this subject is being discussed by almost all the political groups that make up the parliament shows that we believe that no european citizen, whatever the problems that may affect him, should be discriminated against. this is the case for the "dys", which, thanks to increasingly detailed studies, are found to be very numerous, although still too little visible. as the only french member of parliament speaking tonight, i can boast that my country is not the least active in taking account of the problems of the disabled. the activism of parents' associations and professionals has made it possible to organize the first national day, scheduled for 10 october in paris, and has brought the press increasingly attentive to the situation of people, especially children, affected by these disorders. however, the purpose of my question tonight is not to congratulate myself on the positive progress in one or another state, so much work remains to be done, but to ask ourselves collectively how we could share good practice at european level, since some member states do not even recognize the existence of these conditions. it seems to me that the call for the creation of a european multidisciplinary network for specific learning disabilities contained in the written declaration is in line with this. the same applies to the judicious use of community programmes such as the seventh framework programme. in this respect, the initiative you mentioned, commissioner, neurodys, which aims to highlight the cognitive, cerebral and genetic origins of dyslexia and brings together 15 scientific research groups from nine member states - and i would also point out, by the way, that it is important that they cover almost all european languages - is an example here, since it seems to me that in the long run europe should be the world leader in terms of knowledge of these diseases and the collection of biological data on them. but it should also set an example in recognizing the best methods of rehabilitation and therapy that enable children to regain hope and to face life with optimism. does the commission envisage other such programmes in the future? you mentioned, commissioner, a call for tenders which had not been answered. we want, perhaps, to fill this lack of information or motivation with the awareness-raising campaign which is being launched at the moment by the associations and by the members who signed the written declaration. we hope that your willingness to mobilise european funds to meet this expectation will make it possible to tackle, through appropriate research, other 'dys' disorders such as dyspraxia or dysphasia, for example.
member of the commission. mr president, madam rapporteur, ladies and gentlemen, the commission welcomes this report on the application of directive 2000/43/ec of 29 june 2000 on the implementation of the principle of equal treatment between persons irrespective of racial or ethnic origin. the commission takes note of the concerns expressed by parliament on various aspects and would like to draw your attention to the following points. as regards the monitoring of the implementation of the directive by the member states, the commission opened infringement proceedings against 14 member states at the end of june last year for failing to transpose the directive correctly into national law. i should like to point out that a number of member states have already changed their legislation to meet the commission's concerns, or have indicated that they are prepared to do so. as regards detailed information on the transposition of the directive in the member states, as we indicated in our 2005 communication on a framework strategy for non-discrimination and equal opportunities for all, we publish the full report of the legal expert group each year, and the individual national reports are available online. mrs buitenweg rightly points out that equality bodies play a key role in the fight against discrimination. this is why we are financing the equinet network, which brings together the bodies of the member states for the purpose of exchanging experience and good practice. as the report indicates, data collection is a sensitive subject. however, without it it is impossible to assess the extent of discrimination and to know whether the measures taken are effective. since much of the information collected may be personal data revealing the racial or ethnic origin of the person, or even his religious beliefs or sexual life, it should be treated in accordance with the applicable provisions of directive 95/46/ec on data protection. in general, this directive prohibits the processing of sensitive personal data. however, it provides for certain exceptions to this rule, in particular where the data subject has given his or her explicit consent or where the processing is necessary for the purposes of complying with specific labour rights and obligations. in addition, subject to appropriate safeguards, member states may provide for derogations on grounds of important public interest. it is therefore up to the member states to decide whether or not to collect data on ethnic origin in order to produce statistics to combat discrimination, provided that the safeguards required by the data protection directive are in place. the eurobarometer survey on discrimination in the european union showed that, overall, many european citizens were willing to provide personal information anonymously in a census to combat discrimination. three out of four eu citizens would be willing to share personal information relating to their ethnic origin and religion or beliefs. this type of information is particularly important in the context of positive action to address deep-rooted discrimination and disadvantages. in february, the european commission published a european equality data guide to help member states improve data collection. the same eurobarometer survey of january 2007 revealed that citizens did not feel that they knew enough about their rights as victims of discrimination. although the level of awareness varies considerably between, for example, finland, where 65% of the respondents say they know their rights, and austria, where only 17% of the respondents think so, the average rate, which is only 32%, clearly shows, as you have very well pointed out, that awareness activities are still more necessary than ever. i am confident that our current activities, reinforced by the european year of equal opportunities for all in 2007 with some 430 actions at member state level, and the diversity and anti-discrimination campaign will help to fill this knowledge gap. i would like to point out in particular that we are financing training programmes for ngos, trade unions, lawyers and businesses. the commission is determined to use all available instruments to improve the situation of the roma in the european union. this includes ensuring the application of directive 2000/43/ec, making use of the community structural funds, in particular the european social fund, and raising awareness of the rights and obligations of both roma and the general public. a high-level expert advisory group on the social and occupational integration of ethnic minorities, including roma, will present its report and a set of recommendations in early december. the aim of this group is to identify barriers to integration and to highlight good practice in the public sector and in business. in this context, we welcome the european parliament's interest in the issue of multiple discrimination and i am naturally looking forward to hearing the results of a study being carried out for the commission at the end of this year. it is clear that non-discrimination alone is not sufficient to offer equal opportunities to certain groups, which are more disadvantaged than others socially. the commission has therefore commissioned an in-depth analysis of good practice in the member states, especially in the context of employment policy. the commission also considers it very important that the member states apply the legal framework correctly, but it is clear that legislation alone is not enough. we want to complement it with research, awareness-raising, training and the exchange of good practice, so as to prevent discrimination and, where this is not possible, to offer adequate redress to victims.
the european parliament has a duty to protect the environment. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank mrs buitenweg for the quality of her work. the report is fair and balanced. the most important problems concerning the application of the directive are mentioned exhaustively. it is true that very few of our fellow citizens are clearly aware of their rights in the event of discrimination. as such, it seems absolutely necessary to ensure better dissemination of information to our fellow citizens, especially this year, the european year of equal opportunities. i particularly support the idea of allocating sufficient resources to equality bodies. they play a decisive role in this area and, as the report rightly points out, it is imperative that they remain independent. but the most worrying observation is certainly the non-transposition, or incomplete transposition, of the directive in some member states. we must make every effort to ensure that all member states have the necessary legislation so that everyone, regardless of where he resides, can enjoy the necessary protection. the report makes it clear that the most sensitive aspect of data collection is that it must be done with respect for privacy and for the sole purpose of detecting discrimination against minorities. it is by no means a dangerous diversion towards ethnic profiling, but it is a matter of finally having data that will make it possible to measure the importance of this phenomenon and to provide appropriate solutions. when it comes to a fundamental principle such as equal treatment, europe cannot be satisfied with words, europe cannot be satisfied with a minimum of legislation, europe cannot be satisfied with observing. we have to be careful. but we too must act, we must go forward, and make europe an example in this matter: the more it is, the more irreproachable it will be.
on behalf of the pse group. mr president, commissioner, i would like to thank mrs buitenweg for her excellent work. we fully support his report. recent data unfortunately show that discrimination remains a major current problem in many european countries. the first report of the european agency for fundamental rights, from august 2007, shows that racist crimes are increasing in at least eight eu countries. this is all the more worrying as the european union has very advanced anti-discrimination legislation. however, i agree that it is poorly transposed and incompletely implemented by the member states. european citizens are ill-informed and know, or do not know, that they have the possibility of using this legislation to enforce their rights when they are victims of discrimination. as rapporteur for the european year on equal opportunities for all and the framework decision on racism and xenophobia, i believe that an additional effort must be made by the member states to ensure the proper application of european legislation. it is also necessary to make our texts widely known so that european citizens can take them up. the real progress of this directive on equal treatment is, moreover, the reversal of the burden of proof. we must therefore insist that concrete instruments be put in place to guarantee this progress in all european states. finally, i believe that it is necessary to strengthen the european legal framework for combating discrimination by adopting a horizontal directive covering all the forms of discrimination listed in article 13 of the treaty and, moreover, i would like to ask the commission what progress has been made in this feasibility study for such a directive.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal we are considering today is a response to an invitation from the european council last june. article 9a of the draft treaty provides that the composition of parliament will now be governed by secondary law. it will be a council decision, taken unanimously, on the initiative of parliament and with its assent. the council invites us to anticipate this procedure. he obviously prefers to see us process this hot potato. this is a real political challenge for our parliament. are we capable of designing a reform that applies to ourselves? the last time we were invited to do so was in 2000 and parliament had not succeeded. that is why the vote in the afco committee is already a remarkable political result. we have a large majority: two thirds on the final vote and three quarters on the main point, the numerical distribution of seats among the member states. what's the problem? first of all, the current parliament of 785 members is no longer in conformity with the new legal situation resulting from the amended treaty of nice. this system would apply, on the basis of 736 members, in the absence of a new decision. so far, in the council as in parliament, member states have been divided into categories of countries: super-large, large, medium, small, etc. each category has the same voting rights in the council, the same number of seats in parliament. it's over now! the future treaty introduces two types of innovation in relation to this system. on the one hand, there are figures: a maximum of 750 members, a ceiling of 96 and a floor of 6 seats per member state. it also introduces a principle: between the floor and the ceiling, the member states must be represented in a degressive proportionality, and it is up to us, the parliament, to define this principle today, that is to say, to choose the dose of proportionality and the dose of degressivity, or the degree of overrepresentation of the less populated countries and the degree of underrepresentation of the more populated countries. your committee proposes that this principle be translated as follows: first, the minimum and maximum figures laid down in the treaty must be fully used. in particular, the use of the 750-seat ceiling will allow us to have a small reserve of seats, so to speak, so that we can apply the degressive proportionality without reducing the number of seats for any country. this is a fundamental political choice, absolutely necessary to achieve unanimity in the european council. secondly, the more populous a country is, the more seats it is entitled to, of course. thirdly, the more populated a country is, the more people each mep represents. so at the moment, mr president, a spanish member represents more than 875,000 people, while a german member represents only 832,000. so far, germany has twice the population of spain. this anomaly will be corrected by allocating four additional seats to spain. in total, ten countries are concerned by the proposed increases. we are fully aware that this is only a temporary solution. it would be desirable to arrive at a quasi-mathematical formula, automatically applicable to future enlargements. but the tight deadlines imposed on us did not allow it. the resolution does, however, make recommendations on this point. similarly, we had to use the only population figures available, the eurostat figures, because we could not have the citizens' figures. adrian severin will elaborate on this point. finally, we warn our colleagues against amendments which contradict the fundamental principles of the report and which, depending on the case, would have the effect of giving the large countries an abnormal advantage over the small ones or the small ones over the large ones, in which case all our work would have been for nothing, because in the absence of unanimity in the council, we would be left with the 736 seats of the treaty of nice. so, ladies and gentlemen, let us not have national auctions. we have spent the afternoon proclaiming ourselves the only democratic institution which defends the european interest against the other institutions, above national egos. now is the time to prove that our words are true. in conjunction with a reduction in co2 emissions if we want to bring about a situation which makes maritime transport even appear to be much more consumer friendly. to do this, it is important to many factors behind the phenomenon of missing trader fraud. however, we do not see any proof that weaknesses of the transit system led to carousel fraud. i would like to clarify that, even though all member states indicate the brands they have seized and there is therefore no complete data available. moreover, the notifications of seizures by the member states do not always differentiate to prepare an olaf report on this topic, as suggested by parliament, but i consider that it would more beneficial to wait until 2010 for a comprehensive overview. this is due to the fact that many member of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in 2005, the commission, with the support of the council and parliament, started a process of reforming the statistical governance of the european union, with the aim of strengthening the independence, integrity and accountability of the national statistical institutes of all the member states of the union and, of course, of eurostat the european statistical agency. the first element of this process was the adoption, in may 2005, of a code of good practice for european statistics. the implementation of this code has resulted in closer cooperation between eurostat and the national statistical institutes and improved reliability of the statistical data collected for many purposes, but i would like to refer in particular to one objective which has been discussed here over the years, namely the excessive government deficit procedure. in proposing the code of practice, the commission also recommended that the self-regulatory approach be balanced with the establishment of a notification system to monitor compliance with the code. in this context, the idea of creating an external advisory body to contribute an independent and authoritative opinion to the effective application of the code of good practice throughout the european statistical system was born. the commission also pointed to the need to reform the functioning and composition of the european statistical information advisory committee in the economic and social fields, in order to make it more efficient and to enable it to play a more strategic role. the ecofin council and, in general, the national statistical authorities, welcomed both recommendations and the commission put them into practice in a double proposal in october last year, proposals which we are discussing today with the prospect - i hope that it will be confirmed if you think so - of being adopted at first reading. i would like to congratulate the two rapporteurs, mrs bowles and mrs van den burg, on their efforts and on the quality of their reports. this process of strengthening european statistical governance is completed by a new commission proposal, adopted on 16 october - just a few days ago - for the revision of the regulation governing the production of european statistics. this proposal is also subject to the co-decision procedure of parliament and the council and we shall therefore have occasion to discuss it again here in the coming months. with this set of initiatives, the union will have a modern, reliable and efficient european statistical system capable of improving citizens' confidence in official statistical data. i am referring again to the debates we have had in this house on numerous occasions in recent years about the importance of having reliable budgetary data, or reliable data on the rest of national public accounts, gdp, etc., or the need for a price index which is absolutely reliable by the citizens. in the light of the reports we are discussing tonight, let me simply say that, from our point of view, it would have been preferable to have respected the institutional balance more closely, as we believe our initial proposal did, with regard to the appointment of the members of the advisory committee on european statistical governance and the preparation and transmission of the reports of that committee. in any case, the commission recognizes that the amendments to the original proposals have undoubted value, have the support of the council and parliament, and do not alter the essential content of our original proposals. i would like to thank the rapporteur, the committee on economic and monetary affairs, for the excellent work they have done and for the constant support they have given to the commission in its efforts to update our statistical system and make it more reliable and more robust.
the european parliament has a duty to protect the environment. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the improvement of the european statistical system is part of the broader context of the union's economic governance and in particular of the adaptation of the stability and growth pact. i share the concern expressed by both the commission and the member states to improve the quality of statistical data. i believe that the classification of the excessive deficit depends in particular on the reliability of the data. if this is not the case, the stability and growth pact as a whole is weakened. the flexibility introduced in the implementation of the pact by the reform adopted by the european council in march 2005 requires, in return, that the figures be unquestionable and verifiable. this reliability is also important in the current context of the enlargement of the euro area. it is worth learning from the past! the european union has already been forced to revise the statistics on the budget deficit and debt of a member state; the number of member states applying to join the euro area is increasing, and the number of statistical data to be processed and the number of contacts will increase. the proposed improvement of the european statistical system aims to address legitimate concerns raised about the validity and control of data provided by member states. it is necessary to avoid that suspicion undermines the overall statistical system and the ability of eurostat to check the validity of the budgetary data reported by the member states. that is why i support the reform which leads, on the one hand, to the creation of a european advisory committee on community statistical information policy and, on the other hand, to the creation of a european advisory council on statistical governance, which will be able to play an active role in monitoring the implementation of the code of good practice by the european statistical system as a whole. i naturally support the proposals of our two excellent rapporteurs.

in writing. as rapporteur for the opinion on water quality, i was able to note that pesticides were involved in the degradation of the environment, especially surface and coastal waters, because they are persistent over time, can be transported over long distances, and that it was also a diffuse pollution, difficult to identify, resulting from runoff, direct losses in the soil and in the air, the washing of plants by rain... more broadly, the current use of pesticides in our agriculture can have harmful consequences for our health. the commission's legislative proposals on the use of pesticides, on the authorization and marketing procedures were therefore eagerly awaited. however, i think the targets are not enough and that is why i unsuccessfully supported in parliament's plenary the position adopted by the environment committee calling for a community target of reducing the frequency of pesticide use by 25% over 5 years and 50% over 10 years and 10 m buffer zones between fields and watercourses. i regret this, especially since this is a first reading and the text is still in danger of being weakened.
in writing. historically used to protect plants against various pests, pesticides have dramatically transformed agriculture. however, it is now clear that the widespread use of these pesticides in agricultural and non-agricultural environments has a negative impact on the environment (pollution of water, air, soil, etc.) and also on health (development of certain cancers, reproductive disorders). in response, the eu has decided to amend its legislation to encourage the reduction of pesticide use. in particular, in the context of the breyer report on the placing on the market and sustainable use of pesticides, i voted in favour of the establishment of strict criteria for all toxic substances (neurotoxic, bioaccumulative, carcinogenic, etc.). similarly, in continuity with the french national pesticides plan and reach, i have also advocated a 50% reduction by 2013 of pesticides of very high concern and the replacement of the most dangerous substances by safer substitutes (including non-chemical ones). finally, in keeping with the spirit of the french environmental grenelle, i voted in favour of a tax on pesticides which would encourage our farmers to reduce their consumption of pesticide products.
in writing. i voted in favour of the klass and breyer reports on the use of pesticides because they mark progress towards a better consideration of the environmental and health impact of the use of plant protection products. i particularly welcome the adoption of the socialist proposal to ban the use of pesticides in populated or sensitive areas. i also welcome the adoption of our proposals on the systematic promotion of non-chemical techniques. i regret, however, that the european right has opposed the introduction of quantified targets for reducing the use of these products. however, many examples show that reduction is possible and that a strategy of gradual reduction could have been implemented without endangering industry and employment. once again, the right wing will have preferred profits... but small steps count, and these reports are one step in the right direction, towards sustainable agriculture of tomorrow and a healthier environment for our children.
