mr president, there is a famous law on budgetary discussions called the law of the three 'l's', because budgetary discussions are litanies, as in a religious liturgy, which eventually leads to economic lethargy and this is verified in the 2008 budget. litany first. mr virrankoski is reciting these litanies, as mr elles did in 2006, as our colleague, garriga polledo, did in 2005. first, the litany of cutting appropriations: the council of ministers, in the draft budget, cuts the appropriations in the preliminary draft budget. mr mulder explained that this was a classic in agricultural matters, for example. and the european parliament is proposing to reinstate the appropriations. the litany of a budget which is still below the ceilings of the multiannual financial framework. the multiannual financial framework is already very low in appropriations and the budget is even lower. it's a cascade of malthusianism. the litany of political priorities is also there: year after year we hear about the fight against poverty, education, learning, multifunctional agriculture, the seventh framework programme for research, and that is where the liturgy is. the liturgy is first of all in the budget nomenclature and in the ideology that supports this nomenclature. the nomenclature is the presentation of the budget by activity, the establishment of the budget by activity. in concrete terms, expenditure is broken down by heading, by policy area, which corresponds to general directions. and the budget looks like a giant salami, a sort of grocery inventory, with a problem that the rapporteur has seen very well, namely that the activity-based budget creates confusion with the multiannual financial framework, which is divided into broad categories. five categories on the one hand: competitiveness, conservation of natural resources, freedom, the european union as a global partner, administration and, on the other hand, some 30 political activities, with a difficult match to be made. all this is done in the name of a budgetary ideology, which is the ideology of performance, competitiveness, efficiency, efficiency, result, and it gives a cloudy mess of tools, the result indicators, the performance indicators, the activity sheets, and this budgetary technology that is presented as a new one, the cutting edge of budgetary intelligence, is an old one that goes back to 1947. the american hoover commission was the first to speak of the concepts of performance, cost/benefit, efficiency, objectives and results. and what will give the united states in the 1960s, under president johnson, the planning-programming-budgeting system, and what will give under president carter the bbz, the zero base budget, that is to say this ideology of budgetary performance that we will find after: new zealand, great britain, france in 2001 with its organic law on financial laws, and even mexico in 2006. and from this we can understand why the european budget has no transparency and, in fact, no efficiency. there are not 100 people in the european parliament who are capable of controlling the european budget by activity, with the consequence that this entails: an economic lethargy of the european union, because if there is no galileo, if there is no link between lyon and turin, if there is no link between genoa and barcelona, if the capitals are not connected by high-speed trains, if the research budget is not what it should be, if the european budget of 27 is equal to the amount of the spanish budget, if the european budget is one twentieth of the budget of the united states, it is precisely because of this malthusian ideology. it is perhaps time to understand that, alongside an ordinary budget, an extraordinary budget is needed to make loans financed by member of the commission. mr president, i would like to make a statement on behalf of the commission. in its preliminary draft amending budget 6/2007, the commission proposed the creation of a new budget item – ‘damage requests resulting from legal procedures against the commission’s decisions in the field of competition’ and the classification of the related expenditure under heading 1a of the multiannual financial framework as it refers to an operational activity in the competition policy area. the commission would charge against this budget item possible budgetary implications stemming from rulings of the court of justice or the court of first instance in the field of competition. the need for this budget item derives from recent judgments of the court of first instance and from the structure of the budget. while fines in the field of competition policy are entered as general budget revenue, the amounts to be paid require the creation of a budget item in the expenditure side of the budget, which does not exist at the moment. the commission takes note that the budgetary authority does not intend to support the creation of this budget item for the year 2007. despite this decision, if necessary the commission may have to proceed to payments in order to meet legal obligations that might result from the court’s decisions in 2007 within the limits of the current budget and in application of the relevant rules. it does not prejudge the final decision on the creation of the dedicated budget line and on the classification of the related expenditure within the multiannual financial framework.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report. 19% of the co2 emissions produced in the european union today come from cars and light commercial vehicles. it is essential that the european union commits itself to an ambitious and realistic target of reducing the average emissions of all cars placed on the eu market. the impact of road transport on air quality must be able to be reduced as the vehicle fleet is renewed. i welcome the adoption of the deadlines by the european parliament. if verifiable and measurable actions by industry are to be taken as early as 2011, the date of 2015 to reach a limit threshold of 125g/km for cars placed on the market seems to me the most relevant. it corresponds to the entry into force of euro vi standards. effective legislation must first be realistic, and the industry has long placed environmental issues at the heart of its policies. when we talk about climate change, the priority must be to reduce co2 emissions in absolute mass.
in writing. the european parliament has approved the community strategy to reduce co2 emissions from cars, and i welcome this. this will reduce carbon dioxide emissions and thus contribute to the eu's wider environmental and energy independence objectives. however, the signal sent by this vote to the european commission and the international community could have been more ambitious. since 1995, the 120g/km co2 threshold has been put forward as an achievable target by the automotive industry. the commission has therefore been delaying its implementation for 12 years, even though technological progress is now making it possible to reduce co2 emissions even more than 12 years ago. the european parliament is not going far enough by simply accepting a maximum threshold of 125 g co2/km. i therefore voted against amendments nos 42 and 52, the objectives of which, under the guise of being realistic and prudent, are in fact quite modest. at a time when consumers are increasingly sensitive to the cleanliness of vehicles, reducing co2 emissions from vehicles will benefit the automotive industry, the consumer and, of course, the planet.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report which proposes to support the member states in their very strict measures on smoking, but also to promote the promotion of public health. not only is tobacco smoke the number one air pollutant, but the chemicals in cigarettes pose great risks to smokers and non-smokers alike. this is particularly true in enclosed spaces (workplaces, bars, restaurants, etc.). i therefore think it is essential to ban smoking in such places clearly and unilaterally. strict legislation aimed at protecting the health of our citizens to the greatest extent possible cannot be effectively implemented without a genuine effort to raise awareness and inform about the risks of smoking. i also welcome the desire to carry out effective information campaigns for target groups, including young people, pregnant women and parents. finally, i regret the adoption of the amendment calling on the commission to study the health risks of chewing tobacco and its impact on cigarette consumption. i believe that this request has no place in such a report because the health risks of chewing tobacco are widely known (cancer of the tongue, etc.).
in writing. i congratulate the rapporteur on the adoption of the resolution on eu-turkey relations. the resolution by mrs oomen-ruijten is a consensual and balanced document in which she has tried to deal with all the issues relating to this issue. the resolution welcomes the recent free elections in turkey, calls on the government to speed up the reform process and welcomes the government's intention to adopt a new civil constitution. the resolution also calls for the launch of a new political initiative for a lasting settlement of the kurdish question. the resolution of the cyprus problem in the framework of the un is also mentioned. on the other hand, in line with the position taken by france, i welcome the fact that the resolution recalls that turkey's accession remains subject to full compliance with all the copenhagen criteria and the european union's capacity for integration. all these reasons led me to vote in favour of adopting this resolution in the final vote in plenary. i only regret once again very much that the european parliament has not formally called on turkey to officially recognise the armenian genocide of 1915.
in writing. this resolution is losing its force because fundamental amendments on the recognition of the armenian genocide have been rejected by the majority of my colleagues. i am and remain in favour of turkey's membership of the european union. however, this membership requires an assumed history. i am also totally opposed to the contradiction which the european parliament has just made. in paragraph 5 of its resolution of 28 september 2005, the council called on turkey to recognise the armenian genocide and considered such recognition a precondition for membership of the european union. the choice not to mention the armenian genocide in this new resolution is a step backwards which i cannot endorse on this point.
in writing. i abstained on the resolution on eu-turkey relations to express my opposition to the ongoing accession negotiations. two recent events should make clear the risks of this hypothetical accession. first, the political crisis that the country went through before the appointment of its president of the republic: it illustrated the tensions within turkish society but also the institutional fragility of this country. i am also thinking of the tensions on the iraqi border and the risk of destabilising one of the few areas where the war was contained. the decision of the turkish parliament to authorize the army to make military incursions into iraq is not acceptable. turkey is playing a dangerous regional game and the eu should not support the current populist and bellicose drift. all this reinforces my conviction that if we extend the union to the borders of iraq, i do not see what remains of it as a european union! i think that turkey is still not ready to join the eu. it is up to us to propose alternative formulas: in this context, the union for the mediterranean proposed by nicolas sarkozy is certainly an opportunity for the eu and turkey to seize.

for the greens/efa group madam president, despite the stated intentions, it cannot be said that there are new elements to the debates which have been going on for months on the partnership between the european union and africa. of course, peace and the rule of law must be absolute priorities, and the european union is playing an increasing role in these, which is to be welcomed. the support given to the organisation of elections, for example, still needs to be carefully monitored and monitored so that the people concerned can see the practical benefits of the introduction of democracy in their daily lives. the other thing i would say is that the european union's proposals are still very traditional, between promoting good governance and free trade, focusing on economic development and concern for health policies. but, while the news is hot, these europe/africa strategies, in our view, miss two key issues. firstly, food security, in a context of rising prices for raw materials, cereals in particular, and the rise in biofuels, and the need to preserve and develop agriculture, to which the next edf is allocating only a small percentage of its budget, as, alas, most governments in african countries do. even the world bank has recently stressed the urgency of reviewing the views in this area. the question of food is absolutely crucial today, as is the future of farming, which is too often neglected by development aid policies. secondly, as you know, africa is a vast reservoir of natural resources, which unfortunately the people are not getting, despite the fact that prices have risen considerably. all the major economic powers, as well as emerging countries like china, are racing to exploit these increasingly scarce resources. this rush, this voracity has consequences of extreme brutality in social and environmental terms, and continues to fuel wars and corruption. the european union, in this respect, has a very theoretical, even angelic, discourse, while also participating in the exploitation of these resources. how can we rationalise, control and share access to these resources so that the people concerned can really benefit from them without seeing their environment destroyed? this is a major issue which the eu/africa strategy is not addressing sufficiently and which will be imposed on it anyway, given the rapidity of developments in this area.
madam president, africa today has two faces: the face of extreme poverty and human tragedies such as those in darfur and somalia, but also the face, too often ignored, of a continent which is still innovating, which is democratizing, albeit too slowly, and which is gradually returning to the path of growth. the new europe-africa strategy must therefore take account of this dual reality and support this still fragile dynamic with a genuine political partnership based on unity, because it is africa as a whole, through the voice of the african union, which must be our first interlocutor, on equity with an agenda decided jointly and not imposed by the north, on humility, because europe is no longer africa's only exclusive partner. with the millennium development goals as a road map, with respect for the promises made and the financial commitments made by the union and the member states and, finally, with recognition of the role of african parliaments. the martens report is in fact the message we are sending today to the commission and the council, and we will be in lisbon in december to see if that message is really heard.
in writing. while the importance of the european parliament's report on the state of eu-africa relations, in preparation for the eu-africa summit in december, should be underlined, its realism should be particularly welcomed. the report calls for a genuine eu-africa partnership, a democratic, realistic partnership based on effective and coherent aid and trade. i would particularly like to express my support for the negotiation of economic partnership agreements (epas), because, as the report stresses, international trade must be seen as an instrument of development. only moderated, equitable and sustainable economic growth, as a result of commercial activity stimulated by market access, can reduce poverty in a sustainable way. free trade is not an end in itself, it must serve the acp countries; the eaps will therefore have to be implemented gradually and asymmetrically to take account of local specificities. we cannot be satisfied with one-off aid, otherwise we will not solve the problems, but at most we will put them off. africa is not just a theatre for humanitarian aid, it must be an actor in its development, with the european union as a partner.

ombudsman. madam president, first of all i wish to thank ms sbarbati, the rapporteur for my annual report for 2006 at this year’s plenary. i also wish to thank the very large number of members who, in fact, took the time to comment on my report. i am deeply grateful for the interest that this expresses and the guidance that it contains. with respect to ms sbarbati, let me just say that i of course worked very closely and intend to continue to work very closely with the petitions committee, with which i have excellent relations. the petitions committee and the ombudsman will continue to be the major instrument through which this august body will also be able to deal with citizens’ approaches to the european institutions. i take note of your remarks. i can tell you that i have already launched an own-initiative inquiry concerning epso, as you know, but i want to announce it to this body. i also have taken a strong interest and continue to monitor very carefully developments in the european schools. i wish to thank ms wallström for her remarks. i note that she has recorded the increase in the number of cases where the commission apologises for instances in which its services have not abided by best practice. i am very grateful to her for acknowledging that. i will be meeting with ms wallström in the near future, and i will also be meeting with the directors-general of the commission and the coordinators of all the services dealing with the ombudsman, precisely in order to be able to bring about better coordination and better results. this is an indication of how closely i am working with the commission, and i hope to be able to elicit better results to report to you next year, and of course to report to citizens. that includes the infringement, and i will be dealing with that as well. on a more general point, let me just say that i am very grateful to you for your general support on broad issues like the culture of service, which is very central to my concerns; for your references to the need for more resources for the ombudsman; for your support on the issue of the charter of fundamental rights and of the statute; and for your call for greater accountability, which for me of course is extraordinarily important. i can also let you know that i have launched, as of this year, a concerted effort to reach out to business associations as opposed to individuals, with an eye to better informing them of their rights as well. because of the pressure of time, allow me not to switch languages, but first of all to say to ms mcguinness and also to ms panayotopoulos-cassiotou, that i manage to help 70% of the 70% that are outside my mandate. therefore, my work involves not only the percentage that is within my mandate, but on top of that there is a great deal of effort being expended by my staff to be able to help every single citizen who comes to us whose concern is outside the mandate, by referring to the appropriate institution, be it at european or national level. therefore, this covers 3 830 cases, not 885. allow me now to switch languages. κυρία παναγιωτοπούλου, θέλω να σας διαβεβαιώσω ότι ο ευρωπαίος διαμεσολαβητής έχει πλήρη αίσθηση της υποχρέωσής του να λειτουργεί εντός των νόμιμων ορίων και βεβαίως πάντοτε θα λειτουργεί με βασική αρχή την έννοια της λογοδοσίας απέναντι σ’ αυτό το σώμα, και απέναντι σας, και πάντοτε με πολύ μεγάλη αίσθηση της ευθύνης του. lastly, i am doing all i can to promote the creation of a national ombudsman in italy. i have been there four or five times and i will continue to do so, hoping that we will be able to welcome an italian national ombudsman into our midst in the near future.
vice-president of the commission. madam president, i would like to respond to two direct questions. the first concerns the reform of the statute of the ombudsman. i can tell you that, very early on, the ombudsman kept us informed about the work on the new statute, and we have been in constant touch about this. of course, there are some things we could easily approve, but others are more complicated. the commission will formally give its opinion only after parliament makes its proposals. we have also met with ms jäätteenmäki, and we are looking forward to her report with interest. the other direct question was from ms mcguinness about the carrot-and-stick approach and whether we applied it. no, not enough, i would say – or not yet. but what we have been doing over the last period of time is to create more of a visibility of these issues and also create an ownership within the commission for every directorate-general and through all the hierarchical levels in the commission. i think that creating that sense of responsibility and visibility will help us to encourage and also sometimes to make it known when we are not pleased with how individual officials are dealing with cases. i think it is rather rarely the case of an individual official making a mistake; it is more about the culture. this is what we have in the walls, and this is what we have to change now. i think the reforms we have taken will move us in the right direction. let me just finally mention one thing that i hope will be welcomed by the commission as well as the european parliament: we are working with citizens’ summaries on our proposals. again, to come closer to citizens, we also have to express ourselves not in eu jargon but in plain language, and i hope this will help.
in writing. ms sbarbati's report on the activities of the european ombudsman shows her commitment to this institution created by the maastricht treaty in 1992 to defend the citizens of the union in cases of maladministration by the community institutions. the text rightly stresses certain priorities for the ombudsman's future, such as the importance of cooperation with the ombudsmen of the member states or the proposal to improve internal control of the administration of the union's bodies. nevertheless, the report raises two issues that it would be dangerous to exclude from the european debate: firstly, the ombudsman's activities must lead to a reflection on his recognition and accessibility throughout europe. the number of complaints lodged with the ombudsman has tended to fall (3 830 in 2006, a 2% decrease compared with 2005), while complaints often come from states where the national culture already encourages citizens to refer cases to their institutions. the report also raises questions about the extension of the ombudsman's powers (access to documents and hearings without conditions). a change in the ombudsman's statute should in no way overlook the major role of parliament's committee on petitions, which derives its legitimacy directly from popular suffrage.
in writing. i voted in favour of the 2008 draft budget prepared by the european parliament, as it proposes clear improvements to the draft budget put forward by the council. for 2008, a balance was struck between financing external policies, aid to kosovo and palestine, and funding galileo, a project of european unity. the priorities of the european socialists are thus well reflected in the european parliament's proposal at first reading for the 2008 community budget. i would like to stress, however, the modesty of this budget: it currently represents only 0.99% of eu gdp. this is the first time we've fallen below 1% of gdp. without resources, the eu cannot act in the interests of its citizens. it is time for the member states to take responsibility.
in writing. the european parliament has defended its priorities well in this first reading of the 2008 budget and i support the results achieved by the two rapporteurs, particularly in the areas of cohesion and sustainable growth. however, it should be remembered that, because of the insufficient level of the financial perspective for 2007-13, the annual budget will be small - only 0.99% of gni - which is something that we regret, together with my political group, and will not be able to meet the expectations of all the parliamentary committees and to finance sufficiently the major projects of the future of the european union such as galileo. nevertheless, we have succeeded in defending the broad lines of information and communication policy: the emphasis will thus be placed on the local media in view of their role as a vehicle for information for all european citizens. this is particularly important for the forthcoming ratification of the lisbon treaty and the preparation of the 2009 european elections. as the permanent rapporteur for information policy in the cobu, i welcome the possibilities offered in this area by this new budget.
in writing. the mutual recognition of judgments in criminal matters is a sensitive subject. we do not have a uniform criminal law in europe today, and far from it. legal traditions and values as well as criminal laws differ from one country to another. the criminal law is linked to the identity of the member states. examples of national disparities in criminal law are as numerous as they are varied. this is particularly the case with regard to the protection and infringement of freedom of expression, which differ considerably from one state to another. the automatic application of a sentence handed down in one state and carried out in another would therefore be very dangerous, not only for the person subject to the penalty but also for the rule of law as a whole. extreme caution is therefore required in this area, since it is impossible today to ensure that a person is complying with certain common minimum standards of criminal procedural law. i am thinking in particular of respect for the principle of ne bis in idem, respect for genuine defence and not just formal defence, and respect for the rights of victims. there are two fundamental principles that must always be followed and respected. if not, the rule of law will disappear. these are the principles of legality and legal certainty.
the next item is the commission's statement on company rights.
member of the commission. mr president, let me answer both questions. in answer to the first, i think it is clear. in answer to the second, concerning the 14th company law directive, we had suggested that a further means of improving mobility might be a directive stipulating the conditions for the transfer of registered offices in the european union. the results of the economic analysis of the possible added value of a directive were inconclusive; companies already have the legal means to effect cross-border transfer. several companies have already transferred their registered office using the possibilities offered by the european company statute. soon, the cross-border mergers directive, which will enter into force in december, will give all limited liability companies, including smes, the option to transfer their registered office. they could do so by setting up a subsidiary in the member state to which they want to move and then merging the existing company into this subsidiary. in the commission’s view, it is only if this framework is found wanting that future legislative action in the shape of a 14th company law directive can be justified. therefore, mr mccreevy has decided for the moment not to proceed with this 14th company law directive, but i will certainly communicate your concerns again.

madam president, i would also like to begin by congratulating our rapporteurs and to commend mrs gutiérrez for her hard work in achieving a result to protect our soils. unlike other colleagues, i believe that a more binding legislative approach would have provided better protection. i also regret that our colleagues, whose countries have stricter regulations than the proposed one, are still trying to weaken this report by amendments which i very strongly urge you to reject tomorrow. our agricultural, industrial, transportation patterns have upended the quality of our soils. yet these soils are the basis of biodiversity and our food. they filter and store organic and mineral matter, and they also help us access water. they play a prominent role in the fight against climate change. moreover, with the growing demand for food and energy production, it is essential to safeguard and restore the quality of our soils and to prevent desertification. so without legislation at european level, we cannot hope for any results.
madam president, my first move on this proposal for a directive was to reject the text. i think that a framework directive may not have been the appropriate solution. why should we have a text on soil protection when we already have a set of regulations on soil, on waste, on pesticides, on nature protection? as part of the better lawmaking process, i thought that we should not give the impression that we are once again passing the baton to the european commission. i put myself in the position of the mayors of our municipalities who would still have to find a text that needed to be peeled. but there is a reality: human practices have not respected the soil. to produce intensively, we have exhausted the soils. added to this is climate change, desertification. our urban policies have mineralized the soil, degraded it, and our citizens are now surprised to experience catastrophic floods because the soil no longer absorbs rain. who has not seen the open wounds in the landscape of the quarries that provide us with such useful materials? poor, dry, degraded, polluted, bruised, this is the land that the previous generations spoke of with reverence, for to them the land was everything: work, food, life, the only good for many. today we look at this once rich land with suspicion. what will be the effect of this degradation and pollution on our environment and our health? mrs gutiérrez has done a remarkable job of finding an acceptable approach, of bringing together those who did not want this directive with those who did. she listened to our parliament. it has found balanced positions, respecting the necessary subsidiarity in the choice of methods, because there is a huge disparity between the member states. the final text has evolved considerably. it avoids the administrative burden by encouraging us to correct the mistakes of the past, of our agricultural, industrial and urban practices, which have not respected the soil. this report, completely reworked by mrs gutiérrez, is satisfactory. there is such a diversity of soils in the european union that ensuring subsidiarity is essential, while ensuring the protection and sustainable use of soils.

member of the commission. mr president, first of all i would like to thank all the speakers in tonight’s debate for their positive contributions and i would like to turn to the details of some of the amendments. there are many amendments that are acceptable, at least in part or in principle. for example, the commission accepts that it would be useful to require aircraft operators to develop monitoring and reporting plans. operators in the current scheme must also do this to obtain a greenhouse gas permit. this will facilitate credible verification and thus safeguard the environmental integrity of the scheme by preventing fraud. other examples include the exemption of certain activities such as humanitarian or firefighting flights. however, while i fully agree that we need to get started as soon as possible, a 2010 start date would be very challenging. there would be insufficient time to complete the preparatory work and, in particular, to complete the allocation process which requires more lead time than the process used in the current system. regarding the scope, i have already explained why the commission still believes a two-step approach would be helpful to convince third countries that the european union is ready to take the lead, consistent with our special obligations as a region of developed countries. regarding the call for more auctioning, i am well aware that this is in line with the growing consensus about the advantages of auctioning and i expect we will soon discuss this a lot more in the context of the general ets review. however, in the period before 2013, aviation should be treated as much as possible like other sectors. the share of allowances auctioned should therefore be the average percentage of auctioning applicable to other sectors, as laid down in the national allocation plans for 2008-2012. what happens after 2012 should depend on the general review of the ets. finally, i will share with you some concerns we have regarding amendments that relate to limits on the use of non-aviation credits, to the use of a multiplier for non-carbon dioxide effects and to an additional energy efficiency factor. these amendments all have the effect of limiting the possibility of aviation operators to use allowances, other than aviation allowances, to cover their emissions. this is not consistent with the fundamental idea of open emissions trading, which is what ensures cost-effective solutions. moreover, these changes would complicate the scheme significantly. the commission’s proposal already provides aircraft operators with extra incentives to improve fuel efficiency. there is, in our view, no need for additional features that will just make it more complicated. in summary, the commission can support 27 of the 100 proposed amendments fully, in part or in principle. i will give parliament’s secretariat a list detailing the commission’s position on the amendments commission’s position on amendments by parliament: see annex., including amendment 47 for which i would like to say that the commission will maintain the provisions which foresee a change of the registry regulation, but is open to consider ways to ensure that conversion of aviation allowances does not burden member states’ compliance with a kyoto target. commission’s position on amendments by parliament liese report (a6-0402/2007) the commission can support fully, in part, or in principle 27 amendments: numbers 1, 3-5, 7, 8, 10, 14, 17, 26, 29, 30, 36-38, 40, 45, 47, 49, 51-53, 57, 65, 70, 76, 79.the amendments which the commission cannot support are numbers 2, 6, 9, 11-13, 15, 16, 18-25, 27, 28, 31-35, 39, 41-44, 46, 48, 50, 54-56, 58-60, 61-64, 66-69, 71-75, 77, 78, 80-100.

in writing. the need for rapid and effective action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions is now undeniable. in this context, it is crucial to reduce the impact of transport on global warming. the text we are discussing is one of the steps taken in this direction, and i support this initiative. however, this legislation will be successful if we succeed in reconciling the environmental objective with that of the mobility of citizens, while respecting third countries. it is therefore essential to achieve a reduction in co2 emissions at the lowest cost to travellers. the effort required from aviation must be sufficient not to undermine the reductions achieved by other sectors, while being balanced so as not to penalise the growth of the aviation sector. i therefore believe that too rapid and too severe co2 reduction targets, while praiseworthy from a purely environmental point of view, are unrealistic and risk having a counterproductive effect. i hope that our vote tomorrow will take account of these various parameters.

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, commissioner, we are now back to committee procedure. the main thing is - as you have said - to implement this agreement, which we all hailed as a success when we concluded it in july 2006. it has two aspects: the practical aspect, which i shall not go into, but also the translation into each of the directives, and today we are dealing with the 26 priority directives. in any case, i am speaking on behalf of those who have been referred to the committee on economic and monetary affairs. in this connection, i would like to express our determination to ensure that the european parliament's position when it examines these 26 priority directives is as consistent as possible. the aim is to apply the same comitology arrangement in all 26 directives, hence the idea of a parallel approach. but we know that in these negotiations the devil is in the details and we have encountered him in the course of these negotiations, particularly on three points which i would like to mention briefly. the first point concerns something which in the committee on economic and monetary affairs - but not only - has been regarded as a provocation. as regards accounting standards, an area in which the european parliament exercises its powers and competence to the full, the commission has put forward a proposal to consider that, in this area, the urgency procedure should be applied as an ex officio procedure. we did not accept it and, fortunately, i can see that we succeeded in making the commission back down on this point and in forcing it to abandon this systematic request for urgency which would have deprived parliament of any right of effective control in a field where, on the contrary, it has demonstrated its capacity to be a useful, effective and relevant actor. the second point is, of course, the question of what have been called the sunset clauses or the revision clauses. the commission and the council were very keen to see these clauses removed. they considered this to be an essential element of the comitology agreement reached last year. we have, in a spirit of cooperation, obtained that the commission be asked to verify regularly, every three years, the effectiveness and democratic functioning of the conditions for the transfer of implementing powers. i think that is a good way of doing things and i note that in the commitment that the commission has agreed to undertake through what is now called a revision clause, it is asked to look at the extent of its competence and to justify any changes in legislation or the absence of such changes. the third area is obviously the question of scope. what we see is that the council has not always followed the commission's proposals, whether it be transparency or prospectuses, the definition of crossborder missions and equivalence. i believe, however, that in a spirit of cooperation, including on the part of the portuguese presidency, we are reaching a result which should satisfy all the institutions and i welcome that.
vice-president of the commission. mr president, thank you for your constructive comments at this late hour. let me just make two short last comments. first of all, on the register, i think you are absolutely correct in underlining the need to have information about the procedure, to be well-informed about the progress of different files, and one of the measures that we have agreed on is, of course, to update our comitology register as well. this we have agreed between the institutions, and the commission is investing in this and we are sure that it will be in place by march next year. so i think at least this will help, but we will also encourage, of course, our services to work as closely as possible with the parliament. the other comment is simply to say that i hope that we agree that the whole idea behind this particular procedure is to ensure that we have a consistent and coherent application of the new rules. that is also why we have proposed this sort of package or omnibus proposals, and that is, i think, the way forward: to make sure that we follow closely what has been agreed and that we can, between the two institutions, handle it as effectively as possible as well.

chairman of the committee on economic and monetary affairs. mr president, commissioner, there is a certain logic in the sequence of discussions we are having, since in this debate we are being asked to decide whether or not to adopt the so-called 'ifrs 8' standard at european union level. in a previous debate, on 25 april 2007, when this house was called upon to decide on this standard, we had made it clear that we did not consider that the conditions were right for us to do so. and there are two reasons for this. the first is that we have just made it very clear to the european commission and the council that, in our view, the convergence process in which the european union engages with third countries for the recognition of their accounting standards cannot be reduced to copying and pasting their standards with the international standard. and we considered that the process of convergence should be a mutual process. we felt that this was not the way the international organization was going about this ifrs 8 and we wanted to alert the public to this approach. the second reason for doing so is that many people warned us, and i think rightly so, that this accounting standard was being offered to all users, i.e. auditors, investors, supervisors, without any impact assessment having been carried out beforehand. we know that the commission, chaired by mr barroso, is obsessed with ensuring that, as part of this better regulation which serves as its road map, these impact assessments are formulated on a regular basis. it seems to us that what is valid at the level of the european union must also be valid with regard to the self-regulating international standardization bodies. we therefore asked the commission to carry out this impact study itself, in the absence of such a study by the international body. the commission has complied with its formal commitment by presenting the conclusions of this impact study to the economic and monetary affairs committee at the beginning of september, as agreed. however, in the future we must recognize that the scope of this study, the way in which all the parties were heard, probably deserves to be reviewed in the future, to improve the spectrum of those who are heard, so that it is not only those who are called preparers, that is to say those who draw up the accounts. however, with a desire to make progress in this debate and perhaps also to help make these international standards the reference throughout the world, this parliament is today calling for the adoption of ifrs 8 and is thus demonstrating both its sense of seriousness in the procedure for adopting accounting standards and its sense of responsibility. at a time when an important debate is taking place, particularly with the united states, on the conditions under which that country could also adopt accounting standards, we feel it is important to show our determination to do so in a clear-sighted and responsible manner. i hope that this parliament will adopt the ifrs 8 standard tomorrow, insisting that when it is revised - and this programme is already under way within the iasb, the international body responsible for developing accounting standards - the need for accurate financial information about the reality of the activities of groups will be taken into account. many ngos, in particular, are sensitive to the fact that through this information, a readability of the activity of the groups, for example mining in a particular geographical area or country by country when this is significant, can be given to those concerned by these activities. finally, i would like to say to the commission that we regard the outcome of this procedure as a very important call for the european voice to be respected in the field of equivalence and that, when impact studies are carried out, they should allow all parties to express their views.
i would like to point out that the vote will not take place tomorrow but on wednesday.

the rapporteur. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, with the convergence of television, telecommunications and the internet, television has become interactive, the viewer has become a teleactor. it can now search for content, select programs, and respond to broadcasts, but to do this it needs an ever-increasing number of devices. to make it easier to use and to avoid additional costs for the consumer, these devices must be able to communicate and work together. this is called interoperability. the report before you aims to promote this interoperability within the european union. it also aims to ensure respect for information pluralism and diversity of content in the new technological context, which calls for an active, constant and vigilant policy on the part of public authorities at national and european level.

nothing is less certain. the preparatory documents are hopelessly hollow. how can this be surprising when we know that no field organisation - among those who, every day, are faced with the situation of migrants in transit, wandering, in danger on mediterranean waters - none of them has been involved in their preparation, not even unhcr. the preliminary conclusions ignore the right to asylum, the illegal detention of migrants, their rights, whether they are illegal or not, the unacceptable violence they suffer, especially that of migrant women, the rights of minors, the criminalisation of assistance to migrants. the eu's international commitments and the conventions it is supposed to implement or ratify are at a standstill: the geneva convention for some, the convention on the rights of migrant workers and members of their families for all the countries of the european union. where do we really hope to end up with such a euro-mediterranean policy, with such a lack of requirements in the area of the common rights and obligations of the states? what's the risk? the risk is that of a screen of legal migration selected by hand, behind which massive violations of the rights of everyone else are perpetuated. if it were to spare sensitive issues by abandoning an ambitious policy, the conference would be preparing for its futility. it would therefore justify in advance the proliferation of bilateral agreements such as the italy-libya type, signed in secret, which violate the principle of non-refoulement with impunity. it's not too late to act. invite unhcr, invite a representative of ngos, start from the original document of the southern mediterranean countries, much more ambitious, and the conference, perhaps, will have a chance to mark a positive and significant step.

acting president of the council. madam president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, as you know, on 27 june this year the commission presented a proposal based on article 191 of the treaty on the european community, which aims to improve and adjust regulation 2004/2003 on the statute and funding of political parties at european level. this proposal was followed by a report assessing the application of a regulation adopted by the european parliament on 23 march 2006. the commission proposal introduces a new feature: the possibility of funding foundations at european level, given that they have an important role to play in supporting and promoting the activities and objectives of political parties at european level. since political foundations are closely linked to european political parties, it is proposed that they apply for funding through the european political party to which they are linked and under the same legal basis applicable to their funding, i.e. article 191 of the treaty on the european communities. i know that the political parties represented in this parliament are setting up, or have already set up, foundations at european level, and the council welcomes the possibility of community financial support for the activities of these foundations within the framework of very clear rules which, among other things, make it possible to distinguish clearly between the spheres of action of the parties, which must be complementary and not overlapping. the second main part of the commission proposal is aimed at improving the financial provisions governing the financing of political parties at european level in the light of the experience gained in the meantime. the commission proposes, among other measures, two exceptions to the rule of non-profit provision in article 109 of the financial regulation. the first measure is the possibility of transferring up to 25% of total annual revenues from one year to the first quarter of the following year to enable parties to better respond to changing political circumstances and priorities. the second measure is to allow political parties at european level to build up financial reserves by saving party-generated revenues that exceed a new minimum co-financing level of 15%. i would also like to stress that, according to the proposal, it should be made very clear that appropriations from the community budget may also be used to finance campaigns organised by political parties at european level in the context of elections to the european parliament, provided that this does not constitute direct or indirect funding of national political parties or their candidates. in the council the proposal was first examined three times by the general affairs group in september and october of this year and was generally welcomed by the delegations. however, some delegations expressed concerns about the proposed legal basis and the derogations from budgetary discipline. the council's legal service was consulted on this issue and considered that the derogations from the no-profit rule laid down in article 109 (2) of council regulation (ec) no 1605/2002 could only be laid down in a separate regulation based on article 279 tec and intended to introduce these derogations into the financial regulation itself by amending it. this procedure involves splitting the proposal into two legal acts and consulting the european parliament and the court of auditors. on 17 october 2007, coreper ii discussed for the first time a compromise text submitted by the presidency and the proposal of the council's legal service. on 24 october 2007, one week later, coreper agreed on: first, the splitting of the proposal into two legal acts, a regulation based on article 279 tec containing the provisions amending the financial regulation and a regulation containing the remaining provisions of the proposal based on article 191 tec; second, the consultation of the european parliament and the court of auditors on the amendment of article 109 of regulation 1605/2002 in line with article 279 tec, which was carried out immediately. the two compromise texts resulting from the split were examined by the general affairs group on 9 november 2007, so very recently. and that is why i am very pleased to announce that the general affairs group, which met last friday, has found that there is broad agreement between the national delegations on the subject matter of the two regulations resulting from the split. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the commission, parliament and the council agree on the essential points concerning the political foundations at european level and the modification of the provisions governing the functioning of european political parties. the question of the legal basis was, and is, a strictly technical legal matter and it was not, nor is it, the council's intention to prevent an agreement between the three institutions. i can tell you on behalf of the council that we want the two regulations resulting from the split to be adopted by the end of this year so that they can enter into force on 1 january 2008. i therefore propose to you, i propose to this parliament, that you postpone the vote on your opinion scheduled for this week so that through appropriate contacts we can reach an agreement at first reading on the codecision act based on article 191 of the treaty. in that case, parliament's opinion on the amendment of the financial regulation should be adopted as soon as possible. we have asked the court of auditors for the same brevity. we have little time, but we believe that is enough time to adopt the two regulations under the conditions desired by parliament, the commission and, i repeat, the council.

brought the matter to the wto. the european union took note of the fact that the united states preferred litigation to negotiation and asked the wto to declare the us subsidies to boeing illegal. believe, a special responsibility to ensure effective and adequate humanitarian aid. we can and must be a political driving force, i would also say a political benchmark and reference force. this is the context in which we decided to launch, almost a year ago, the initiative to define an explicit consensus on humanitarian aid at the level of the european union. these are concerns which are very well reflected in mr cornillet's report and i can of course only support the important elements which the european parliament wishes to emphasize and defend with a view to the development of a european humanitarian consensus. this consensus, and appropriate follow-up involving all the member states of the union of twenty-seven and the community, will provide for the first time a common political foundation of values, objectives and principles to which both the member states of the european union and the commission subscribe, and will strengthen complementarity and coordination between member states and the commission. what are the main elements of the draft consensus? first, respect for the humanitarian principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality and independence. you obviously know what he's talking about. secondly, the need to strengthen respect for and enforcement of international humanitarian law at the international level. a quick aside: i remember, i won't name any countries, but i remember, not so long ago, i was in a theatre of particularly dramatic humanitarian operations, and i was questioning an official of the country, who was still responsible for what was happening there, and i said to him, "but you don't respect international humanitarian law". he got this answer, which was absolutely terrible: "that's true, but we are in a time of war". it is clear that international humanitarian law is precisely made, it is precisely made for times of war. and so, you can imagine how, deep down, we are moving further and further away, in a way without reacting, or we accept moving further and further away from the most basic standards in this matter. thirdly, the need to improve donor practices and methods, as well as the quality of partnership with humanitarian organisations, in order to improve aid effectiveness. fourthly, the voluntary commitment of the member states to strengthen the complementarity and coordination of our humanitarian action, and this is obviously all the more necessary now that we have just expanded to twenty-seven states. the future consensus will also have to provide a general framework that specifies the articulation of humanitarian aid with other external policies of the european union. all this is aimed at enhancing the coherence and effectiveness of the european union's humanitarian action. all this will contribute greatly to strengthening the international system under the auspices of the united nations, and i would also like to stress this point. the promotion of a european approach is obviously not intended to weaken or challenge the central role of the united nations. on the contrary, it will only strengthen this central role and i am sometimes a little saddened to see some reluctance towards this european consensus, on the grounds that it would be a form of competition with the united nations. it's not that at all. it is, on the contrary, to strengthen the european pillar in the framework of the united nations, of course. the draft text of the consensus declaration clearly refers to the elements of the consensus which will, in a certain way, form the humanitarian doctrine of the european union in the future. i would like to express my deep appreciation for the work of parliament and the portuguese presidency in the negotiations on the text. we are now reaching the final stages of this trilateral procedure, which should enable us to achieve the ambition of signing a joint declaration by the three institutions on 18 december. this declaration of consensus is, of course, the beginning of a process. it's not an end in itself, it's the beginning of a process. we are aware that this approach will require considerable effort to ensure that our words are translated into action. to this end, we will present early next year an action plan for the implementation of the future humanitarian consensus. during the months of discussions in preparation for the consensus, the european parliament made some very specific suggestions which we think are very appropriate to include in the action plan, such as your proposal to draw up an atlas of humanitarian aid along the lines of the development atlas. let me add a few words on two subjects of particular interest to our colleagues in this house. these are issues which touch on almost philosophical conceptions of humanitarianism, which are today at the centre of certain discussions and which are also issues, particularly for the purpose of humanitarian aid. first, the question of the responsibility to protect. following parliament's suggestion, we have recalled in the draft text of the consensus the commitments made in this respect by states within the un and the international community. i would like to stress that humanitarian action and the responsibility to protect are two different approaches, even if there is an important common element, namely to combat human suffering. we need to avoid confusing these approaches, because obviously this risks undermining the perception of neutrality and independence of humanitarian actors, which is essential to our ability to help people in humanitarian crises. the concept of the responsibility to protect is still very ambiguous. this concept is, historically, and still today very largely linked to the idea of the right of intervention and military interventionism for humanitarian purposes, in extreme circumstances, for example to prevent genocide. but this interpretation is precisely the cause of the rejection of the concept of the responsibility to protect by regimes that see it as a political cover for the west in order to justify their imperialism, to justify interventions motivated not by humanitarian interests but by power interests. there is sometimes confusion between this doctrine of the responsibility to protect and the humanitarian action of protection which, among other things, has traditionally been part of the mandate of the icrc. we fully support the latter type of activity through our humanitarian aid. the cornillet report also raises a very relevant question concerning the institutional framework for the debate on humanitarian issues. parliament has appointed a permanent rapporteur on humanitarian aid, which we very much welcome. mr cornillet's report rightly raises the question of these interlocutors in the council. on behalf of the commission, we are very grateful for the considerable efforts made by the portuguese presidency to give the council the time it needed to prepare the consensus within the development working party. the institutional decision to set up a council group on humanitarian affairs is of course a matter for the member states, but i fully agree with mr cornillet that we must find an appropriate body which can systematically address humanitarian policy issues on an equal footing with the other external policies of the union. humanitarian aid remains neutral and independent of political or other objectives, but there is no political vacuum. on the contrary, the issues and actors that threaten the humanitarian space are political in nature. the lisbon treaty clearly recognises that humanitarian aid is a separate chapter in our international action and i believe that this should be reflected in an institutional structure. i would like to say that there is a trend that i sense - which i am not denouncing yet, because as long as nothing suspicious is done, there is no reason to denounce - but i do feel that there is a growing tendency to consider that, for example, the logistical capabilities of the armies could very well, in a certain way, be more closely involved in the humanitarian field. i am not against anything a priori, but i would still like to say that we must be wary of interference from a sector which does not have humanitarian aims. i can understand that in some cases military logistics are used to help humanitarian causes, but i will not hide from you that i would prefer that in such cases such interventions should no longer be carried out under the auspices of the minister of defence or the ministers of defence, but rather, as is the case in some countries, under the political responsibility of the ministers for foreign affairs. it's a debate that's not over, but i sense that there's a growing tendency to see emerging in the humanitarian field sectors or logistics, corpuses, which can be undeniably confusing. in conclusion, mr president, mr cornillet, ladies and gentlemen, i am pleased with the european community's considerable contribution to the provision of humanitarian aid and i pay particular tribute to all the men and women who are working on the ground in very difficult circumstances to provide a humanitarian response to people in need. i am convinced that this consensus should allow for more systematic and coordinated action. it is in a certain sense the doctrinal basis, it is also the principle basis, it really opens up a framework for permanent coordination at european level. i think that on the basis of this future consensus, we can become much more efficient, which is obviously the goal.
the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i shall try not to repeat what the commissioner has just said. we are indeed moving into a completely new landscape. in so far as the much we were committed to them and why, and above all to say that these points were retained in the consensus and that the european parliament was satisfied with all the points it had requested. as regards the first point, and this was in perfect connection with the previous subject on natural disasters, we wanted to redefine the scope of humanitarian action because, of course, there are armed conflicts which, by their nature, are not necessarily predictable and there are disasters which, paradoxically, can begin to be, due in particular to climate change. we know that there will be disasters in a number of countries, although we do not know when they will occur, such as the floods in south-east asia. so we wanted the scope of humanitarian action to start much further upstream, with staff training and prepositioning. then, further downstream, we can see the gray area that may exist between what is still humanitarian but is already becoming reconstruction and will become development aid again. we have therefore been keen to extend this scope. this will have budgetary consequences, which i will discuss later. there is also an element to which the european parliament has been very attached in relation to this area, namely the forgotten crises, which are indeed forgotten by public opinion, but not by those who are experiencing them on the ground. let us just remember that there are almost as many displaced persons in colombia as there are in darfur, and we must pay attention to that. the second point is, of course, the definition of humanitarian aid and its principles, which were mentioned by the commissioner: humanity, neutrality, impartiality, independence. we find in the consensus the definitions of these principles of action which underlie the humanitarian action of our institution. finally, reference was made to the most vulnerable people, with particular reference to women, gender and the special role played by women in humanitarian action. we also wanted to highlight the role of local actors and civil society. i shall come back to this subject of food aid. as regards the use of military means - the commissioner has spoken very well about it - military means and particularly logistical means - and we are of course thinking of helicopters which can be absolutely essential in a first-level intervention in a natural disaster - can of course only be used as a last resort and within the framework of a mandate, so that they are extremely supervised. there is always the risk that they are parties to the conflict or are considered to be parties to an armed conflict, and therefore it is important to think carefully about this. the same applies to civil protection, where we want the use of civil protection logistics to be an exception and to be well regulated, to avoid the humanitarian area being very poorly defined by the intervention of actors who are not directly involved in it. we in the european parliament, of course, support reforms within the un, but with a clarification, commissioner. we therefore want the funds to be allocated to cerf to be allocated in an additional way. there is no reason why our institutions should deprive themselves of the driving force which our directorate-general for echo in particular gives us. if member states or other donors wish to contribute to the united nations first aid fund, this cannot be at the expense of what is already being done, it must be in a totally additional way. another point we were very concerned about was food aid, which was naturally included in the framework of humanitarian aid, but which we wanted to emphasize the harmful effect of sometimes disorganizing local markets. when food aid is placed without thought, the principle of primo non nocere, first of all, do not harm, is violated. the example of other countries which are very famous for this should be taken into account in their humanitarian action, so as not to make the same mistakes. finally, i would like to talk about the responsibility to protect. i think what the commissioner said is very important and we fully endorse what you said about the right of interference or the reflection that we must have and the absolute respect for the humanitarian space that should lead our european union to consider possible sanctions. finally, we have, thank you for pointing this out, the interlocutor. we simply want this consensus report to be not just a petition of principle but a road map with which we will have an annual meeting, as we have agreed, so that parliament can play its full part here too.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, globalisation, or, as the jesuit teilhard de chardin put it, globalisation, is a commonplace fact: we are facing a second globalisation, more complete than that of the 1900s, since it is at the same time financial, economic, linguistic, migratory and ideological, with a dominant model, the market. this globalisation, another commonplace, has negative effects in the south with the over-exploitation, in india and china, of the soil, forests, seas, waters, and the endangerment of human rights. in the north, it is the relocations, the loss of jobs, the financial destabilisation of our social systems and, because of ageing and the costs of the elderly, the risk that europe will become a rwanda of the elderly, with all the contempt for life and, therefore, the violation of human rights that this entails. in the face of these realities, these banalities, what do we do? we do incantation, we do the foolish and we do divination. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the political charm is to invoke the lisbon strategy, the most competitive economy. you'd think khrushchev at the un in the '60s, trying to catch up with the capitalist system. it's like harry potter with globalization. we're also doing a little bit of trivia. the perfect example is the budget fund on globalisation, with some financial suckers. when things are out of control, we leave it to god and we do divination. in the name of father adam smith, son ricardo and the holy spirit of the market, in the great temple of free trade the world over, we are reducing tariffs and finally abolishing them. well, that's magical thinking, you know. the european genius is that it invented, 2,500 years ago, logical thinking, that is, reason. the reason is that free trade is necessary, but social and cultural protection is also necessary. so we must reconcile free trade with human security. to this end, there is a new customs technology, the technology of deductible customs duties, that is to say customs duties which are borne, of course, by the exporter, but which open up to him a customs credit equal to the amount of customs duties borne by him and which can be deducted from his purchases in the country of the importer. these new generation of modular, refundable, negotiable and subsidisable tariffs will solve the common problem of economic, social and environmental asymmetries in international trade between the north and the south.

for the gue/ngl group mr president, mr prime minister, you have just made a fine speech. in many ways it was a humanist discourse, which i readily endorse as the ideal for the europe of the future. but let us face it, if the realities experienced by europeans are to be brought closer to a vision such as the one you have just described, many changes are needed in the orientations and structures of the european union. our europe is a social europe, you say. that's good. but it is not pessimistic to say that the social europe is still largely to be built. the current framework of european social policy is, according to the treaties, an open market economy with free competition, that is to say, a framework which naturally encourages competition between social models and which naturally tends to bring down the gains made in the name of competitiveness. it is a framework which naturally leads to lower labour costs, precarious employment and weaker social rights. the social question is probably the main cause of the problems of trust between citizens and the european institutions. the president of the european central bank, for example, was able to verify this fact himself when he spoke at the recent congress of the european trade union confederation, where he developed his theory, the official theory of the european union on wage moderation in the name of price competitiveness. it was unanimous against him. the german minister for economic affairs himself, as i have already said, has spoken of the risk of a crisis of legitimacy of the european economic and social model. so let's face it, just to make the vision you've developed for the future credible. you also spoke of relations with africa and the need to respond, you said, to their demand for justice. you're right! mr president-in-office, i shall confine my remarks to the issue of immigration, which is of major importance for the future of europe and on which you have just made consensual proposals. it is true that no one can give lessons in this difficult area, but no one can be exempt from the solidarity needed in a unified area. opinion polls show that some countries have a more economic approach and others a more cultural approach. for those states which see the economic interest first, it is of course convenient to try to procure the indispensable workers by adapting the law, hence the massive regularization measures taken from time to time by this or that national government, without worrying about the air demand this causes, while the other member states try to control the migratory flows. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full. france regretted it and disapproved of it at the time. our president of the republic has expressed it frankly. we must not repeat this operation in the future. the european union is rightly helping spain to cope with the dramatic situations on its african borders. the epp advocates encouraging policies based on the individual treatment of regularisation applications and thus rejecting massive regularisations which only increase the appeal effect. it is in the same vein that the french presidency of the european union will propose a european pact on immigration. and in the future, mr president, the treaty of lisbon will finally provide the means to act together and to abandon the politics of the lone wolf. this is in the long-term interest of the european union, of spain and of all the member states.
mr president, when we talk about the future of europe, history is never far away. for our fellow citizens, as long as the berlin wall was in place, it was simple. we knew where the threat was, it had a place, a face. we were the vanguard of freedom, even against franco, and then, at the same time, we didn't have to talk about borders because it was an iron curtain that drew it. this is europe in blocks and that's over! and today, for me, the future of europe is in its geography. just look at our proximity. we are close to the battlefield of the world, from gaza to kabul. the spirit of european reconciliation must be instilled here. we're also close to the poverty zone, the pandemic zone of the world -- you mentioned it, africa. we must share here, because it is also from here that we control migration flows. we are also close to the area where religious fanaticism has been developing for a number of years, although i am not confusing everyone. and at the same time, we must advocate dialogue between cultures and not clash of civilizations. and at the same time, and finally, we're close to oil and gas reserves. we need it. this implies that we can also envisage security of supply and energy independence. these are some of the things we can explain to our fellow citizens, who are a little lost. europe is now at the centre of continental countries. she's done with her empires. you had one, we had one. there's still some left. she's done with the pads. europe must be given a new meaning. this cannot be an addition of directives. it is necessary to give up some broad horizons in order to resume or try again some kind of european dream. that is my vision, at least partial, of the future of europe. in conclusion, mr president, i would ask for your indulgence, because next year is the 200th anniversary of napoleon's presence in spain. as i know you, and as this is the french presidency, i would like you to be a little lenient with us at this time.

mr president, with this apparently technical question of the interoperability of the european rail system and the role of the european railway agency in safety, we are at the heart of a real choice of civilization. either the union establishes a european railway market based on competition of 'all against all' and the dismantling of national railway companies in the hope that a proper level of safety will be maintained - that is the meaning of the commission's proposals - or we organise cooperation between all the railway companies of the member states to set up a railway network throughout the union to transport passengers and freight at high speed in the greatest safety. it is in this sense that the railteam alliance, which brings together the main lng operators on the continent, could be developed. it should be noted that the history of european railways has already distinguished between the two systems. the commission has already proposed the following options for the whole of the railway network in great britain ten years ago. the result is a general deterioration in the quality of service, a deterioration in safety leading to fatal accidents. on the other hand, thalys was set up ten years ago on the basis of cooperation between sncf and sncb, and this despite the commission's ill will. the result is a quality, efficient and safe service that meets the needs of users. in the light of this historical experience, i ask the commission to abandon the choice of railway competition in favour of cooperation.
